form.003cb1cc70cf5a2c.locally-nilpotent-.text: An ideal I in a commutative ring R is locally nilpotent (in the Stacks Project terminology) when each element x of I is nilpotent, with the exponent allowed to depend on x.

form.003cb1cc70cf5a2c.nilpotent-ideal.text: An ideal I of a ring R is nilpotent when there is a single positive integer n for which the product ideal I^n is the zero ideal.

form.03b55b8ca41abb20.jacobson-ring.text: A commutative ring R is a Jacobson ring when every radical ideal I of R equals the intersection of the maximal ideals of R containing I.

form.03b55b8ca41abb20.jacobson-ring-prim.text: Equivalently, a commutative ring R is Jacobson if each prime ideal p is the intersection of all maximal ideals containing p.

form.03c6dc1e9f953f76.krull-topology.display_term: Krull topology on an absolute or relative Galois group
form.03c6dc1e9f953f76.krull-topology.context: Infinite Galois theory: Krull topology on an absolute or relative Galois group
form.03c6dc1e9f953f76.krull-topology.text: For a Galois extension E/F, the Krull topology on Gal(E/F) is the weakest topology making every evaluation map sigma ↦ sigma(a), for a in E, continuous when E is discrete. With this topology the Galois group is profinite.

form.049afb81432d58ef.constructible-subs.display_term: constructible subset of a Noetherian space
form.049afb81432d58ef.constructible-subs.context: Topology: constructible subset of a Noetherian space
form.049afb81432d58ef.constructible-subs.text: If X is a Noetherian topological space, a subset C of X is constructible exactly when C can be expressed as a finite union of sets U∩F, where U is open in X and F is closed in X.

form.05531f966e3a206f.associate-elements.context: Factorization in integral domains: associate elements
form.05531f966e3a206f.associate-elements.text: Two elements a and b of an integral domain R are associates if a=ub for some invertible element u of R.

form.05531f966e3a206f.dedekind-domain.context: Commutative algebra: ideal-factorization characterization of Dedekind domain
form.05531f966e3a206f.dedekind-domain.text: An integral domain R is a Dedekind domain in this factorization characterization if every nonzero ideal factors as a finite product of nonzero prime ideals and this decomposition is unique up to permuting the factors.

form.05531f966e3a206f.irreducible-elemen.context: Factorization in integral domains: irreducible element
form.05531f966e3a206f.irreducible-elemen.text: An element r of an integral domain R is irreducible if it is nonzero and not a unit and every factorization r=ab has at least one unit factor.

form.05531f966e3a206f.prime-element.context: Factorization in integral domains: prime element
form.05531f966e3a206f.prime-element.text: A nonzero nonunit element p of an integral domain R is a prime element when the principal ideal (p) is a prime ideal; equivalently, p divides ab only if p divides a or p divides b.

form.05531f966e3a206f.principal-ideal-do.text: An integral domain R is a principal ideal domain if every ideal of R can be generated by a single element.

form.05531f966e3a206f.unique-factorizati.text: An integral domain R is a unique factorization domain when every nonzero nonunit factors into finitely many irreducibles, and any two such factorizations agree after reordering factors and multiplying them by units.

form.081430bc340a055a.cardinality.text: For a set A, its cardinality may be represented by the smallest ordinal equipotent to A, meaning the least ordinal for which a bijection with A exists.

form.097db25e2f156689.clopen-subset-of-s.display_term: clopen subsets of an affine spectrum
form.097db25e2f156689.clopen-subset-of-s.context: Commutative algebra: clopen subsets of an affine spectrum
form.097db25e2f156689.clopen-subset-of-s.text: For a commutative ring R, a subset U of Spec(R) is simultaneously open and closed exactly when there is an idempotent e of R (so e²=e) such that U=D(e)={p in Spec(R):e is not in p}; this e is unique.

form.09cfb70140dddf4d.categorically-comp.display_term: categorically compact or finitely presentable object
form.09cfb70140dddf4d.categorically-comp.context: Category theory: categorically compact or finitely presentable object
form.09cfb70140dddf4d.categorically-comp.text: In a category C, an object X is categorically compact if for every filtered diagram M_i whose colimit exists, the natural map colim_i Hom_C(X,M_i) → Hom_C(X,colim_i M_i) is bijective.

form.0bf601085c1029d4.two-one-category.text: A strict (2,1)-category is a strict 2-category in which each 2-morphism is invertible with respect to vertical composition, so every hom-category is a groupoid.

form.0c1db7d894ba43e1.g-unramified-at-pr.context: Commutative algebra: G-unramified at a target prime
form.0c1db7d894ba43e1.g-unramified-at-pr.text: For a ring map R→S and prime q of S, the map is G-unramified at q if there exists g outside q such that R→S_g is G-unramified.

form.0c1db7d894ba43e1.g-unramified-ring-.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is G-unramified in the Stacks Project convention if it is of finite presentation and Ω_{S/R}=0.

form.0c1db7d894ba43e1.unramified-at-prim.context: Commutative algebra: unramified at a target prime
form.0c1db7d894ba43e1.unramified-at-prim.text: For a ring map R→S and a prime ideal q in S, the map is unramified at q if some g in S outside q makes the localized map R→S_g unramified.

form.0c1db7d894ba43e1.unramified-ring-ma.text: A homomorphism of commutative rings R→S is unramified in the Stacks Project convention when S is finitely generated as an R-algebra and the module of Kähler differentials Ω_{S/R} is zero.

form.0c2b2ef0c7e5c91b.multiplicative-mon.display_term: field-valued multiplicative character of a monoid
form.0c2b2ef0c7e5c91b.multiplicative-mon.context: Algebra: field-valued multiplicative character of a monoid
form.0c2b2ef0c7e5c91b.multiplicative-mon.text: For a monoid G and a field L, an L-valued multiplicative character of G is a homomorphism from G to the multiplicative monoid of L; in particular it sends the identity of G to 1 and respects multiplication.

form.0c4c23579959165d.algebraic-independ.display_term: algebraic independence over a base field
form.0c4c23579959165d.algebraic-independ.context: Field theory: algebraic independence over a base field
form.0c4c23579959165d.algebraic-independ.text: A family (x_i) of elements of a field extension K/k is algebraically independent over k when the evaluation homomorphism k[X_i:i∈I]→K, sending each indeterminate X_i to x_i, is injective.

form.0c4c23579959165d.algebraically-clos.context: Field theory: relatively algebraically closed subfield
form.0c4c23579959165d.algebraically-clos.text: Given K/k, the base field k is algebraically closed in K when every element of K algebraic over k already belongs to k; equivalently, its relative algebraic closure in K equals k.

form.0c4c23579959165d.purely-transcenden.text: An extension K/k is purely transcendental if it is isomorphic as an extension of k to the field of rational functions in an arbitrary set of algebraically independent indeterminates over k.

form.0c4c23579959165d.relative-algebraic.display_term: relative algebraic closure inside an extension
form.0c4c23579959165d.relative-algebraic.context: Field theory: relative algebraic closure inside an extension
form.0c4c23579959165d.relative-algebraic.text: For a field extension K/k, the algebraic closure of k inside K is the intermediate subfield consisting of all elements of K that are algebraic over k; this is a relative, not necessarily algebraically closed, field.

form.0c4c23579959165d.transcendence-basi.text: A transcendence basis B of K over k is an algebraically independent subset B⊆K for which every element of K is algebraic over the subfield k(B) generated by k and B.

form.0c4c23579959165d.transcendence-degr.text: The transcendence degree trdeg_k(K) of a field extension K/k is the cardinality of any transcendence basis of K over k, independent of the particular basis chosen.

form.0d4f86b655697ed4.relative-flat-locu.display_term: flat locus of an S-module over a base ring
form.0d4f86b655697ed4.relative-flat-locu.context: Commutative algebra: flat locus of an S-module over a base ring
form.0d4f86b655697ed4.relative-flat-locu.text: Given a ring homomorphism R→S and an S-module M, its flat locus relative to R is the subset of Spec(S) consisting of primes q for which the localization M_q is flat as an R-module, equivalently as an R_p-module for p=q∩R.

form.0e1768811a8dab34.representable-cova.context: Category theory: covariant set-valued representable functor
form.0e1768811a8dab34.representable-cova.text: A covariant functor F:C→Sets is representable if there exists an object X of C together with a natural isomorphism F(Y)≅Hom_C(X,Y) for every object Y in C.

form.0f0d38aaaffaa719.stacks-scheme-size.context: Set theory and algebraic geometry: cardinal size of a scheme
form.0f0d38aaaffaa719.stacks-scheme-size.text: The size of a scheme S in the Stacks Project's set-theoretic convention is max(aleph_0,κ_1,κ_2), where κ_1 counts affine open subsets of S and κ_2 is the supremum of cardinalities of their rings of global sections.

form.12e554f8d49d5361.purely-inseparable.context: Stacks Definition 9.14.1: extension in characteristic p>0, every element has a suitable p-power in the base field
form.12e554f8d49d5361.purely-inseparable.text: For a field F of characteristic p greater than zero, an extension K/F is purely inseparable if, for every alpha in K, some p-power alpha^(p^n) lies in F.

form.138b13bf27c037c1.naive-cotangent-co.display_term: naive cotangent complex of a ring homomorphism
form.138b13bf27c037c1.naive-cotangent-co.context: Commutative algebra: naive cotangent complex of a ring homomorphism
form.138b13bf27c037c1.naive-cotangent-co.text: For a ring map R→S, let P=R[X_s:s∈S] map canonically onto S and put I=ker(P→S). The naive cotangent complex NL_{S/R} is the two-term complex I/I²→Ω_{P/R}⊗_P S, with I/I² in homological degree 1 and the induced differential from universal derivation.

form.141c0f3fd90dc7b4.final-object.text: In a category C, an object T is terminal (final) if for every object Y of C there is exactly one morphism from Y to T.

form.141c0f3fd90dc7b4.initial-object.text: In a category C, an object I is initial if every object Y of C is the target of exactly one morphism originating at I.

form.143bfc18b9ce9385.universal-homeomor.display_term: universal homeomorphism induced by a ring map
form.143bfc18b9ce9385.universal-homeomor.context: Commutative algebra: universal homeomorphism induced by a ring map
form.143bfc18b9ce9385.universal-homeomor.text: A homomorphism of commutative rings R→S induces a universal homeomorphism on spectra if for every R-algebra R′ the canonical map Spec(S⊗_R R′)→Spec(R′) is a homeomorphism.

form.14c44fee62bf6075.regular-local-ring.context: Commutative algebra: regular Noetherian local ring
form.14c44fee62bf6075.regular-local-ring.text: A Noetherian local ring (R,m) of Krull dimension d is regular local if m can be generated by d elements; equivalently dim_{R/m}(m/m²)=d.

form.14c44fee62bf6075.regular-system-of-.context: Commutative algebra: regular system of parameters
form.14c44fee62bf6075.regular-system-of-.text: In a regular Noetherian local ring (R,m) of dimension d, a regular system of parameters is a d-element sequence in m that generates the maximal ideal m.

form.15af666c5e2af983.linearly-disjoint-.text: If fields K and L extend k inside a common field, K and L are linearly disjoint over k when the multiplication map from their tensor product over k to their compositum KL is injective.

form.162eb0d0411cd217.flat-module-lazard.context: Commutative algebra: flat module, filtered-colimit characterization
form.162eb0d0411cd217.flat-module-lazard.text: An R-module M is flat if and only if M is a filtered colimit of finite-rank free R-modules; this is Lazard's equivalent characterization of the usual exactness-preservation definition of flatness.

form.16790121c4453020.weakly-associated-.display_term: weakly associated prime ideal of a module
form.16790121c4453020.weakly-associated-.context: Commutative algebra: weakly associated prime ideal of a module
form.16790121c4453020.weakly-associated-.text: For an R-module M, a prime ideal p of R is weakly associated to M if some element m∈M has p among the prime ideals minimal over its annihilator Ann_R(m).

form.16ce0f7c4ee1fdca.quasicoherent-shea.display_term: quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine scheme
form.16ce0f7c4ee1fdca.quasicoherent-shea.context: Algebraic geometry: quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine scheme
form.16ce0f7c4ee1fdca.quasicoherent-shea.text: On X=Spec(R), a quasi-coherent O_X-module is an O_X-module isomorphic to the sheaf ~M associated with some R-module M; for every standard open D(f), the sections of ~M on D(f) identify with the localization M_f.

form.1be2fa074ef447b0.i-adic-completenes.context: Commutative algebra: I-adically complete module or ring
form.1be2fa074ef447b0.i-adic-completenes.text: An R-module M is I-adically complete when its canonical map M→lim_n M/I^n M is an isomorphism; a ring R is I-adically complete when it has this property as its own module.

form.1be2fa074ef447b0.i-adic-module-comp.context: Commutative algebra: I-adic completion of a module
form.1be2fa074ef447b0.i-adic-module-comp.text: For an R-module M and ideal I⊆R, the I-adic completion of M is lim_n M/I^n M; its elements can be viewed as mutually compatible residue classes modulo powers of I.

form.1be2fa074ef447b0.i-adic-ring-comple.context: Commutative algebra: I-adic completion of a ring
form.1be2fa074ef447b0.i-adic-ring-comple.text: For a commutative ring R and ideal I, its I-adic completion R^ is the inverse limit of the quotient rings R/I^n over positive integers n, with transition maps given by reduction modulo smaller powers.

form.1dfdf703a26031d2.local-tor-criterio.display_term: Tor-based local criterion for module flatness
form.1dfdf703a26031d2.local-tor-criterio.context: Commutative algebra: Tor-based local criterion for module flatness
form.1dfdf703a26031d2.local-tor-criterio.text: For a local map of Noetherian local rings R→S with residue field k of R and a finitely generated S-module M, M is flat over R if and only if Tor_1^R(k,M)=0.

form.1fd51873f9f0afbd.field-from-irreduc.display_term: quotient field construction from an irreducible polynomial
form.1fd51873f9f0afbd.field-from-irreduc.context: Field theory: quotient field construction from an irreducible polynomial
form.1fd51873f9f0afbd.field-from-irreduc.text: For a field k and irreducible polynomial f in k[x], the quotient k[x]/(f) is a field extending k, obtained by adjoining the class of x as a root of f.

form.1fd51873f9f0afbd.prime-field-finite.display_term: finite prime field of characteristic p
form.1fd51873f9f0afbd.prime-field-finite.context: Field theory: finite prime field of characteristic p
form.1fd51873f9f0afbd.prime-field-finite.text: For a prime integer p, the finite prime field F_p is the quotient field Z/(p), whose elements are integer residue classes modulo p with operations inherited from integers.

form.21c2ca138324d040.spectrum-ring.text: For a commutative ring R, the prime spectrum Spec(R) is the set consisting of all prime ideals of R, equipped with the Zariski topology whose closed sets comprise the common zero-locus sets V(I).

form.22c049b8eee93897.chain-of-prime-ide.display_term: chain and length of prime ideals
form.22c049b8eee93897.chain-of-prime-ide.context: Commutative algebra: chain and length of prime ideals
form.22c049b8eee93897.chain-of-prime-ide.text: A chain of prime ideals of R is a strictly increasing finite sequence p_0⊊p_1⊊⋯⊊p_n; its length is the number n of strict inclusions.

form.22c049b8eee93897.height-prime-ideal.context: Commutative algebra: height of a prime ideal
form.22c049b8eee93897.height-prime-ideal.text: For a prime ideal p of a commutative ring R, the height of p is the Krull dimension of the local ring R_p, equivalently the supremum of lengths of strict prime chains terminating at p.

form.22c049b8eee93897.krull-dimension-ri.context: Commutative algebra: Krull dimension of a ring
form.22c049b8eee93897.krull-dimension-ri.text: The Krull dimension of a commutative ring R is the supremum of the lengths of all finite strict chains of prime ideals in R, with the value infinite when those lengths are unbounded.

form.22c049b8eee93897.system-of-paramete.display_term: system of parameters of a Noetherian local ring
form.22c049b8eee93897.system-of-paramete.context: Commutative algebra: system of parameters of a Noetherian local ring
form.22c049b8eee93897.system-of-paramete.text: A system of parameters of a Noetherian local ring (R,m) of dimension d is a sequence of d elements of m whose generated ideal is m-primary, also called an ideal of definition.

form.23afebc5bde9e408.functor-of-points.display_term: functor of points of a scheme
form.23afebc5bde9e408.functor-of-points.context: Algebraic geometry: functor of points of a scheme
form.23afebc5bde9e408.functor-of-points.text: For a scheme X, its functor of points is the contravariant functor h_X from schemes to sets that assigns to a scheme T the set Hom_Sch(T,X), with pullback along T'→T defined by precomposition.

form.23afebc5bde9e408.t-valued-point-sch.context: Algebraic geometry: T-valued point of a scheme
form.23afebc5bde9e408.t-valued-point-sch.text: A T-valued point of a scheme X is a scheme morphism T→X; for T=Spec(k) with k a field, such a point is a map from the spectrum of k into X.

form.26b6764e3ef7a953.pushout.text: Given morphisms B to A and B to C in a category, a pushout is an object P equipped with morphisms A to P and C to P agreeing on B, such that every other compatible pair of maps to an object T factors uniquely through P.

form.26fa733af18b53e7.galois-field-exten.text: A field extension E/F is Galois if it is algebraic, separable, and normal over F; for finite extensions this is equivalent to having precisely [E:F] F-automorphisms.

form.26fa733af18b53e7.galois-group.context: Field theory: Galois group of an extension
form.26fa733af18b53e7.galois-group.text: For a Galois extension E/F, the Galois group Gal(E/F) is the group of all field automorphisms of E that fix each element of F, with group law given by composition.

form.27eb121021fd989d.quasicompact-map.text: A continuous map f:X to Y is quasi-compact if the inverse image of each quasi-compact open subset of Y is quasi-compact in X.

form.27eb121021fd989d.quasicompact-space.text: A topological space X is quasi-compact if each open cover of X contains a finite subcollection that still covers X; no Hausdorff condition is required.

form.29b2c34cc33d4b62.degree-zero-locali.context: Graded commutative algebra: degree-zero homogeneous localization
form.29b2c34cc33d4b62.degree-zero-locali.text: For a positively graded ring S and homogeneous element f of positive degree, S_(f) denotes the degree-zero subring of the graded localization S_f, consisting of fractions a/f^n with deg(a)=n·deg(f).

form.29b2c34cc33d4b62.homogeneous-ideal.text: For a graded ring S=⊕_d S_d, an ideal I is homogeneous if it is graded as an S-submodule; equivalently, every homogeneous component of every element of I also belongs to I.

form.29b2c34cc33d4b62.proj-graded-ring.context: Graded commutative algebra: homogeneous spectrum Proj(S)
form.29b2c34cc33d4b62.proj-graded-ring.text: For a nonnegatively graded commutative ring S, Proj(S) is the topological space of homogeneous prime ideals that do not contain the irrelevant ideal S_+=⊕_{n>0}S_n, equipped with the subspace topology inherited from Spec(S).

form.29edcdafba2cae3d.standard-etale-rin.context: Commutative algebra: standard étale ring homomorphism
form.29edcdafba2cae3d.standard-etale-rin.text: A ring map R→S is standard étale when S is isomorphic as an R-algebra to R[x]_g/(f) for a monic polynomial f∈R[x] and polynomial g∈R[x], with f′ invertible in R[x]_g/(f).

form.2a92541d9744fa5d.combinatorially-eq.context: Grothendieck sites: combinatorially equivalent covering families
form.2a92541d9744fa5d.combinatorially-eq.text: Two families (f_i:U_i→U) and (g_j:V_j→U) are combinatorially equivalent when every map in either family occurs in the other, ignoring multiplicities and the indexing sets; equivalently each family admits an indexing map into the other identifying the arrows.

form.2a92541d9744fa5d.covering-family-of.display_term: covering family in a Grothendieck site
form.2a92541d9744fa5d.covering-family-of.context: Category theory: covering family in a Grothendieck site
form.2a92541d9744fa5d.covering-family-of.text: For a site (C,Cov), a covering family of an object U is a collection of arrows {U_i→U} included in Cov(U), where the designated covering families contain isomorphism covers and are stable under compositional refinement and pullback along arrows into U.

form.2a93c6a662a51d67.geometrically-norm.text: A k-algebra A is geometrically normal over a field k if for every extension of fields K/k the base-changed algebra K⊗_k A is a normal ring.

Equivalently, a k-algebra A is geometrically normal if its scalar extension k^perf⊗_k A to the perfect closure of k is a normal ring; this also tests normality over all finite purely inseparable field extensions.

form.2ab2c62d4a9bd0a6.direct-sum-devissa.text: A direct sum dévissage of an R-module M is an ordinal-indexed increasing family of submodules M_α starting at zero, continuous at limit ordinals and with union M, such that each successor inclusion M_α⊆M_{α+1} splits as a direct summand.

form.2ab2c62d4a9bd0a6.kaplansky-devissag.text: A Kaplansky dévissage of an R-module M is a direct sum dévissage whose every successive quotient M_{α+1}/M_α is a countably generated R-module.

form.2c5739452921ea24.geometrically-irre.text: A k-algebra A is geometrically irreducible over the field k when, for every field extension K/k, the ring A⊗_k K has exactly one minimal prime ideal, equivalently its prime spectrum is irreducible.

form.2cde0248ffe81c00.tor-flatness-crite.context: Homological algebra: Tor-vanishing criterion for module flatness
form.2cde0248ffe81c00.tor-flatness-crite.text: An R-module M is flat if and only if Tor_1^R(M,R/I)=0 for every finitely generated ideal I⊆R; equivalently, Tor_i^R(M,N)=0 for all R-modules N and every i>0.

form.2cde0248ffe81c00.tor-functor-module.text: For modules M and N over a commutative ring R and integer i≥0, Tor_i^R(M,N) is the ith homology module of F_•⊗_R N, where F_• is any free resolution of M; its isomorphism type is independent of that resolution.

form.2d96a50b600ecbfc.noetherian-topolog.text: A topological space is Noetherian when every descending sequence of its closed subsets eventually becomes constant.

form.2ec41283717d02b0.left-dual-object.display_term: left dual of a monoidal object
form.2ec41283717d02b0.left-dual-object.context: Category theory: left dual of a monoidal object
form.2ec41283717d02b0.left-dual-object.text: A left dual Y of an object X in a monoidal category comes with maps η:1→X⊗Y and ε:Y⊗X→1 for which the resulting two triangle, or snake, composites on X and Y are the respective identity maps.

form.2ec41283717d02b0.monoidal-category.text: A monoidal category consists of a category C, a bifunctor ⊗:C×C→C, a natural associativity isomorphism satisfying the pentagon, and a unit object 1 with natural unit isomorphisms satisfying the triangle coherence identity.

form.2ec41283717d02b0.strong-monoidal-fu.text: A strong monoidal functor F:C→D between monoidal categories is a functor equipped with coherent natural isomorphisms F(X)⊗F(Y)≅F(X⊗Y) and a compatible identification of F(1_C) with the unit in D.

form.2ec41283717d02b0.symmetric-monoidal.text: A symmetric monoidal category is a monoidal category equipped with a natural exchange isomorphism X⊗Y→Y⊗X that is involutive and compatible with the associator through the required coherence diagrams.

form.2ec41283717d02b0.symmetric-monoidal.context: Category theory: symmetry-preserving strong monoidal functor
form.2ec41283717d02b0.symmetric-monoidal.text: A symmetric monoidal functor is a strong monoidal functor between symmetric monoidal categories whose structural tensor isomorphisms also commute with the symmetry/exchange isomorphisms of the two categories.

form.2ec41283717d02b0.tensor-invertible-.text: An object X in a monoidal category is tensor-invertible if there exists an object Y with X⊗Y≅1 and Y⊗X≅1, where 1 is the unit object.

form.2ed79f667742de34.essentially-consta.context: Category theory: essentially constant filtered diagram/ind-object
form.2ed79f667742de34.essentially-consta.text: A filtered diagram M_i with cocone M_i→X is essentially constant with value X if some stage M_i admits a map X→M_i splitting M_i→X, and for every stage j the maps from M_j into a later common stage eventually agree with those factoring through X and the chosen M_i.

form.2ed79f667742de34.essentially-consta.context: Category theory: essentially constant inverse diagram/pro-object
form.2ed79f667742de34.essentially-consta.text: A cofiltered diagram M_i with cone X→M_i is essentially constant with value X if some stage M_i maps back to X splitting X→M_i, and for each stage j there exists a common earlier stage where the transition maps factor through X and the selected M_i.

form.30083611f9483a64.characteristic-pol.display_term: characteristic polynomial of a square matrix
form.30083611f9483a64.characteristic-pol.context: Linear algebra: characteristic polynomial of a square matrix
form.30083611f9483a64.characteristic-pol.text: The characteristic polynomial of an n×n matrix A over a commutative ring R is the polynomial χ_A(t)=det(t I_n−A) in R[t], where I_n denotes the identity matrix.

form.31325e4cfe9a4f13.smooth-ring-homomo.context: Commutative algebra: smooth homomorphism of rings
form.31325e4cfe9a4f13.smooth-ring-homomo.text: A homomorphism R→S of commutative rings is smooth when S is finitely presented as an R-algebra and the naive cotangent complex of S over R is quasi-isomorphic to a finite projective S-module concentrated in degree zero.

form.321eb2225cb4b4a2.locally-closed-imm.text: A morphism of schemes is a locally closed immersion if it admits a factorization through a closed immersion followed by an open immersion.

form.34c38bc0b482f182.binary-coproduct-c.context: Category theory: binary coproduct of objects
form.34c38bc0b482f182.binary-coproduct-c.text: A coproduct of objects X,Y in a category C is an object P together with maps i:X→P and j:Y→P such that for any Z and arrows f:X→Z and g:Y→Z there is a unique h:P→Z satisfying h∘i=f and h∘j=g.

form.35c4e2887892c696.catenary-topologic.text: A topological space X is catenary if between each pair of nested irreducible closed subsets Y⊆Z, the codimension codim(Y,Z) is finite and all maximal chains of irreducible closed subsets connecting Y to Z have the same length.

form.35c4e2887892c696.codimension-irredu.display_term: codimension of an irreducible closed subset
form.35c4e2887892c696.codimension-irredu.context: Topology: codimension of an irreducible closed subset
form.35c4e2887892c696.codimension-irredu.text: For an irreducible closed subset Y of a topological space X, codim(Y,X) is the supremum of lengths of strict chains Y=Y_0⊊Y_1⊊⋯⊊Y_n of irreducible closed subsets of X; it may be infinite.

form.363d711d668364b7.normal-integral-do.text: An integral domain R is normal when every element of its fraction field that satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in R already belongs to R.

form.363d711d668364b7.normal-ring.text: A commutative ring R is normal if each localization R_p at a prime ideal p is an integrally closed domain in its own fraction field.

form.3653fa0ad844d187.category-fibred-in.context: Category theory: category fibred in sets
form.3653fa0ad844d187.category-fibred-in.text: A category p:E→C is fibred in sets over C when p is a category fibred in groupoids and each fibre E_U over an object U of C is a discrete category.

form.3653fa0ad844d187.discrete-category.text: A category C is discrete if every morphism in C is an identity morphism; consequently it has no arrows between distinct objects and no nonidentity endomorphisms.

form.3653fa0ad844d187.two-category-fibre.context: Higher category theory: 2-category of categories fibred in sets
form.3653fa0ad844d187.two-category-fibre.text: For a base category C, the 2-category of categories fibred in sets over C has such fibrations as objects, functors commuting with their projections to C as 1-morphisms, and natural transformations lying over identity arrows as 2-morphisms.

form.3718becace9c852d.quasifinite-at-pri.display_term: quasi-finite ring map at a prime
form.3718becace9c852d.quasifinite-at-pri.context: Commutative algebra: quasi-finite ring map at a prime
form.3718becace9c852d.quasifinite-at-pri.text: Let R→S be a finite-type ring homomorphism and q∈Spec(S) lying over p∈Spec(R). The map is quasi-finite at q if q is an isolated point of the fibre Spec(S⊗_R κ(p)); equivalently its local fibre has dimension zero.

form.39488f3e396a1c77.algebraic-closure.text: Given a field F, an algebraic closure of F is an extension field K containing F in which every element is algebraic over F and every nonconstant polynomial over K has a root in K.

form.39488f3e396a1c77.algebraically-clos.text: A field K is algebraically closed precisely when it has no proper algebraic field extension; equivalently, each nonconstant one-variable polynomial with coefficients in K admits a root in K.

form.3a0545450d7a5285.internal-hom-modul.display_term: internal Hom module of two R-modules
form.3a0545450d7a5285.internal-hom-modul.context: Module theory: internal Hom module of two R-modules
form.3a0545450d7a5285.internal-hom-modul.text: For modules M,N over a commutative ring R, the internal Hom Hom_R(M,N) is the R-module of R-linear homomorphisms M→N, with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication (r·f)(m)=r·f(m).

form.3aaa8d6f2195bb8e.minimal-polynomial.text: If an element alpha of an extension E/k is algebraic over k, its minimal polynomial over k is the unique monic polynomial generating the kernel of evaluation k[t] to E at alpha; it is irreducible over k.

form.3c73940f47e92e99.open-immersion-loc.display_term: open immersion of locally ringed spaces
form.3c73940f47e92e99.open-immersion-loc.context: Algebraic geometry: open immersion of locally ringed spaces
form.3c73940f47e92e99.open-immersion-loc.text: A morphism f:(X,O_X)→(Y,O_Y) of locally ringed spaces is an open immersion if f is a homeomorphism of X onto an open subset of Y and the induced morphism f^{-1}O_Y→O_X is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings.

form.3c73940f47e92e99.open-subspace-loca.context: Algebraic geometry: open locally ringed subspace
form.3c73940f47e92e99.open-subspace-loca.text: For an open subset U of the underlying space of a locally ringed space (X,O_X), its open subspace is the locally ringed space (U,O_X|_U) obtained by restricting the structure sheaf to U.

form.3d054062d7995be3.snake-lemma-connec.context: Homological algebra: snake lemma connecting homomorphism
form.3d054062d7995be3.snake-lemma-connec.text: For a commutative diagram of abelian groups with exact rows X→Y→Z→0 and 0→U→V→W and vertical maps α,β,γ, the snake connecting map ∂:ker(γ)→coker(α) sends z to the class of an element u∈U whose image in V equals β(y), where y∈Y maps to z; this class is independent of the choices.

form.3d055c0c9618e129.artin-schreier-ext.text: For a field K of prime characteristic p, an Artin-Schreier extension is obtained by adjoining a solution of t^p - t = a, for a in K; a nontrivial such extension has cyclic Galois group of order p.

form.3f6a26f1786a8223.base-change-module.context: Commutative algebra: base change of a module
form.3f6a26f1786a8223.base-change-module.text: Given an R-algebra S, an S-module M and a map R→R′, the base change of M along R→R′ is the module M⊗_R R′ over S⊗_R R′.

form.3f6a26f1786a8223.base-change-ring-m.display_term: base change of a ring homomorphism
form.3f6a26f1786a8223.base-change-ring-m.context: Commutative algebra: base change of a ring homomorphism
form.3f6a26f1786a8223.base-change-ring-m.text: For ring homomorphisms R→S and R→R′, the base change of R→S along R→R′ is the induced homomorphism R′→S⊗_R R′.

form.3f6cdddd076e5ca0.nagata-ring.text: A commutative ring R is Nagata if it is Noetherian and R/p is Japanese (N-2) for each prime ideal p of R.

form.3f6cdddd076e5ca0.universally-japane.text: A ring R is universally Japanese if every finite-type R-algebra S that is an integral domain is Japanese (N-2), meaning the integral closure of S in any finite extension of its fraction field is finite over S.

form.3fcd082413a6b2eb.relative-dimension.display_term: relative dimension of a finite-type ring map at a prime
form.3fcd082413a6b2eb.relative-dimension.context: Commutative algebra: relative dimension of a finite-type ring map at a prime
form.3fcd082413a6b2eb.relative-dimension.text: For a finite-type ring map R→S and prime q of S lying over p in R, the relative dimension at q is the local topological dimension at the corresponding point of the fibre Spec(S⊗_R κ(p)).

form.3fcd082413a6b2eb.relative-dimension.display_term: relative dimension of a ring map
form.3fcd082413a6b2eb.relative-dimension.context: Commutative algebra: relative dimension of a ring map
form.3fcd082413a6b2eb.relative-dimension.text: The relative dimension of a finite-type ring homomorphism R→S is the supremum over all primes q∈Spec(S) of its relative fibre dimensions dim_q(S/R).

form.3fe40ac4fb74bff2.pure-ideal.text: An ideal I in a commutative ring R is pure if the quotient module R/I is flat over R.

form.3fe40ac4fb74bff2.pure-ideal-interse.text: Equivalently, an ideal I⊆R is pure when I∩J=IJ for every ideal J of R; it is enough to test finitely generated ideals J.

form.415a1503ae7ed97d.finitely-presented.context: Commutative algebra: algebra of finite presentation
form.415a1503ae7ed97d.finitely-presented.text: An R-algebra S is finitely presented if it admits a presentation S≅R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m) with finitely many generators x_i and finitely many polynomial relations f_j.
An R-module M is finitely presented if an exact sequence R^m→R^n→M→0 exists with both m and n finite; equivalently M has finitely many generators and relations.

form.41e3aea7f356bae3.determinantal-idea.context: Commutative algebra: ideal of maximal nonzero-size minors
form.41e3aea7f356bae3.determinantal-idea.text: For a homomorphism φ:R^m→R^n of rank r, its maximal-rank determinantal ideal I(φ) is the ideal of R generated by all r×r minors of a matrix representing φ; by convention it equals R when r=0.

form.41e3aea7f356bae3.rank-of-map-finite.context: Commutative algebra: rank of a finite-free-module map
form.41e3aea7f356bae3.rank-of-map-finite.text: For a homomorphism φ:R^m→R^n of finite free modules, its rank is the largest integer r for which the induced exterior-power map ∧^rφ is nonzero (and is zero when φ itself is zero).

form.42730c7ef758df2a.iso-comma-category.context: Category theory: iso-comma construction of a 2-fibre product
form.42730c7ef758df2a.iso-comma-category.text: For functors F:A→C and G:B→C, their iso-comma category A×_C B has triples (a,b,α:F(a)≅G(b)) as objects and compatible pairs of arrows in A and B as morphisms.

form.42730c7ef758df2a.two-fibre-product.context: Higher category theory: 2-fibre product in a (2,1)-category
form.42730c7ef758df2a.two-fibre-product.text: For 1-morphisms X→Z←Y in a (2,1)-category, a 2-fibre product X×_Z Y is a terminal object, in the 2-categorical sense, among objects W equipped with maps W→X and W→Y and an invertible 2-morphism between the two resulting maps W→Z.

form.42730c7ef758df2a.two-final-object.context: Higher category theory: final object of a (2,1)-category
form.42730c7ef758df2a.two-final-object.text: A final object T of a (2,1)-category C is an object such that, for every Y in C, there is a 1-morphism Y→T and any two such 1-morphisms are connected by exactly one 2-morphism.

form.428415804368c582.stone-cech-compact.context: Topology: Stone–Čech compactification by universal property
form.428415804368c582.stone-cech-compact.text: A Stone–Čech compactification of a topological space X (in this source's universal-map sense) is a continuous map η:X→βX into a compact Hausdorff space βX such that every continuous f:X→K with K compact Hausdorff factors uniquely through a continuous map βX→K.

form.4406a87f2ff9b7d8.field-norm.display_term: norm of an element in a finite field extension
form.4406a87f2ff9b7d8.field-norm.context: Field theory: norm of an element in a finite field extension
form.4406a87f2ff9b7d8.field-norm.text: For a finite extension L/K and α∈L, the field norm N_{L/K}(α) is the determinant over K of the multiplication-by-α endomorphism L→L.

form.4406a87f2ff9b7d8.field-trace.display_term: trace of an element in a finite field extension
form.4406a87f2ff9b7d8.field-trace.context: Field theory: trace of an element in a finite field extension
form.4406a87f2ff9b7d8.field-trace.text: For a finite extension L/K and α∈L, the field trace Tr_{L/K}(α) is the trace over K of the K-linear endomorphism of L given by multiplication x↦αx.

form.445e8dc5147c408d.tensor-algebra.text: For an R-module M, its tensor algebra is the graded associative R-algebra obtained by taking the direct sum over n at least zero of the n-fold tensor powers of M, with the degree-zero summand R and multiplication by concatenation of tensors.

form.448c7ba2c12aceac.monomorphism-of-sc.text: A morphism f:X to Y of schemes is a monomorphism when for every scheme T and two morphisms g,h:T to X, equality f composed with g = f composed with h forces g=h.

form.44fae2299dfd2f0a.formally-unramifie.context: Commutative algebra: formally unramified ring homomorphism
form.44fae2299dfd2f0a.formally-unramifie.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is formally unramified if, for every R-algebra A and square-zero ideal I⊆A, any R-algebra map S→A/I admits at most one lift to an R-algebra map S→A.

form.44fae2299dfd2f0a.formally-unramifie.context: Commutative algebra: formally unramified ring homomorphism
form.44fae2299dfd2f0a.formally-unramifie.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is formally unramified exactly when its module of Kähler differentials Ω_{S/R} is zero.

form.471f985f2fbe7b49.splitting-field.text: For a nonconstant polynomial P over a field F, a splitting field is a field extension E/F in which P factors into linear terms and which is generated over F by all its roots.

form.4777518984e96a98.finite-field-exten.text: A field extension E/F has degree equal to the vector-space dimension of E over F; the extension is finite exactly when this dimension is a finite integer.

form.4b6af5c19e4a290c.smooth-ring-map.text: A homomorphism R→S of commutative rings is smooth if S is finitely presented as an R-algebra and the naive cotangent complex NL_{S/R} is quasi-isomorphic to a finite projective S-module in degree zero.

form.4b9834a2990971e9.finite-colimit.text: A colimit of a diagram F:I→C is a finite colimit when the index category I contains only finitely many objects and morphisms.

form.4b9834a2990971e9.finite-limit.text: A limit of a diagram F:I→C is a finite limit if the indexing category I has finitely many objects and finitely many morphisms, including identities.

form.4bf98f05c3f5ea58.primitive-element.text: For a finite field extension E/F, a primitive element is an element alpha of E such that the smallest subfield containing F and alpha is all of E.

form.4c373b6c62943620.associated-prime.text: For an R-module M, a prime ideal p of R is associated to M if p is the annihilator ideal of some element of M.

form.4c7d59ba7058613b.affine-scheme.text: An affine scheme is a locally ringed space isomorphic to the prime spectrum of a commutative ring equipped with its structure sheaf.

form.4f7edb6d32334f67.local-ring-unique-.text: A nonzero commutative ring R is local if it possesses exactly one maximal ideal.

form.4f7edb6d32334f67.local-ring-nonunit.text: Equivalently, a nonzero commutative ring R is local if the set of its nonunits is an ideal; this ideal is necessarily the ring's unique maximal ideal.

form.504ceffbd86d9488.coherent-ring.text: A ring R is coherent if every finitely generated ideal of R admits a finite presentation as an R-module.

form.50710e767dabd981.colimit-diagram-se.display_term: colimit of a diagram of sets
form.50710e767dabd981.colimit-diagram-se.context: Category theory: colimit of a diagram of sets
form.50710e767dabd981.colimit-diagram-se.text: For a set-valued diagram F:I→Sets, its colimit is the disjoint union of the sets F(i), modulo the equivalence relation generated by x∼F(u)(x) for each arrow u:i→j.

form.50710e767dabd981.limit-diagram-sets.display_term: inverse limit of a diagram of sets
form.50710e767dabd981.limit-diagram-sets.context: Category theory: inverse limit of a diagram of sets
form.50710e767dabd981.limit-diagram-sets.text: For a set-valued diagram F:I→Sets, its limit is the subset of the Cartesian product ∏_i F(i) consisting of families (x_i) satisfying F(u)(x_i)=x_j for every arrow u:i→j in I.

form.50d335de00e5f11d.algebraic-extensio.text: An extension K/k of fields is algebraic if every element α∈K satisfies a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in k.

form.50d335de00e5f11d.galois-extension-r.text: An algebraic extension K/k is Galois precisely when it is both separable and normal over k.

form.50d335de00e5f11d.normal-algebraic-e.text: An algebraic extension K/k is normal if every irreducible polynomial over k having one root in K splits completely into linear factors over K.

form.50d335de00e5f11d.purely-inseparable.text: An algebraic field extension K/k in characteristic p>0 is purely inseparable if every α∈K has α^(p^n)∈k for some integer n≥0.

form.50d335de00e5f11d.separable-algebrai.text: An algebraic extension K/k is separable if the minimal polynomial of each α∈K has no repeated roots over an algebraic closure of k.

form.521431d12a6a6ea2.representable-fibr.context: Category theory: representable category fibred in groupoids
form.521431d12a6a6ea2.representable-fibr.text: A category p:S→C fibred in groupoids is representable if there exists an object X of C and an equivalence over C between S and the slice category C/X.

form.52683cac2ccf3bad.locally-ringed-spa.text: A locally ringed space is a topological space X together with a sheaf of rings O_X whose stalk at every point of X is a local ring.
A morphism of locally ringed spaces consists of a continuous map and a compatible morphism of structure sheaves, with induced maps on all stalks required to be local ring homomorphisms.

form.559efcb6f15ddc96.total-quotient-rin.text: The total quotient ring Q(R) of a commutative ring R is the localization S^{-1}R at the multiplicative set S of all nonzerodivisors of R, allowing fractions with any regular denominator.

form.559efcb6f15ddc96.zerodivisor-of-rin.context: Commutative algebra: zerodivisor and regular element
form.559efcb6f15ddc96.zerodivisor-of-rin.text: An element r of a commutative ring R is a zerodivisor when some nonzero element s∈R satisfies rs=0; a nonzerodivisor is an element for which multiplication by r on R is injective.

form.56119d315cf02fdf.two-category-over-.display_term: 2-category of categories over a base category
form.56119d315cf02fdf.two-category-over-.context: Higher category theory: 2-category of categories over a base category
form.56119d315cf02fdf.two-category-over-.text: For a category C, its 2-category of categories over C has as objects functors p:S→C, as 1-morphisms functors G:S→S′ satisfying p′G=p, and as 2-morphisms natural transformations between such functors whose components project to identity morphisms in C.

form.56d9781f393fa7d7.representable-func.context: Algebraic geometry: functor representable by a scheme
form.56d9781f393fa7d7.representable-func.text: A contravariant functor F:Sch^op→Sets is representable by a scheme if some scheme X admits a natural isomorphism F(T)≅Hom_Sch(T,X) for every scheme T.

form.57385eed4f89f154.exact-functor.text: A functor between categories with the requisite finite limits and colimits is exact if it preserves both finite limits and finite colimits (equivalently it is both left exact and right exact).

form.5a7f5216e916198b.separable-arbitrar.context: Field theory: separable extension not necessarily algebraic
form.5a7f5216e916198b.separable-arbitrar.text: An arbitrary field extension K/k is separable if every finitely generated intermediate extension E/k with k⊆E⊆K is separably generated.

form.5a7f5216e916198b.separably-generate.text: A field extension K/k is separably generated if there exists a transcendence basis B⊆K over k such that K is a separable algebraic extension of the rational-function field k(B).

form.5b29c5555567bd3d.cohen-macaulay-loc.context: Commutative algebra: Cohen–Macaulay locus of the spectrum
form.5b29c5555567bd3d.cohen-macaulay-loc.text: For a Noetherian ring S, the Cohen–Macaulay locus of Spec(S) is the set of prime ideals q for which the local ring S_q is Cohen–Macaulay.

form.5b6d4a7f88629b12.left-adjoint.text: For functors L:C to D and R:D to C, L is left adjoint to R when there are bijections between the morphisms L(X) to Y in D and X to R(Y) in C, natural in both X and Y.

form.5d1733b1dcffde12.universal-square-z.display_term: universal first-order thickening of a formally unramified map
form.5d1733b1dcffde12.universal-square-z.context: Deformation theory: universal first-order thickening of a formally unramified map
form.5d1733b1dcffde12.universal-square-z.text: For a formally unramified ring map R→S, a universal square-zero thickening is a surjective R-algebra map S′→S with square-zero kernel such that every R-algebra map S→A/I, for any square-zero ideal I of A, has a unique compatible lift S′→A.

form.5e4b8f6efeda6522.category-fibred-in.context: Category theory: category fibred in groupoids
form.5e4b8f6efeda6522.category-fibred-in.text: A functor p:E→C is a category fibred in groupoids if every morphism f:V→U in C lifts to a morphism y→x above f for each object x over U, and each compatible base morphism between the sources of two arrows into x lifts uniquely to a morphism between their domains.

form.60f5f43d4514a466.universally-closed.context: Algebraic geometry: universally closed scheme morphism
form.60f5f43d4514a466.universally-closed.text: A scheme morphism f:X→S is universally closed if for every morphism S′→S the induced base-change map X×_S S′→S′ sends closed subsets to closed subsets.

form.62a7307a49a4bcdd.filtered-colimit-e.display_term: filtered colimit of étale ring maps
form.62a7307a49a4bcdd.filtered-colimit-e.context: Commutative algebra: filtered colimit of étale ring maps
form.62a7307a49a4bcdd.filtered-colimit-e.text: An R-algebra A is a filtered colimit of étale R-algebras if there exists a filtered diagram of étale R-algebras (A_i) and an R-algebra isomorphism A≅colim_i A_i.

form.62b07936747a7a38.closed-union-conne.display_term: closed unions of connected components of Spec(R)
form.62b07936747a7a38.closed-union-conne.context: Commutative algebra: closed unions of connected components of Spec(R)
form.62b07936747a7a38.closed-union-conne.text: A subset T of Spec(R) is closed and a union of connected components if and only if it can be expressed as V(I) for an ideal I generated by idempotent elements of R.

form.646e4dcbd9b6f1e1.profinite-topologi.text: A profinite group is a topological group that is isomorphic as a topological group to an inverse limit of finite discrete topological groups.

form.646e4dcbd9b6f1e1.topological-group.text: A topological group is a group G with a topology under which the multiplication map G×G→G and inversion map G→G are both continuous.

form.646e4dcbd9b6f1e1.topological-module.context: Topology: module over a topological ring
form.646e4dcbd9b6f1e1.topological-module.text: Given a topological ring R, a topological R-module is an R-module M endowed with a topology such that addition M×M→M and scalar multiplication R×M→M are continuous.

form.646e4dcbd9b6f1e1.topological-ring.text: A topological ring is a ring R with a topology for which its addition R×R→R and multiplication R×R→R are continuous maps.

form.65fea875f9a5aa40.gluing-data-scheme.context: Algebraic geometry: descent/gluing data for schemes
form.65fea875f9a5aa40.gluing-data-scheme.text: Gluing data for schemes comprises schemes X_i, open subschemes U_ij⊆X_i, and isomorphisms φ_ij:U_ij→U_ji, with U_ii=X_i, such that the overlaps are compatible on triples and φ_ik=φ_jk∘φ_ij wherever both compositions are defined.

form.6676171d9e5698af.affine-closed-subs.display_term: closed subscheme of an affine scheme
form.6676171d9e5698af.affine-closed-subs.context: Algebraic geometry: closed subscheme of an affine scheme
form.6676171d9e5698af.affine-closed-subs.text: A closed subscheme of the affine scheme Spec(R) is a scheme isomorphic over Spec(R) to Spec(R/I) for some ideal I⊆R, equipped with the closed immersion induced by the quotient map R→R/I.

form.672a4a502273760f.generalization-sta.text: A subset T⊆X is stable under generalization if it contains every generalization y of each point x that it contains.

form.672a4a502273760f.generalizing-conti.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is generalizing if any generalization y′⇝f(x) in Y lifts to a generalization x′⇝x in X with f(x′)=y′.

form.672a4a502273760f.specialization-sta.text: A subset T⊆X is stable under specialization if whenever y∈T and x lies in the closure of {y}, then x also belongs to T.

form.672a4a502273760f.specialization-top.text: For points x and y in a topological space X, x is a specialization of y when x lies in the closure of the singleton {y}; equivalently y is a generalization of x.

form.672a4a502273760f.specializing-conti.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is specializing if every specialization f(x′)⇝y in Y can be lifted to a specialization x′⇝x in X with f(x)=y.

form.6775f8b2e6e1cceb.grothendieck-fibre.text: A functor p:E→C is a category fibred over C when for each object x∈E lying over U and each morphism f:V→U in C there exists a p-cartesian morphism y→x lying over f.

form.6775f8b2e6e1cceb.strongly-cartesian.display_term: cartesian arrow over a base category
form.6775f8b2e6e1cceb.strongly-cartesian.context: Category theory: cartesian arrow over a base category
form.6775f8b2e6e1cceb.strongly-cartesian.text: For a functor p:E→C, a morphism φ:y→x in E is strongly p-cartesian if for every object z in E, each pair consisting of a map ψ:z→x and a base arrow p(z)→p(y) that composes with p(φ) to p(ψ) factors uniquely through φ.

form.68206e8850bdd349.universally-exact-.context: Module theory: pure short exact sequence
form.68206e8850bdd349.universally-exact-.text: A short exact sequence 0→M_1→M_2→M_3→0 of R-modules is universally exact if the first nonzero arrow M_1→M_2 remains injective after tensoring with any R-module; equivalently the entire sequence remains exact after every such tensor product.

form.68206e8850bdd349.universally-inject.context: Module theory: universally injective or pure monomorphism
form.68206e8850bdd349.universally-inject.text: A homomorphism f:M→N of R-modules is universally injective if for every R-module Q the induced tensor map f⊗id_Q:M⊗_R Q→N⊗_R Q is injective.

form.6a21c2d4f3354c8f.reduced-induced-cl.display_term: reduced induced structure on a closed subset
form.6a21c2d4f3354c8f.reduced-induced-cl.context: Algebraic geometry: reduced induced structure on a closed subset
form.6a21c2d4f3354c8f.reduced-induced-cl.text: For a closed subset T of a scheme X, its reduced induced closed subscheme is the unique reduced closed subscheme of X whose underlying topological space equals T.

form.6a21c2d4f3354c8f.reduced-scheme.text: A scheme X is reduced if each local ring O_{X,x} is a reduced ring, meaning it contains no nonzero nilpotent element.

form.6a21c2d4f3354c8f.reduced-scheme-sec.text: Equivalently, a scheme X is reduced exactly when the ring O_X(U) has no nonzero nilpotent elements for every open subset U of X.

form.6a3376e5ecb82bfb.topology-basis.text: For a topological space X, a basis is a family B of open sets such that, whenever an open U contains x, some member of B contains x and is itself contained in U.

form.6a3376e5ecb82bfb.topology-subbasis.text: A subbasis for an existing topology on X is a family of open subsets whose finite intersections form a basis for that topology, with the empty intersection taken as X.

form.6a3d6fae0a1573e0.equivariant-map-g-.display_term: equivariant map between sets with a G-action
form.6a3d6fae0a1573e0.equivariant-map-g-.context: Group theory: equivariant map between sets with a G-action
form.6a3d6fae0a1573e0.equivariant-map-g-.text: If X and Y are G-sets, a G-equivariant map f:X→Y is a function satisfying f(g·x)=g·f(x) for every g∈G and x∈X.

form.6a3d6fae0a1573e0.group-left-action.display_term: left group action on a set
form.6a3d6fae0a1573e0.group-left-action.context: Group theory: left group action on a set
form.6a3d6fae0a1573e0.group-left-action.text: A left action of a group G on a set X is a map G×X→X such that e·x=x for all x and (gh)·x=g·(h·x) for every g,h∈G and x∈X.

form.6c51aeb904a0fe74.geometrically-redu.text: A k-algebra A is geometrically reduced if for every field extension K/k the tensor-product K-algebra A⊗_k K is a reduced ring.

form.6c51aeb904a0fe74.geometric-reducedn.text: Equivalently, A is geometrically reduced over k if A⊗_k k^perf is reduced, where k^perf denotes the perfect closure of k; this is a field-extension test of the same property.

form.6cf5ec77f1eb9581.projective-module-.display_term: characterization of projectivity using flatness and Mittag-Leffler modules
form.6cf5ec77f1eb9581.projective-module-.context: Module theory: characterization of projectivity using flatness and Mittag-Leffler modules
form.6cf5ec77f1eb9581.projective-module-.text: An R-module M is projective if and only if it is flat and Mittag-Leffler and is isomorphic to a direct sum of countably generated R-modules.

form.6d6a6ac3c1bd1c00.finite-ring-homomo.text: A homomorphism R→S of rings is finite if S is finitely generated as an R-module through the given homomorphism.

form.6f35dab884da6c30.etale-at-prime.display_term: local étaleness at a target prime
form.6f35dab884da6c30.etale-at-prime.context: Commutative algebra: local étaleness at a target prime
form.6f35dab884da6c30.etale-at-prime.text: A ring map R→S is étale at a prime q∈Spec(S) if there is an element g∈S\q such that the localized ring map R→S_g is étale.

form.6f35dab884da6c30.etale-ring-map.text: A ring map R→S is étale if S is finitely presented over R and its naive cotangent complex NL_{S/R} has zero homology in both degrees 1 and 0, equivalently H_1(NL_{S/R})=0 and Ω_{S/R}=0.

form.702f390cae5f9540.equalizer-category.context: Category theory: equalizer of two parallel arrows
form.702f390cae5f9540.equalizer-category.text: Given parallel morphisms f,g:X⇉Y in a category C, an equalizer is a morphism e:E→X such that f∘e=g∘e and any h:Z→X satisfying f∘h=g∘h factors uniquely through e.

form.709d3d2f82950c5b.directed-preordere.text: A directed set is a nonempty preordered set I such that for any i,j∈I there is k∈I satisfying i≤k and j≤k.

form.709d3d2f82950c5b.inductive-system.context: Category theory: direct system over a preorder
form.709d3d2f82950c5b.inductive-system.text: For a preorder I, an inductive or direct system in a category C assigns objects M_i and maps f_{ij}:M_i→M_j for i≤j with identity maps f_{ii} and composition compatibility f_{ik}=f_{jk}∘f_{ij}.

form.709d3d2f82950c5b.inverse-system.context: Category theory: inverse system over a preorder
form.709d3d2f82950c5b.inverse-system.text: An inverse system over a preorder I in a category C assigns objects M_i and transition maps f_{ij}:M_i→M_j whenever j≤i, with f_{ii}=id and f_{ik}=f_{jk}∘f_{ij} when k≤j≤i.

form.709d3d2f82950c5b.partially-ordered-.text: A partially ordered set is a preordered set whose relation also satisfies antisymmetry: i≤j and j≤i together imply i=j.

form.709d3d2f82950c5b.preordered-set.context: Order theory: preorder and preordered set
form.709d3d2f82950c5b.preordered-set.text: A preordered set is a set I endowed with a reflexive and transitive binary relation ≤.

form.70f44988651b76b5.module-localizatio.context: Module theory: localization of an R-module
form.70f44988651b76b5.module-localizatio.text: For an R-module M and multiplicative subset S⊆R, the module S^{-1}M consists of fractions m/s modulo (m,s)∼(m′,s′) when t(s′m−sm′)=0 for some t∈S, with its natural S^{-1}R-module structure.

form.70f44988651b76b5.ring-localization-.display_term: ring localization at a multiplicative subset
form.70f44988651b76b5.ring-localization-.context: Commutative algebra: ring localization at a multiplicative subset
form.70f44988651b76b5.ring-localization-.text: Given a commutative ring R and multiplicative subset S⊆R, the localization S^{-1}R is the ring of fractions r/s modulo (r,s)∼(r′,s′) if t(rs′−r′s)=0 for some t∈S.

form.711d6a9a3f5a61ca.relative-de-rham-c.context: Commutative algebra: relative algebraic de Rham complex
form.711d6a9a3f5a61ca.relative-de-rham-c.text: For a ring homomorphism A→B, the relative de Rham complex Ω^•_{B/A} is the graded complex with Ω^p_{B/A}=∧^p_B Ω^1_{B/A}, Ω^0=B, and differentials d:Ω^p→Ω^{p+1} uniquely extending the universal derivation and satisfying d(b_0 db_1∧⋯∧db_p)=db_0∧db_1∧⋯∧db_p.

form.720eaae9156f6f4e.separable-algebrai.text: An algebraic element α in a field extension E/F is separable over F if its minimal polynomial over F is separable.
An algebraic extension E/F is separable if every element of E is separable over F.

form.720eaae9156f6f4e.separable-degree-p.display_term: separable degree of an irreducible polynomial
form.720eaae9156f6f4e.separable-degree-p.context: Field theory: separable degree of an irreducible polynomial
form.720eaae9156f6f4e.separable-degree-p.text: The separable degree of an irreducible polynomial f over F is the number of its distinct roots in an algebraic closure of F, counted without multiplicities.

form.720eaae9156f6f4e.separable-irreduci.text: An irreducible polynomial f∈F[x] is separable if f and its formal derivative f′ are relatively prime; equivalently, f has no repeated root in an algebraic closure of F.

form.7210832bc589f307.field-extension.text: An extension E/F of fields is an inclusion F⊆E of fields; equivalently, it is an injective field homomorphism F→E with the image identified as a subfield of E.

form.7210832bc589f307.tower-of-field-ext.text: A tower of field extensions is a finite sequence of inclusions E_0⊆E_1⊆⋯⊆E_n, so each E_i is a field extension of E_{i−1}.

form.7368f71dcc6adfef.profinite-topologi.display_term: profinite space via finite inverse limits
form.7368f71dcc6adfef.profinite-topologi.context: Topology: profinite space via finite inverse limits
form.7368f71dcc6adfef.profinite-topologi.text: A topological space X is profinite when it is homeomorphic to an inverse limit of finite discrete topological spaces.

form.7368f71dcc6adfef.profinite-space-co.display_term: profinite space via finite inverse limits
form.7368f71dcc6adfef.profinite-space-co.context: Topology: profinite space via finite inverse limits
form.7368f71dcc6adfef.profinite-space-co.text: Equivalently, a topological space is profinite exactly when it is quasi-compact, Hausdorff, and totally disconnected.

form.73fe3063f488b859.embedded-associate.display_term: embedded associated prime of a module
form.73fe3063f488b859.embedded-associate.context: Commutative algebra: embedded associated prime of a module
form.73fe3063f488b859.embedded-associate.text: For an R-module M, an embedded associated prime is a prime p∈Ass_R(M) that is not minimal under inclusion among the associated prime ideals of M.

form.73fe3063f488b859.embedded-prime-rin.display_term: embedded prime ideal of a ring
form.73fe3063f488b859.embedded-prime-rin.context: Commutative algebra: embedded prime ideal of a ring
form.73fe3063f488b859.embedded-prime-rin.text: An embedded prime of a ring R is an embedded associated prime of R considered as an R-module.

form.74cd6dc48e0606fc.category-fibred-in.context: Category theory: category fibred in setoids
form.74cd6dc48e0606fc.category-fibred-in.text: A category fibred in setoids over C is a category fibred in groupoids p:E→C such that each fibre category E_U is a setoid.

form.74cd6dc48e0606fc.setoid-category.text: A setoid is a groupoid C in which every object has only its identity automorphism; equivalently, between two objects there is at most one arrow, and its existence is an equivalence relation.

form.74cd6dc48e0606fc.two-category-fibre.context: Higher category theory: 2-category of fibred setoids
form.74cd6dc48e0606fc.two-category-fibre.text: The 2-category fibred in setoids over C has such fibred categories as objects, functors commuting with their projections as 1-morphisms and natural transformations over identity arrows of C as 2-morphisms.

form.74e36635b2776fe8.bilinear-map-modul.text: For R-modules M,N,P, a map b:M×N→P is R-bilinear if it is R-linear in M when N is fixed and R-linear in N when M is fixed.

form.74e36635b2776fe8.tensor-product-mod.context: Module theory: tensor product by universal property
form.74e36635b2776fe8.tensor-product-mod.text: For R-modules M and N, their tensor product M⊗_R N is an R-module equipped with a bilinear map M×N→M⊗_R N universal among all bilinear maps into R-modules: every bilinear map b:M×N→P factors uniquely through an R-linear map M⊗_R N→P.

form.7748e9fee3d01ef2.countably-generate.context: Module theory: countably generated projective module criterion
form.7748e9fee3d01ef2.countably-generate.text: A countably generated R-module M is projective if and only if it is both flat and Mittag-Leffler, in the sense of the canonical tensor-product comparison.

form.7748e9fee3d01ef2.mittag-leffler-mod.context: Module theory: Mittag-Leffler module via tensor-product comparison
form.7748e9fee3d01ef2.mittag-leffler-mod.text: An R-module M is Mittag-Leffler if for every family (Q_i) of R-modules, the canonical homomorphism M⊗_R∏_i Q_i→∏_i(M⊗_R Q_i) is injective.

form.7781214e9120a52e.finite-global-dime.context: Homological algebra: global dimension of a ring
form.7781214e9120a52e.finite-global-dime.text: A ring R has finite global dimension if a finite integer n exists such that every R-module has projective dimension at most n; the minimum such n is the global dimension of R.

form.7781214e9120a52e.projective-dimensi.context: Homological algebra: projective dimension of a module
form.7781214e9120a52e.projective-dimensi.text: The projective dimension pd_R(M) of an R-module M is the least integer n≥0 for which there exists an exact projective resolution 0→P_n→⋯→P_0→M→0, or infinity when no finite such resolution exists.

form.788671763be693df.ext-group.context: Homological algebra: derived Hom or Ext group
form.788671763be693df.ext-group.text: For R-modules M and N, Ext_R^i(M,N) is the ith cohomology of the cochain complex Hom_R(F_•,N) obtained by applying Hom_R(−,N) to a free resolution F_•→M.

form.788671763be693df.free-module-resolu.text: A free resolution of an R-module M is an exact augmented chain complex ⋯→F_2→F_1→F_0→M→0 with every F_i a free R-module.

form.7ca4fb934b2f076c.kahler-differentia.context: Commutative algebra: Kähler differentials via universal derivation
form.7ca4fb934b2f076c.kahler-differentia.text: For a ring map R→S, the module of Kähler differentials Ω_{S/R} is an S-module with a universal R-derivation d:S→Ω_{S/R} such that composition with d gives a bijection Hom_S(Ω_{S/R},M)≅Der_R(S,M) for every S-module M.

form.7ca4fb934b2f076c.r-derivation.display_term: derivation relative to a base ring
form.7ca4fb934b2f076c.r-derivation.context: Commutative algebra: derivation relative to a base ring
form.7ca4fb934b2f076c.r-derivation.text: For a ring map R→S and an S-module M, an R-derivation D:S→M is an additive map vanishing on the image of R and satisfying Leibniz's law D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a).

form.7ee45a1fa46d2b2f.bourbaki-proper-ma.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is Bourbaki-proper if the product map id_Z×f:Z×X→Z×Y is closed for every topological space Z.

form.7ee45a1fa46d2b2f.proper-topological.display_term: proper map requiring separatedness and universal closedness
form.7ee45a1fa46d2b2f.proper-topological.context: Topology: proper map requiring separatedness and universal closedness
form.7ee45a1fa46d2b2f.proper-topological.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is proper under the Stacks Project's convention if it is both separated (its diagonal is closed) and universally closed.

form.7ee45a1fa46d2b2f.quasiproper-contin.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is quasi-proper when the inverse image under f of every quasi-compact subset of Y is quasi-compact in X.

form.7ee45a1fa46d2b2f.universally-closed.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is universally closed if every base change f_Z:X×_Y Z→Z along an arbitrary continuous map Z→Y is a closed map.

form.8069f09a769d34f5.binary-product-cat.context: Category theory: binary product of objects
form.8069f09a769d34f5.binary-product-cat.text: A product of objects X,Y in a category C is an object P with projections p:P→X and q:P→Y such that for every Z and arrows f:Z→X and g:Z→Y there is a unique arrow h:Z→P with p∘h=f and q∘h=g.

form.82307b7a25fdc9fd.quasiregular-seque.display_term: quasi-regular sequence relative to a module
form.82307b7a25fdc9fd.quasiregular-seque.context: Commutative algebra: quasi-regular sequence relative to a module
form.82307b7a25fdc9fd.quasiregular-seque.text: For an R-module M and elements f_1,…,f_c generating J⊆R, the sequence is M-quasi-regular if the graded map (M/JM)⊗_{R/J}(R/J)[X_1,…,X_c]→⊕_{n≥0}J^nM/J^{n+1}M, sending X_i to the class of f_i, is an isomorphism.

form.829f95eb2dfbf360.catenary-commutati.text: A commutative ring R is catenary when, for any primes p⊆q, maximal finite chains of primes connecting p to q all have the same length and the possible chain lengths are bounded above.

form.829f95eb2dfbf360.universally-catena.context: Commutative algebra: universally catenary Noetherian ring
form.829f95eb2dfbf360.universally-catena.text: A Noetherian ring R is universally catenary if every finitely generated R-algebra is catenary.

form.831db4eab7a244a4.geometrically-inte.text: A k-algebra A is geometrically integral when, for every field extension K/k, the tensor-product algebra A⊗_k K is an integral domain.
Equivalently, a k-algebra A is geometrically integral when A⊗_k k̄ is an integral domain, where k̄ is an algebraic closure of k.

form.83a528850cdf6a59.strict-continuous-.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is strict when the quotient topology from X on the image f(X) agrees with the subspace topology induced on f(X) from Y.

form.83a528850cdf6a59.submersive-continu.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is submersive if it is surjective and Y has the quotient topology for f; equivalently, U⊆Y is open exactly when f^{-1}(U) is open in X.

form.8594a432b165bcda.integral-closure-r.display_term: integral closure inside a specified ring
form.8594a432b165bcda.integral-closure-r.context: Commutative algebra: integral closure inside a specified ring
form.8594a432b165bcda.integral-closure-r.text: For a ring homomorphism R→S, the integral closure of R in S is the subring of S consisting of all elements integral over the image of R.

form.8594a432b165bcda.integral-element-o.display_term: integral element over a base ring
form.8594a432b165bcda.integral-element-o.context: Commutative algebra: integral element over a base ring
form.8594a432b165bcda.integral-element-o.text: For a ring homomorphism R→S, an element s of S is integral over R if s satisfies some monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of R.

form.8594a432b165bcda.integral-ring-homo.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is integral if every element s∈S is integral over R, that is, satisfies some monic polynomial with coefficients from R.

form.86b5d488b98c612f.noetherian-commuta.text: A commutative ring R with identity is Noetherian if every ideal of R is finitely generated.

form.wave2.variant71.noetherian.ascendin.text: A commutative ring R is Noetherian if every ascending chain of ideals I_1⊆I_2⊆⋯ stabilizes.

form.wave2.variant71.noetherian.maximal-.text: A commutative ring R is Noetherian if each nonempty collection of ideals of R has a maximal element under inclusion.

form.wave2.variant71.noetherian.noetheri.text: A commutative ring R is Noetherian if R, regarded as a left R-module over itself, is Noetherian.

form.88f3852fe6ad95bb.mittag-leffler-inv.context: Category theory and homological algebra: Mittag-Leffler inverse system
form.88f3852fe6ad95bb.mittag-leffler-inv.text: A directed inverse system (A_i,φ_{ji}) of sets is Mittag-Leffler if, for every index i, there is j≥i such that im(φ_{ki}:A_k→A_i)=im(φ_{ji}:A_j→A_i) for all k≥j.

form.8a5f1888f076f50d.formally-etale-rin.context: Commutative algebra: formally étale ring map
form.8a5f1888f076f50d.formally-etale-rin.text: A ring map R→S is formally étale if for every R-algebra A and ideal I⊆A with I²=0, every R-algebra map S→A/I lifts to exactly one R-algebra map S→A.

form.8a65ad25b01e5104.base-change-scheme.context: Algebraic geometry: base change of a scheme
form.8a65ad25b01e5104.base-change-scheme.text: For a scheme morphism X→S and a morphism S′→S, the base change of X to S′ is the fibre-product scheme X_{S′}=X×_S S′, equipped with its projection to S′.

form.8a65ad25b01e5104.base-change-stable.display_term: stability of a relative property under base change
form.8a65ad25b01e5104.base-change-stable.context: Algebraic geometry: stability of a relative property under base change
form.8a65ad25b01e5104.base-change-stable.text: A property P of schemes over a base is preserved under arbitrary base change if every X→S having P yields X×_S S′→S′ with P for every morphism S′→S.

form.8a65ad25b01e5104.scheme-theoretic-f.text: For f:X→S and s∈S, the scheme-theoretic fibre X_s is X×_S Spec(κ(s)), considered as a scheme over the residue field κ(s).

form.8af10c63c1949034.inertia-of-fibred-.context: Higher category theory: inertia fibred category
form.8af10c63c1949034.inertia-of-fibred-.text: For a category S fibred over C, its inertia fibred category I_S has as objects pairs (x,α) with x in S and α an automorphism of x over the identity morphism of its image in C; morphisms are arrows intertwining these automorphisms.

form.8af10c63c1949034.relative-inertia-o.text: For a morphism F:S→S′ of fibred categories over C, relative inertia I_{S/S′} consists of objects (x,α), where α is an automorphism of x in S whose image F(α) is the identity on F(x).

form.8ca03a051e6b318a.japanese-domain.text: An integral domain R with fraction field K is N-2, or Japanese, if the integral closure of R inside every finite field extension L/K is a finite R-module.

form.8ca03a051e6b318a.n-one-domain.text: An integral domain R with fraction field K is N-1 if its integral closure inside K is a finitely generated R-module.

form.8d020efdba1941aa.noetherian-graded-.context: Graded commutative algebra: Noetherian graded ring
form.8d020efdba1941aa.noetherian-graded-.text: A graded ring A=⊕_{n≥0}A_n is Noetherian if it is a Noetherian ring after forgetting the grading, equivalently every ascending chain of homogeneous ideals stabilizes and each ideal is finitely generated.

form.8d61300dcabf30c0.inverse-limit-sequ.display_term: inverse limit of a countable module system
form.8d61300dcabf30c0.inverse-limit-sequ.context: Module theory: inverse limit of a countable module system
form.8d61300dcabf30c0.inverse-limit-sequ.text: The inverse limit of an inverse system ⋯→M_3→M_2→M_1 is the submodule of ∏_{n≥1}M_n consisting of compatible tuples (m_n), so φ_n(m_n)=m_{n−1} for every n≥2.

form.8d61300dcabf30c0.inverse-sequence-o.context: Module theory: inverse sequence of modules
form.8d61300dcabf30c0.inverse-sequence-o.text: An inverse system of R-modules indexed by positive integers is a sequence M_1←M_2←⋯ with R-linear transition maps φ_n:M_n→M_{n−1}; composites give coherent maps M_n→M_m for all n≥m.

form.8dbafc093b30c2a3.global-complete-in.display_term: global complete intersection over a field
form.8dbafc093b30c2a3.global-complete-in.context: Commutative algebra: global complete intersection over a field
form.8dbafc093b30c2a3.global-complete-in.text: A finite-type algebra S over a field k is a global complete intersection if some presentation S≅k[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c) satisfies dim(S)=n−c.

form.8dbafc093b30c2a3.local-complete-int.display_term: local complete intersection over a field
form.8dbafc093b30c2a3.local-complete-int.context: Commutative algebra: local complete intersection over a field
form.8dbafc093b30c2a3.local-complete-int.text: A finite-type k-algebra S is a local complete intersection over k if Spec(S) has a cover by standard open affines D(g_i) for which each ring S_{g_i} is a global complete intersection over k.

form.8f376cdea16a26da.closed-immersion-l.display_term: closed immersion of locally ringed spaces
form.8f376cdea16a26da.closed-immersion-l.context: Algebraic geometry: closed immersion of locally ringed spaces
form.8f376cdea16a26da.closed-immersion-l.text: A morphism i:Z→X of locally ringed spaces is a closed immersion if its underlying map identifies Z homeomorphically with a closed subset of X, the sheaf homomorphism O_X→i_*O_Z is surjective, and its kernel is locally generated by sections.

form.8f376cdea16a26da.closed-subspace-fr.display_term: closed subspace determined by an ideal sheaf
form.8f376cdea16a26da.closed-subspace-fr.context: Algebraic geometry: closed subspace determined by an ideal sheaf
form.8f376cdea16a26da.closed-subspace-fr.text: Given a locally ringed space X and a locally section-generated sheaf of ideals I⊆O_X, the associated closed subspace is the support Z of O_X/I with the quotient structure sheaf O_Z whose direct image under Z↪X equals O_X/I.

form.8f7683667fac9d28.category-colimit.context: Category theory: colimit of a diagram
form.8f7683667fac9d28.category-colimit.text: For a diagram F:I→C, a colimit is an object Q equipped with compatible morphisms F(i)→Q such that every other cocone F(i)→Z factors uniquely through Q.

form.8f7683667fac9d28.category-limit.context: Category theory: limit of a diagram
form.8f7683667fac9d28.category-limit.text: For a diagram F:I→C, a limit consists of an object L of C with arrows L→F(i) compatible with every arrow of I, such that each other compatible cone factors uniquely through L.

form.8f7683667fac9d28.general-categorica.context: Category theory: coproduct of a family
form.8f7683667fac9d28.general-categorica.text: The coproduct of a family (X_i) in C is the colimit of the discrete diagram indexed by its family, with injections from the X_i satisfying the dual universal property.

form.8f7683667fac9d28.general-categorica.context: Category theory: product of a family
form.8f7683667fac9d28.general-categorica.text: The product of a family (X_i) in a category C is the limit of the discrete diagram indexed by its family, with projections to the X_i satisfying the usual universal property.

form.90b0d1ecfa394230.jacobson-radical-r.text: For a commutative ring R, its Jacobson radical Jac(R) is the intersection of all maximal ideals of R.

form.90b0d1ecfa394230.jacobson-radical-u.text: Equivalently, an element x∈R belongs to Jac(R) exactly when 1−xy is invertible in R for every y∈R.

form.91ebb3796458d5bb.finite-generated-m.text: An R-module M is finitely generated if there exist m_1,…,m_n∈M such that M=Rm_1+⋯+Rm_n; equivalently there is a surjective homomorphism R^n→M for some finite n.

form.91ebb3796458d5bb.finitely-presented.context: Module theory: finite presentation via filtered-colimit Hom
form.91ebb3796458d5bb.finitely-presented.text: An R-module M is finitely presented if and only if for every filtered diagram N_i the canonical map colim_i Hom_R(M,N_i)→Hom_R(M,colim_i N_i) is a bijection.

form.93aaac46cdf41116.henselian-local-ri.text: A local ring (R,m) with residue field κ is Henselian if every monic f∈R[T] and every simple zero ā of f̄ in κ lift to a zero a∈R reducing to ā modulo m.

form.93aaac46cdf41116.strictly-henselian.context: Commutative algebra: strictly Henselian local ring
form.93aaac46cdf41116.strictly-henselian.text: A local ring R is strictly Henselian if it is Henselian and its residue field has no nontrivial separable algebraic extensions.

form.93ca4dd46b3ed2ee.essentially-finite.display_term: ring map essentially of finite presentation
form.93ca4dd46b3ed2ee.essentially-finite.context: Commutative algebra: ring map essentially of finite presentation
form.93ca4dd46b3ed2ee.essentially-finite.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is essentially of finite presentation if S is a localization of an R-algebra A that admits a presentation with finitely many polynomial generators and relations.

form.93ca4dd46b3ed2ee.essentially-finite.display_term: ring map essentially of finite type
form.93ca4dd46b3ed2ee.essentially-finite.context: Commutative algebra: ring map essentially of finite type
form.93ca4dd46b3ed2ee.essentially-finite.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is essentially of finite type if S is isomorphic to a localization T^{-1}A of an R-algebra A finitely generated over R.

form.9442fc10b22be057.artinian-commutati.text: A commutative ring R is Artinian if every descending chain I_1⊇I_2⊇⋯ of ideals eventually stabilizes.

form.951ae8411d8a974b.depth-module-ideal.display_term: depth of a finite module relative to an ideal
form.951ae8411d8a974b.depth-module-ideal.context: Commutative algebra: depth of a finite module relative to an ideal
form.951ae8411d8a974b.depth-module-ideal.text: For a finite R-module M and ideal I⊆R, depth_I(M) is the supremum of lengths of M-regular sequences whose entries lie in I when IM≠M, and is defined to be infinite when IM=M.

form.951ae8411d8a974b.depth-module-local.context: Commutative algebra: depth over a local ring
form.951ae8411d8a974b.depth-module-local.text: For a finite module M over a local ring (R,m), the depth of M is depth_m(M), the supremal length of an M-regular sequence of elements in m, with depth(0)=infinity.

form.96053e8d2dff5465.lattice-vector-spa.display_term: R-lattice in a finite-dimensional vector space
form.96053e8d2dff5465.lattice-vector-spa.context: Commutative algebra: R-lattice in a finite-dimensional vector space
form.96053e8d2dff5465.lattice-vector-spa.text: For a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain R with fraction field K and finite-dimensional K-vector space V, an R-lattice in V is a finite R-submodule M⊆V whose K-span equals V.

form.96053e8d2dff5465.order-vanishing-on.display_term: order of vanishing along a one-dimensional local domain
form.96053e8d2dff5465.order-vanishing-on.context: Commutative algebra: order of vanishing along a one-dimensional local domain
form.96053e8d2dff5465.order-vanishing-on.text: For a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain R with fraction field K, the order of vanishing of a nonzero a∈R is length_R(R/(a)); it extends to K× by ord_R(a/b)=length_R(R/(a))−length_R(R/(b)).

form.988d26ef7c849694.epimorphism-commut.context: Commutative algebra: categorical epimorphism of rings
form.988d26ef7c849694.epimorphism-commut.text: A ring homomorphism f:R→S is an epimorphism in the category of commutative rings if every pair of ring maps g,h:S→T satisfying g∘f=h∘f are equal; equivalently the multiplication map S⊗_R S→S is an isomorphism.

form.9d27e470d02eae69.filtered-category.text: A category I is filtered if it is nonempty, any two objects admit arrows into a common object, and every pair of parallel arrows u,v:i⇉j can be equalized after an arrow j→k.

form.9d27e470d02eae69.filtered-colimit.context: Category theory: filtered colimit of a diagram
