form.9d27e470d02eae69.filtered-colimit.text: A filtered colimit is a colimit of a diagram F:I→C indexed by a filtered category I; in Sets it identifies elements that become equal at some later common stage.

form.9d9d1e7e5a365423.category-of-dotted.context: Higher category theory: category of dotted-arrow fillers
form.9d9d1e7e5a365423.category-of-dotted.text: Given a fixed 2-commutative solid square in a (2,1)-category, its category of dotted arrows has objects the possible diagonal 1-morphisms completing the square together with specified compatible invertible 2-morphisms, and morphisms the 2-isomorphisms respecting these data.

form.9f75052b1742ab3f.cofiltered-categor.text: A category I is cofiltered if its opposite category I^op is filtered; equivalently I is nonempty, any two objects receive arrows from a common object, and any parallel arrows become equal after precomposition from another object.

form.a12da9dfe3ad7ff8.geometrically-conn.text: A k-algebra A is geometrically connected if for every field extension K/k the topological space Spec(A⊗_k K) is connected.

form.a1d0959fa7703e41.inverse-limit-topo.text: The limit of a diagram of topological spaces (X_i,f_{ij}) is the subset of the product ∏_i X_i consisting of all families (x_i) compatible with the diagram maps, equipped with its subspace topology from the product.

form.a38f1da0bc017afe.noetherian-i-adic-.display_term: I-adic completion of a Noetherian ring
form.a38f1da0bc017afe.noetherian-i-adic-.context: Commutative algebra: I-adic completion of a Noetherian ring
form.a38f1da0bc017afe.noetherian-i-adic-.text: For a Noetherian commutative ring R and ideal I, the I-adic completion R^ is the inverse-limit ring lim_n R/I^n, with structure homomorphism R→R^ induced by the quotient maps.

form.a4bbabe606a10067.affine-blowup-alge.display_term: affine chart algebra of a blowup
form.a4bbabe606a10067.affine-blowup-alge.context: Commutative algebra: affine chart algebra of a blowup
form.a4bbabe606a10067.affine-blowup-alge.text: For a∈I, the affine blowup algebra R[I/a] is the degree-zero part of the homogeneous localization of the Rees algebra ⊕_{n≥0}I^n at the degree-one element represented by a; its elements are represented by x/a^n with x∈I^n.

form.a4bbabe606a10067.rees-blowup-algebr.display_term: Rees algebra or blowup algebra of an ideal
form.a4bbabe606a10067.rees-blowup-algebr.context: Commutative algebra: Rees algebra or blowup algebra of an ideal
form.a4bbabe606a10067.rees-blowup-algebr.text: Given an ideal I of a commutative ring R, the Rees algebra of I is the nonnegatively graded R-algebra ⊕_{n≥0}I^n, with I^0=R and multiplication induced by the products I^m I^n⊆I^{m+n}.

form.a54f6089c72fdd84.small-extension-ar.display_term: small extension of Artinian local rings
form.a54f6089c72fdd84.small-extension-ar.context: Commutative algebra: small extension of Artinian local rings
form.a54f6089c72fdd84.small-extension-ar.text: A small extension of local Artinian rings is a surjective local ring homomorphism B′→B whose kernel I has length one as a B′-module; consequently I²=0 and the maximal ideal of B′ annihilates I.

form.a54f6089c72fdd84.smooth-at-prime-no.display_term: formal lifting characterization of smoothness at a prime
form.a54f6089c72fdd84.smooth-at-prime-no.context: Commutative algebra: formal lifting characterization of smoothness at a prime
form.a54f6089c72fdd84.smooth-at-prime-no.text: For a finite-type ring map R→S with R Noetherian and prime q of S, smoothness at q is equivalent to having lifts of compatible R-algebra maps S→B across all surjections B′→B of local R-algebras with square-zero kernel, provided the maximal ideal of B lies over q.

form.a570f5bed277bd8b.presheaf-fibre-pro.context: Category theory: fibre product of presheaves
form.a570f5bed277bd8b.presheaf-fibre-pro.text: For natural transformations F→G and H→G of set-valued presheaves on C, their fibre product is the presheaf sending X to the set-theoretic fibre product F(X)×_{G(X)}H(X), with restriction maps inherited componentwise.

form.a570f5bed277bd8b.representable-pres.display_term: relatively representable natural transformation of presheaves
form.a570f5bed277bd8b.representable-pres.context: Category theory: relatively representable natural transformation of presheaves
form.a570f5bed277bd8b.representable-pres.text: For presheaves F,G:C^op→Sets, a natural transformation a:F→G is representable when for every object U in C and element ξ∈G(U), the fibre-product presheaf h_U×_G F formed using ξ:h_U→G is representable.

form.a757d94fc61ac37f.jacobson-topologic.text: A topological space X is Jacobson if for each closed subset Z⊆X, the set of points of Z that are closed in X is dense in Z, so Z is its closure.

form.a81a0fbec29f2186.finite-order-diffe.context: Commutative algebra: differential operator of finite order
form.a81a0fbec29f2186.finite-order-diffe.text: For a ring map R→S and S-modules M,N, an R-linear map D:M→N is a differential operator of order at most k if k=0 and D is S-linear, or if k>0 and for every s∈S the commutator m↦D(sm)−sD(m) has order at most k−1.

form.a81a0fbec29f2186.principal-parts-mo.text: For R→S, an S-module M and integer k≥0, the module of principal parts P^k_{S/R}(M) is the S-module representing differential operators of order at most k from M: Hom_S(P^k_{S/R}(M),N) is naturally identified with Diff^k_{S/R}(M,N).

form.a87b0cc83bb541e4.henselization-loca.context: Commutative algebra: henselization of a local ring
form.a87b0cc83bb541e4.henselization-loca.text: For a local ring (R,m), its henselization R^h is a Henselian local R-algebra initial among local R-homomorphisms from R into Henselian local rings, with maximal ideal mR^h and residue field canonically R/m; it may be constructed as a filtered colimit of suitable étale R-algebras.

form.a87b0cc83bb541e4.strict-henselizati.display_term: strict henselization of a local ring
form.a87b0cc83bb541e4.strict-henselizati.context: Commutative algebra: strict henselization of a local ring
form.a87b0cc83bb541e4.strict-henselizati.text: After choosing a separable closure κ^sep of κ=R/m, the strict henselization R^sh of a local ring (R,m) is a strictly Henselian local R-algebra whose residue field is κ^sep and which satisfies the analogous universal local lifting property compatible with the chosen residue-field embedding.

form.a95feee56dc057ee.module-composition.context: Module theory: length of an R-module
form.a95feee56dc057ee.module-composition.text: The length of an R-module M is the supremum of integers n for which M has a strictly increasing chain of R-submodules 0=M_0⊊M_1⊊⋯⊊M_n=M, with infinity if the possible lengths are unbounded.

form.a95feee56dc057ee.simple-module.text: An R-module M is simple when M is nonzero and its only submodules are zero and M itself.

form.a9ca2e716ceffd36.annihilator-module.context: Module theory: annihilator ideal of a module
form.a9ca2e716ceffd36.annihilator-module.text: For an R-module M, its annihilator Ann_R(M) is the ideal consisting of r∈R for which r·m=0 for every m∈M.

form.a9ca2e716ceffd36.annihilator-module.context: Module theory: annihilator ideal of an element
form.a9ca2e716ceffd36.annihilator-module.text: For m in an R-module M, its annihilator Ann_R(m) is the ideal {r∈R:r·m=0}.

form.a9ca2e716ceffd36.support-module.context: Commutative algebra: support of a module
form.a9ca2e716ceffd36.support-module.text: For an R-module M, its support Supp_R(M) is the subset {p∈Spec(R):M_p≠0} of the prime spectrum, where M_p denotes localization at p.

form.aa975a3ff4883909.locally-quasicompa.text: A topological space X is locally quasi-compact if every point x has a neighbourhood basis consisting of quasi-compact neighbourhoods: for every neighbourhood U of x, there exists a quasi-compact neighbourhood K of x contained in U.

form.aacbc297769cc94a.formally-smooth-ri.context: Commutative algebra: formally smooth ring map
form.aacbc297769cc94a.formally-smooth-ri.text: A commutative ring homomorphism R→S is formally smooth if every R-algebra map S→A/I lifts to an R-algebra map S→A whenever A is an R-algebra and I⊆A satisfies I²=0.

form.ab260940ea9c523d.connected-componen.text: A connected component of a topological space X is a connected subset maximal under inclusion among connected subsets of X.

form.ab260940ea9c523d.connected-topologi.text: A nonempty topological space X is connected if it cannot be expressed as a disjoint union of two nonempty open subsets; equivalently its only clopen subsets are ∅ and X.

form.ab260940ea9c523d.locally-connected-.text: A topological space X is locally connected if each point x possesses a fundamental system of connected neighbourhoods.

form.ab260940ea9c523d.totally-disconnect.text: A topological space is totally disconnected if each of its connected components is a singleton.

form.ac17dab9530c0b80.automorphisms-of-f.context: Field theory: automorphism group of an extension
form.ac17dab9530c0b80.automorphisms-of-f.text: For a field extension E/F, Aut(E/F) is the group, under composition, of field automorphisms σ:E→E satisfying σ(a)=a for every a∈F.

form.ac17dab9530c0b80.normal-algebraic-f.text: An algebraic field extension E/F is normal if the minimal polynomial over F of each element α∈E factors completely into linear factors over E.

form.ac92b309b6aae7a4.representable-one-.context: Higher category theory: representable morphism of fibred groupoids
form.ac92b309b6aae7a4.representable-one-.text: A 1-morphism F:X→Y of categories fibred in groupoids over C is representable when, for every U∈C and every 1-morphism C/U→Y, the 2-fibre product (C/U)×_Y X is a category fibred in groupoids representable by an object over U.

form.af6115a1e1deaad3.coequalizer-topolo.text: For two continuous maps f,g:X⇉Y, their coequalizer in topological spaces is Y modulo the smallest equivalence relation identifying f(x) with g(x) for each x, furnished with the quotient topology.

form.af6115a1e1deaad3.coproduct-topologi.context: Topology: coproduct or disjoint union topology
form.af6115a1e1deaad3.coproduct-topologi.text: The coproduct of a family (X_i) of topological spaces is their disjoint union with the topology for which U is open exactly when U∩X_i is open in X_i for every index i.

form.b040ab223731507a.extremally-disconn.text: A topological space X is extremally disconnected if the closure of every open subset U of X is itself an open subset of X.

form.b0ca759b4a7e7bfb.relative-assassin-.display_term: relative assassin over a ring map
form.b0ca759b4a7e7bfb.relative-assassin-.context: Commutative algebra: relative assassin over a ring map
form.b0ca759b4a7e7bfb.relative-assassin-.text: For a ring map R→S and S-module N, the relative assassin Ass_{S/R}(N) consists of primes q∈Spec(S) such that q is associated to the fibre module N⊗_R κ(p), where p=q∩R; equivalently q is an associated prime of that S-module.

form.b1c99b8dae7a6bde.good-stratificatio.text: A good stratification of X is a partition into locally closed pieces X_i such that, whenever X_i meets the closure of X_j, all of X_i lies in the closure of X_j.

form.b1c99b8dae7a6bde.locally-closed-par.context: Topology: partition into locally closed pieces
form.b1c99b8dae7a6bde.locally-closed-par.text: A partition of a topological space X in this setting is a decomposition X=⨆_{i∈I}X_i into pairwise disjoint locally closed subsets whose union is all of X.

form.b1c99b8dae7a6bde.locally-finite-col.context: Topology: locally finite family of subsets
form.b1c99b8dae7a6bde.locally-finite-col.text: A collection (E_i) of subsets of X is locally finite if every x∈X has an open neighbourhood meeting E_i for only finitely many indices i.

form.b1c99b8dae7a6bde.ordered-stratifica.text: A stratification of X consists of a locally closed partition X=⨆_i X_i and a partial order on the index set such that the closure of X_j lies in the union of pieces X_i with i≤j.

form.b1d6371a257864cf.quasiseparated-sch.text: A scheme morphism f:X→S is quasi-separated if the diagonal map X→X×_S X is quasi-compact.

form.b1d6371a257864cf.separated-scheme-a.context: Algebraic geometry: separatedness of a scheme
form.b1d6371a257864cf.separated-scheme-a.text: A scheme X is separated (respectively quasi-separated) if its structure morphism to Spec(Z) is separated (respectively quasi-separated).

form.b1d6371a257864cf.separated-scheme-m.text: A morphism f:X→S of schemes is separated if its diagonal morphism Δ_{X/S}:X→X×_S X is a closed immersion.

form.b3aefc22ee361c53.kummer-extension.display_term: Kummer extension generated by an nth root
form.b3aefc22ee361c53.kummer-extension.context: Field theory: Kummer extension generated by an nth root
form.b3aefc22ee361c53.kummer-extension.text: In the Kummer setting, an extension L/K is obtained by adjoining an element α satisfying α^n=a∈K, where n≥2 is prime to char(K) and K contains the nth roots of unity; when [L:K] is finite, L/K is a cyclic Galois extension of degree dividing n.

form.b64bc15f46fe0245.vector-space-over-.context: Linear algebra: vector space over a field
form.b64bc15f46fe0245.vector-space-over-.text: A vector space over a field k is an abelian group V together with scalar multiplication k×V→V satisfying distributivity, scalar associativity, and the condition 1·v=v; equivalently V is a unital module over k.

form.b85b64499f3fb523.grothendieck-group.context: Algebraic K-theory: Grothendieck group of finite modules
form.b85b64499f3fb523.grothendieck-group.text: For a ring R, K′_0(R) is the abelian group generated by isomorphism classes [M] of finitely generated R-modules, subject to [M]=[M′]+[M″] for every short exact sequence 0→M′→M→M″→0 of finitely generated modules.

form.b85b64499f3fb523.grothendieck-group.display_term: Grothendieck group of finite projective modules
form.b85b64499f3fb523.grothendieck-group.context: Algebraic K-theory: Grothendieck group of finite projective modules
form.b85b64499f3fb523.grothendieck-group.text: For a ring R, K_0(R) is the abelian group generated by finite projective R-modules up to isomorphism, modulo [P⊕Q]=[P]+[Q], equivalently modulo split short exact sequence relations among these modules.

form.b9153ed268862243.valuative-uniquene.context: Algebraic geometry: valuative uniqueness condition for separatedness
form.b9153ed268862243.valuative-uniquene.text: A scheme morphism f:X→S satisfies the uniqueness part of the valuative criterion if, for every valuation ring V with fraction field K and every commutative diagram Spec(K)→X, Spec(V)→S, there is at most one morphism Spec(V)→X making both triangles commute.

form.b9defeff446a0526.hilbert-polynomial.display_term: Hilbert polynomial of a finite local module
form.b9defeff446a0526.hilbert-polynomial.context: Commutative algebra: Hilbert polynomial of a finite local module
form.b9defeff446a0526.hilbert-polynomial.text: For a finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), the Hilbert polynomial is the rational-coefficient polynomial P such that P(n)=length_R(m^nM/m^{n+1}M) for all sufficiently large n.

form.b9defeff446a0526.hilbert-samuel-len.text: For a finite R-module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), its Hilbert–Samuel length function is χ_M(n)=length_R(M/m^{n+1}M) for nonnegative integers n.

form.b9defeff446a0526.ideal-of-definitio.display_term: ideal of definition of a local ring
form.b9defeff446a0526.ideal-of-definitio.context: Commutative algebra: ideal of definition of a local ring
form.b9defeff446a0526.ideal-of-definitio.text: For a Noetherian local ring (R,m), an ideal I⊆R is an ideal of definition when its radical is the maximal ideal m, equivalently I is m-primary.

form.bcda9860a078827b.quasicompact-morph.context: Algebraic geometry: quasi-compact morphism of schemes
form.bcda9860a078827b.quasicompact-morph.text: A morphism f:X→S of schemes is quasi-compact if the inverse image of each quasi-compact open subset of S is quasi-compact in X; it suffices to test affine open subsets of S.

form.bd90654fb341045a.equidimensional-to.text: A topological space X is equidimensional if all of its irreducible components have the same Krull dimension.

form.bd90654fb341045a.krull-dimension-sp.display_term: Krull dimension of a topological space
form.bd90654fb341045a.krull-dimension-sp.context: Topology: Krull dimension of a topological space
form.bd90654fb341045a.krull-dimension-sp.text: The Krull dimension of a topological space X is the supremum of lengths of strict finite chains of irreducible closed subsets of X, taking dimension −∞ for the empty space.

form.bd90654fb341045a.local-krull-dimens.display_term: local Krull dimension at a point
form.bd90654fb341045a.local-krull-dimens.context: Topology: local Krull dimension at a point
form.bd90654fb341045a.local-krull-dimens.text: For a point x in a topological space X, the local Krull dimension dim_x(X) is the minimum of dim(U) over all open neighbourhoods U of x.

form.bd914b941fe03a76.scheme-fibre-produ.display_term: existence and universal property of scheme fibre products
form.bd914b941fe03a76.scheme-fibre-produ.context: Algebraic geometry: existence and universal property of scheme fibre products
form.bd914b941fe03a76.scheme-fibre-produ.text: For scheme morphisms X→S and Y→S, their fibre product X×_S Y is a scheme with projections to X and Y commuting over S such that for every scheme T, morphisms T→X×_S Y correspond bijectively to pairs of maps T→X and T→Y having equal composites to S.

form.bdc3e54fd4523fad.scheme-local-affin.text: A scheme is a locally ringed space (X,O_X) in which every point admits an open neighbourhood isomorphic, as a locally ringed space, to Spec(R) with its structure sheaf for some commutative ring R.

form.bdc3e54fd4523fad.scheme-morphism.text: A morphism of schemes is a morphism of locally ringed spaces: a continuous map f:X→Y together with a compatible sheaf homomorphism O_Y→f_*O_X inducing local ring homomorphisms on stalks.

form.be14669c52f30e79.categorical-fibre-.context: Category theory: pullback or fibre product
form.be14669c52f30e79.categorical-fibre-.text: Given arrows f:X→S and g:Y→S in a category, a fibre product is an object P with arrows p:P→X and q:P→Y satisfying fp=gq, such that every pair u:T→X, v:T→Y with fu=gv factors uniquely through a map T→P.

form.c15e2b26c207d87e.interior-subset-to.text: The interior Int_X(A) of a subset A of a topological space X is the union of all open subsets of X contained in A, equivalently the largest open subset of X lying in A.

form.c15e2b26c207d87e.nowhere-dense-subs.text: A subset A of a topological space X is nowhere dense when the interior of its closure in X is empty.

form.c236facceae1dd0f.geometrically-regu.context: Commutative algebra: geometrically regular Noetherian algebra
form.c236facceae1dd0f.geometrically-regu.text: A Noetherian k-algebra R is geometrically regular over a field k if R⊗_k K is a regular ring for every finite field extension K/k; equivalently this holds for all field extensions K/k under the hypotheses of the Stacks criterion.

form.c31e56dc023fcbcc.affine-scheme-fibr.display_term: affine fibre products via tensor products
form.c31e56dc023fcbcc.affine-scheme-fibr.context: Algebraic geometry: affine fibre products via tensor products
form.c31e56dc023fcbcc.affine-scheme-fibr.text: For ring homomorphisms A→B and A→C, the fibre product Spec(B)×_{Spec(A)}Spec(C) is canonically isomorphic as an A-scheme to Spec(B⊗_A C).

form.c31e56dc023fcbcc.scheme-fibre-produ.context: Algebraic geometry: fibre product of schemes
form.c31e56dc023fcbcc.scheme-fibre-produ.text: For morphisms X→S and Y→S of schemes, their fibre product is a scheme X×_S Y with commuting projection arrows to X and Y, universal among all schemes mapping compatibly to both over S.

form.c4da44394808f995.injectivity-locus-.text: For a homomorphism φ:P→Q of finite projective R-modules, its fibrewise injectivity locus is the set of p∈Spec(R) for which the induced linear map P⊗_R κ(p)→Q⊗_R κ(p) is injective.

form.c4da44394808f995.surjectivity-locus.display_term: locus of surjectivity of a module homomorphism
form.c4da44394808f995.surjectivity-locus.context: Module theory: locus of surjectivity of a module homomorphism
form.c4da44394808f995.surjectivity-locus.text: For a homomorphism φ:M→N of R-modules, its surjectivity locus in Spec(R) is the set of primes p such that φ_p:M_p→N_p is surjective; for finite N this locus is open under the section's hypotheses.

form.c50e4715a45d9236.relative-global-co.context: Commutative algebra: relative global complete-intersection presentation
form.c50e4715a45d9236.relative-global-co.text: A ring map R→S is a relative global complete intersection if S admits a presentation R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c) for which every nonempty fibre of Spec(S)→Spec(R) has dimension n−c.

form.c50e4715a45d9236.syntomic-ring-homo.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is syntomic if it is flat, finitely presented, and each fibre S⊗_R κ(p), over every p∈Spec(R), is a local complete intersection algebra over κ(p).

form.c766a18ce285a2d8.constructible-subs.context: Commutative algebra: constructible subset of affine spectrum
form.c766a18ce285a2d8.constructible-subs.text: A subset C of Spec(R) is constructible if and only if it is a finite union of subsets D(f)∩V(g_1,…,g_m), with f and each g_i drawn from the commutative ring R.

form.c8b6cfd6a058ab26.finite-field.text: A finite field is a field whose underlying set contains finitely many elements; necessarily its cardinality is p^n for some prime p and positive integer n.

form.cae7ec9ae5b49736.mittag-leffler-dir.text: A directed system of finitely presented R-modules (M_i) is Mittag-Leffler if, for every R-module N, the inverse system Hom_R(M_i,N) with maps induced by transitions is Mittag-Leffler, meaning its images eventually stabilize at every stage.

form.cae7ec9ae5b49736.mittag-leffler-mod.text: An R-module M is Mittag-Leffler if it satisfies the equivalent conditions of the Stacks characterization, including that the canonical map M⊗_R∏_j Q_j→∏_j(M⊗_R Q_j) is injective for every family of R-modules Q_j.

form.cbdedf7241d6bd76.cofinal-subset-wel.context: Order theory: cofinal subset of a well-order
form.cbdedf7241d6bd76.cofinal-subset-wel.text: A subset A of a well-ordered set T is cofinal if for every t∈T some a∈A satisfies t≤a.

form.cbdedf7241d6bd76.cofinality-ordinal.context: Set theory: cofinality of an ordinal
form.cbdedf7241d6bd76.cofinality-ordinal.text: For an ordinal α, its cofinality cf(α) is the least ordinal that is order-isomorphic to a cofinal subset of α; equivalently cf(α) is the smallest cardinality of a cofinal subset.

form.cbe7158b0742af88.colimit-modules.text: The colimit of a diagram (M_i,μ_ij) of R-modules is the quotient of the direct sum ⊕_i M_i by the submodule generated by all elements ι_i(m)−ι_j(μ_ij(m)) for i≤j.

form.cbe7158b0742af88.direct-system-modu.context: Module theory: direct system of modules
form.cbe7158b0742af88.direct-system-modu.text: A system of R-modules indexed by a preordered set I consists of modules M_i and maps μ_ij:M_i→M_j whenever i≤j with μ_ii=id and μ_ik=μ_jk∘μ_ij; it is directed if I is directed.

form.ce0580b5d7dc0b7c.coequalizer-catego.text: For parallel arrows f,g:X⇉Y in a category C, a coequalizer is a morphism q:Y→Q with qf=qg such that every h:Y→Z satisfying hf=hg factors uniquely as h=u q for a morphism u:Q→Z.

form.d0a078e59e1495da.algebraic-element-.context: Field theory: algebraic element over a field
form.d0a078e59e1495da.algebraic-element-.text: An element α of a field extension E/F is algebraic over F if some nonzero polynomial f∈F[x] satisfies f(α)=0.

form.d0a078e59e1495da.algebraic-field-ex.text: A field extension E/F is algebraic if every element of E satisfies at least one nonzero polynomial with coefficients in F.

form.d2b85c43cfbc6c05.finite-presentatio.context: Commutative algebra: finitely presented ring homomorphism
form.d2b85c43cfbc6c05.finite-presentatio.text: A ring map R→S is of finite presentation if S is R-isomorphic to R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m) for finite families of polynomial generators and relations.

form.d2b85c43cfbc6c05.finite-type-ring-m.context: Commutative algebra: ring homomorphism of finite type
form.d2b85c43cfbc6c05.finite-type-ring-m.text: A ring map R→S is of finite type if S can be generated as an R-algebra by finitely many elements, equivalently S is a quotient of R[x_1,…,x_n] for some finite n.

form.d4ab743e56d30cb4.cohen-macaulay-loc.text: A Noetherian local ring (R,m) is Cohen–Macaulay if its depth as an R-module equals its Krull dimension, that is, depth_m(R)=dim(R).

form.d4ab743e56d30cb4.cohen-macaulay-noe.text: A Noetherian commutative ring R is Cohen–Macaulay if for every maximal or prime ideal p, the local ring R_p is Cohen–Macaulay.

form.d7087bb79cf848fa.constructible-topo.display_term: constructible or patch topology of a spectral space
form.d7087bb79cf848fa.constructible-topo.context: Topology: constructible or patch topology of a spectral space
form.d7087bb79cf848fa.constructible-topo.text: For a spectral space X, the constructible topology is generated by the quasi-compact open subsets of X together with their complements; these sets constitute a subbasis.

form.d7087bb79cf848fa.spectral-continuou.text: A continuous map f:X→Y between spectral spaces is spectral if inverse images of quasi-compact open sets in Y are quasi-compact in X.

form.d7087bb79cf848fa.spectral-topologic.text: A space X is spectral if it is sober and quasi-compact, intersections of two quasi-compact open sets are quasi-compact, and the quasi-compact opens form a basis for the topology.

form.d8201788fcb507c5.compatible-localiz.display_term: gluing compatible sections on standard opens
form.d8201788fcb507c5.compatible-localiz.context: Commutative algebra: gluing compatible sections on standard opens
form.d8201788fcb507c5.compatible-localiz.text: For elements f_1,…,f_n∈R generating the unit ideal and an R-module M, a compatible family of local sections is a tuple (m_i∈M_{f_i}) whose images agree in M_{f_i f_j} for every pair i,j; such tuples are exactly the image of M under its diagonal localization map.

form.d8201788fcb507c5.module-gluing-data.display_term: descent data over a finite affine open cover
form.d8201788fcb507c5.module-gluing-data.context: Module theory: descent data over a finite affine open cover
form.d8201788fcb507c5.module-gluing-data.text: For a cover of Spec(R) by D(f_i), gluing data for modules comprise R_{f_i}-modules M_i and isomorphisms between their localizations over D(f_i f_j), satisfying identity and triple-overlap cocycle conditions.

form.daec56e6a2a51cae.connected-category.text: A category I is connected if it is nonempty and each pair of its objects can be joined by a finite sequence of morphisms whose directions may alternate.

form.daec56e6a2a51cae.connected-indexed-.context: Category theory: connected limit or colimit
form.daec56e6a2a51cae.connected-indexed-.text: A limit or colimit of a diagram is called connected when its indexing category is connected; this is a property of the index category rather than the limiting object.

form.db846ebeca42b9ee.finitely-generated.text: An R-module M is finitely generated if a finite list m_1,…,m_n generates all of M by R-linear combinations; equivalently there is an R-linear surjection R^n→M.

form.db846ebeca42b9ee.finitely-presented.text: An R-module M is finitely presented if it admits an exact sequence R^m→R^n→M→0 with m,n finite; finitely many generators and defining relations therefore suffice.

form.dbce785fa0c96b0a.field-characterist.text: The characteristic of a field F is the least positive integer n with n·1_F=0 when such an integer exists, and otherwise equals zero; a positive characteristic must be prime.

form.dbce785fa0c96b0a.prime-subfield.text: The prime subfield of F is its unique smallest subfield, isomorphic to Q in characteristic zero and to F_p in characteristic p>0.

form.dbf5b9529c8ec33a.serre-condition-rk.text: A Noetherian ring R satisfies (R_k) if the localization R_p is regular at each prime p of height at most k.

form.dbf5b9529c8ec33a.serre-condition-sk.context: Commutative algebra: Serre S_k for modules
form.dbf5b9529c8ec33a.serre-condition-sk.text: A finite R-module M has property (S_k) if depth(M_p)≥min(k,dim Supp(M_p)) for all primes p of a Noetherian ring R.

form.dbf5b9529c8ec33a.serre-condition-sk.context: Commutative algebra: Serre S_k for rings
form.dbf5b9529c8ec33a.serre-condition-sk.text: A Noetherian ring R satisfies (S_k) when depth(R_p) is at least min(k,dim R_p) for every prime ideal p.

form.dbf5b9529c8ec33a.serre-normality-cr.text: A Noetherian ring R is normal if and only if it has (R_1) and (S_2), meaning regularity in codimension one and the corresponding lower bounds on local depths.

form.dc7429305b3e37b7.separated-continuo.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is separated when the image of its diagonal map X→X×_Y X is closed in that fibre-product topological space.

form.de2c8164874ee4a9.cofinal-category-f.text: A functor H:I→J is cofinal if for every j in J the comma category (j↓H), whose objects are maps j→H(i), is nonempty and connected by finite zigzags.

form.de2c8164874ee4a9.initial-category-f.text: A functor H:I→J is initial if for every object j of J the comma category (H↓j), consisting of maps H(i)→j, is nonempty and connected.

form.e0849711d61cd26f.nth-root-of-unity.context: Field theory: nth root of unity
form.e0849711d61cd26f.nth-root-of-unity.text: An nth root of unity in a field F is an element ζ satisfying ζ^n=1; all such elements form a subgroup μ_n(F) of F×.

form.e0849711d61cd26f.primitive-nth-root.context: Field theory: primitive root of unity
form.e0849711d61cd26f.primitive-nth-root.text: A primitive nth root of unity in a field F is an element ζ of multiplicative order exactly n.

form.e0dd0b0cffcfff0b.generic-point.text: A generic point of an irreducible closed subset Z of a topological space X is a point η∈Z such that the closure of {η} equals Z.

form.e0dd0b0cffcfff0b.irreducible-compon.text: An irreducible component of a topological space X is a maximal irreducible subset of X under inclusion; every such component is closed.

form.e0dd0b0cffcfff0b.irreducible-topolo.text: A nonempty topological space is irreducible if it cannot be expressed as the union of two proper closed subsets.

form.e205fb263a537d99.dimension-function.text: A dimension function on a topological space X is an integer-valued map δ:X→Z that strictly decreases on nontrivial specializations and drops by exactly one for immediate specializations.

form.e205fb263a537d99.immediate-speciali.text: For distinct points x,y of a topological space, y is an immediate specialization of x if y lies in the closure of {x} and no third point lies between x and y in the specialization relation.

form.e39c701ba05418fb.formal-smoothness-.display_term: formal smoothness of a field extension
form.e39c701ba05418fb.formal-smoothness-.context: Field theory: formal smoothness of a field extension
form.e39c701ba05418fb.formal-smoothness-.text: A field extension K/k is formally smooth over k when every k-algebra map K→A/I across a square-zero quotient lifts to A. In positive characteristic this is equivalent to separability of K/k; in characteristic zero every field extension satisfies it.

form.e3f74861fea6f59a.category-localizat.context: Category theory: localization of a category
form.e3f74861fea6f59a.category-localizat.text: A localization of a category C at a multiplicative system S is a category S^{-1}C with functor Q:C→S^{-1}C making each s∈S invertible and universal among functors from C that invert all s∈S.

form.e3f74861fea6f59a.category-multiplic.context: Category theory: multiplicative system of arrows
form.e3f74861fea6f59a.category-multiplic.text: A multiplicative system of arrows in a category contains all identities, is closed under composition, and satisfies both left and right Ore-square completion and the corresponding cancellation axioms.

form.e606496d592fe305.relatively-prime-p.text: Polynomials f,g∈k[x] over a field k are relatively prime when the ideal (f,g) they generate is the entire polynomial ring k[x].
Two polynomials f,g over a field k are relatively prime if and only if they have no common zero in an algebraic closure of k.

form.e62923cd8ef99cd1.hausdorff-space.text: A topological space X is Hausdorff if every pair of distinct points has disjoint open neighbourhoods.

form.e62923cd8ef99cd1.hausdorff-diagonal.text: A topological space X is Hausdorff exactly when the diagonal {(x,x):x∈X} is a closed subset of X×X with its product topology.

form.e91cf25c30aa59b9.faithfully-flat-mo.text: An R-module M is faithfully flat if tensoring with M preserves and reflects exactness of arbitrary sequences of R-modules.

form.e91cf25c30aa59b9.faithfully-flat-ri.context: Commutative algebra: faithfully flat ring map
form.e91cf25c30aa59b9.faithfully-flat-ri.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is faithfully flat if S is faithfully flat as an R-module under the ring map.

form.e91cf25c30aa59b9.flat-module.text: An R-module M is flat when the tensor functor −⊗_R M carries every exact sequence of R-modules to an exact sequence.

form.e91cf25c30aa59b9.flat-ring-map.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is flat if S is flat as an R-module via the given homomorphism.

form.e97dccfabb3dd0c7.cohen-macaulay-loc.text: A finitely generated module M over a Noetherian local ring R is Cohen–Macaulay if depth_R(M) equals the Krull dimension of the support Supp_R(M).

form.e97dccfabb3dd0c7.cohen-macaulay-mod.text: A finite module M over a Noetherian ring R is Cohen–Macaulay if for each prime p the localized module M_p is Cohen–Macaulay over the local ring R_p.

form.e97dccfabb3dd0c7.maximal-cohen-maca.text: A finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay if depth_R(M)=dim(R), not merely the dimension of its possibly smaller support.

form.eb0cd2c67c6ee622.affine-scheme-morp.display_term: affine scheme morphisms and ring maps
form.eb0cd2c67c6ee622.affine-scheme-morp.context: Algebraic geometry: affine scheme morphisms and ring maps
form.eb0cd2c67c6ee622.affine-scheme-morp.text: For commutative rings A and B, a morphism Spec(B)→Spec(A) of affine schemes is equivalently determined by a ring homomorphism A→B, acting on prime ideals by inverse image.

form.ec5e3a0d13f85f3a.equivalence-object.context: Stacks 4.29.4 equivalence of objects in its explicitly defined strict 2-category, not an independently sourced arbitrary weak bicategory
form.ec5e3a0d13f85f3a.equivalence-object.text: Two objects X,Y in a strict 2-category C are equivalent if there are 1-morphisms F:X→Y and G:Y→X together with invertible 2-morphisms F∘G⇒id_Y and G∘F⇒id_X. This is the Stacks Project strict 2-category convention; weak bicategory equivalences require a separate context/source review.

form.ec5e3a0d13f85f3a.strict-two-categor.text: A strict 2-category consists of objects, hom-categories whose objects are 1-morphisms and arrows are 2-morphisms, and strictly associative and unital composition functors between hom-categories satisfying the interchange law.

form.ed035ec300dc4ceb.irreducible-compon.display_term: irreducible components of the prime spectrum
form.ed035ec300dc4ceb.irreducible-compon.context: Commutative algebra: irreducible components of the prime spectrum
form.ed035ec300dc4ceb.irreducible-compon.text: For a commutative ring R, the irreducible components of Spec(R) are exactly the subsets V(p) where p ranges over prime ideals minimal under inclusion.

form.eea0cd4a31af555c.constructible-subs.context: Topology: constructible subset using retrocompact opens
form.eea0cd4a31af555c.constructible-subs.text: A subset E of a topological space X is constructible if it is a finite union of sets U\V with U and V open and retrocompact in X.

form.eea0cd4a31af555c.locally-constructi.text: A subset E of X is locally constructible if there exists an open cover (V_i) of X such that E∩V_i is constructible as a subset of V_i for each i.

form.eed0c34725956bb5.categorical-epimor.text: A morphism f:X→Y in a category C is an epimorphism if for every object W and maps a,b:Y→W, equality a∘f=b∘f implies a=b.

form.eed0c34725956bb5.categorical-monomo.text: A morphism f:X→Y in a category C is a monomorphism if for every object W and maps a,b:W→X, the equality f∘a=f∘b implies a=b.

form.f0d993a60533fc99.groupoid-valued-pr.context: Strict functor-valued presheaf in Stacks Section 4.37, Example 4.37.1; pseudofunctors with nontrivial coherence data are a separate context not established by this source
form.f0d993a60533fc99.groupoid-valued-pr.text: A (strict) groupoid-valued presheaf on a category C is a functor F:C^op→Groupoids, assigning a groupoid F(U) to every object U and a pullback functor f*:F(U)→F(V) to each arrow f:V→U. Pullbacks preserve identities and compose strictly: (f∘g)*=g*∘f*.

form.f0d993a60533fc99.split-fibred-group.context: Category theory: split category fibred in groupoids
form.f0d993a60533fc99.split-fibred-group.text: A category fibred in groupoids over C is split if it is isomorphic over C to the Grothendieck construction associated with a strict contravariant functor C→Groupoids.

form.f17ea18ebee0660f.module-regular-seq.context: Commutative algebra: regular sequence on a module
form.f17ea18ebee0660f.module-regular-seq.text: A finite sequence f_1,…,f_r in a ring R is M-regular for an R-module M if f_i acts injectively on M/(f_1,…,f_{i-1})M for every i and the final quotient M/(f_1,…,f_r)M is nonzero.

form.f3421024042fb45b.symbolic-power-pri.context: Commutative algebra: symbolic powers of prime ideals
form.f3421024042fb45b.symbolic-power-pri.text: For a prime ideal p of a commutative ring R and n≥0, the nth symbolic power p^(n) is the contraction to R of p^n R_p, equivalently the kernel of R→R_p/p^nR_p.

form.f3d1c8c59cda279e.coefficient-ring-c.text: For a complete local ring (R,m) with residue characteristic p, a coefficient ring is a complete local subring Λ⊆R inducing an isomorphism of residue fields and satisfying Λ∩m=pΛ.

form.f3d1c8c59cda279e.cohen-ring.text: A Cohen ring is a complete discrete valuation ring whose maximal ideal is generated by a prime integer p.

form.f3d1c8c59cda279e.complete-local-rin.text: A local ring (R,m) is complete if the canonical homomorphism R→lim_n R/m^n is an isomorphism; equivalently, its m-adic completion introduces no new elements.

form.f6c83ed1311d9b05.going-down-ring-ho.text: A ring map R→S satisfies going down if, given p⊆p′ in Spec(R) and q′ of S lying above p′, a prime q⊆q′ exists that lies over p.

form.f6c83ed1311d9b05.going-up-ring-homo.text: A ring map R→S satisfies going up if, given p⊆p′ in Spec(R) and q∈Spec(S) above p, some prime q′⊇q of S lies above p′.

form.f7206eb9332b9389.category-valued-pr.context: Strict category-valued presheaf in Stacks Section 4.36, Example 4.36.1: functor from the opposite category, not a second contravariant functor from C^op
form.f7206eb9332b9389.category-valued-pr.text: A (strict) category-valued presheaf on a category C is a functor F:C^op→Cat (equivalently, a contravariant functor from C to Cat). It assigns a category F(U) to each object U and a pullback functor f*:F(U)→F(V) to every arrow f:V→U, with (f∘g)*=g*∘f* and (id_U)* the identity functor.

form.f7206eb9332b9389.split-fibred-categ.text: A fibred category p:E→C is split if it is isomorphic over C to the Grothendieck construction of a strictly contravariant category-valued functor on C.

form.f72779e263dd3e51.discrete-valuation.text: A valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring in the Stacks convention if its associated ordered value group is isomorphic to Z, with its usual order.

form.f72779e263dd3e51.domination-local-r.context: Commutative algebra: domination of local rings
form.f72779e263dd3e51.domination-local-r.text: For local subrings A⊆B of a common field, B dominates A if the maximal ideal of B contracts to the maximal ideal of A.

form.f72779e263dd3e51.valuation-ring-fra.text: An integral domain V with fraction field K is a valuation ring if each nonzero x∈K has at least one of x and x^{-1} lying in V.

form.f77b42c1adb38c56.perfect-closure.context: Field theory: perfect closure of a field
form.f77b42c1adb38c56.perfect-closure.text: The perfect closure of a field k of positive characteristic p is its smallest perfect extension obtained by adjoining all compatible p-power roots of elements of k inside a fixed algebraic closure.

form.f77b42c1adb38c56.perfect-field.text: A field k is perfect if every algebraic field extension of k is separable over k; equivalently k has characteristic zero or, in characteristic p>0, every element of k is a pth power.

form.f810d472f5a4d367.limit-ordinal.text: An ordinal λ is a limit ordinal if it is nonzero and is not the successor of any other ordinal.

form.f810d472f5a4d367.successor-ordinal.text: The successor of an ordinal α is the ordinal α+1=α∪{α}; an ordinal is a successor ordinal if it has this form for some α.

form.f810d472f5a4d367.von-neumann-ordina.text: An ordinal is a transitive set α on which the membership relation ∈ is a well-order: each nonempty subset has an ∈-least element, and every member of α is itself a subset of α.

form.fa3b484c09596cfd.graded-module.text: A graded module M over S=⊕_{n≥0}S_n is an S-module with a direct-sum decomposition M=⊕_{j∈Z}M_j and S_nM_j⊆M_{n+j}.

form.fa3b484c09596cfd.graded-module-shif.context: Graded commutative algebra: shift of graded module
form.fa3b484c09596cfd.graded-module-shif.text: The degree shift M(n) of a graded module M is the graded module whose degree-j component is M(n)_j=M_{n+j}, preserving the ungraded module structure.

form.fa3b484c09596cfd.nonnegatively-grad.context: Graded commutative algebra: nonnegative ring grading
form.fa3b484c09596cfd.nonnegatively-grad.text: A nonnegatively graded ring S is a direct sum S=⊕_{n≥0}S_n of additive groups satisfying S_nS_m⊆S_{n+m} for every n,m≥0.

form.fc44c63c239e5c20.projective-module-.text: An R-module P is projective if the covariant functor Hom_R(P,−) is exact; equivalently every R-linear map P→N lifts across every surjective module map M→N.

form.fc44c63c239e5c20.projective-module-.context: Module theory: direct-summand characterization of projectivity
form.fc44c63c239e5c20.projective-module-.text: An R-module P is projective exactly when it is isomorphic to a direct summand of a free R-module, so some Q satisfies P⊕Q≅R^{(I)} for an index set I.

form.fd3c1a1c0145915a.dimension-finite-m.context: Commutative algebra: dimension of a finite module
form.fd3c1a1c0145915a.dimension-finite-m.text: For a finite module M over a Noetherian ring R, its dimension is the Krull dimension of Supp_R(M), the supremum of lengths of chains of prime ideals belonging to its support.

form.fd3c1a1c0145915a.support-finite-mod.context: Commutative algebra: support of a finite module
form.fd3c1a1c0145915a.support-finite-mod.text: For a finitely generated R-module M, its support is Supp_R(M)={p∈Spec(R):M_p≠0}, a closed subset of Spec(R) when R is Noetherian.

form.fd99f695f227af4a.finite-locally-fre.context: Commutative algebra: finite locally free module
form.fd99f695f227af4a.finite-locally-fre.text: An R-module M is finite locally free if Spec(R) has a standard-open cover over which the localizations of M are free of finite rank, with the rank allowed to vary by open set.

form.fd99f695f227af4a.finite-projective-.text: An R-module M is finite projective exactly when it is finitely generated and projective; equivalently M is a direct summand of R^n for some finite n, or finite locally free.

form.fd99f695f227af4a.locally-free-modul.text: An R-module M is locally free if Spec(R) admits a cover by standard opens D(f_i) such that each localization M_{f_i} is free over R_{f_i}.

form.fef4e69e96c25bfa.contravariant-func.text: A contravariant functor F:C→D is by definition an ordinary functor C^op→D; it sends each arrow X→Y in C to an arrow F(Y)→F(X).

form.fef4e69e96c25bfa.opposite-category.text: For a category C, the opposite category C^op has the same objects as C and a morphism X→Y in C^op for each morphism Y→X in C, with composition reversed.

form.fef4e69e96c25bfa.representable-pres.text: For an object U of a category C, the represented presheaf h_U:C^op→Sets assigns to X the set Hom_C(X,U), acting on arrows by precomposition.

form.ffa8e88785ba9c2b.scheme-zariski-top.context: Algebraic geometry: Zariski topology on a scheme
form.ffa8e88785ba9c2b.scheme-zariski-top.text: The Zariski topology of a scheme X is the topology of its underlying locally ringed space, characterized locally by requiring each affine chart Spec(R)⊆X to carry the prime-spectrum topology whose standard opens are D(f).

form.wave2.alternative39.adjacency-matri.display_term: adjacency matrix of a finite simple undirected graph
form.wave2.alternative39.adjacency-matri.context: Finite simple undirected loop-free graph with an ordered vertex set
form.wave2.alternative39.adjacency-matri.text: Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple undirected graph with a chosen ordering V={v_1,…,v_n}. Its adjacency matrix A=(a_ij) is the n×n matrix with a_ij=1 if {v_i,v_j}∈E and a_ij=0 otherwise.

form.wave2.alternative39.bipartite-undir.context: Graph theory: an undirected graph with an edge-crossing partition, not necessarily complete bipartite
form.wave2.alternative39.bipartite-undir.text: An undirected graph G=(V,E) is bipartite if there exist disjoint subsets A,B⊆V such that V=A∪B and every edge in E has one endpoint in A and the other in B.

form.wave2.alternative39.boolean-ring-no.context: Alternative ring-theory convention: idempotent associative ring without a required multiplicative identity
form.wave2.alternative39.boolean-ring-no.text: A Boolean ring in the possibly nonunital convention is an associative ring R, not assumed to have a multiplicative identity, such that x²=x for every x∈R.

form.wave2.alternative39.boolean-ring-un.context: ProofWiki primary ring-theory convention: ring with multiplicative identity and universal multiplicative idempotence
form.wave2.alternative39.boolean-ring-un.text: A Boolean ring in the unital convention is an associative ring R with multiplicative identity 1_R such that x²=x for every x∈R.

form.wave2.alternative39.borel-sigma-alg.display_term: Borel sigma-algebra of a topological space
form.wave2.alternative39.borel-sigma-alg.context: Topology and measure theory: smallest sigma-algebra containing every open subset of a topological space
form.wave2.alternative39.borel-sigma-alg.text: Let (X,τ) be a topological space. The Borel sigma-algebra B(X,τ) is the smallest sigma-algebra on X containing τ, equivalently the intersection of all sigma-algebras on X containing every τ-open subset.

form.wave2.analysis.antiderivative-on-in.context: Elementary real calculus: differentiable real function on an interval
form.wave2.analysis.antiderivative-on-in.text: Let I⊆R be an open interval and f:I→R. A function F:I→R is an antiderivative of f on I if F is differentiable at every x∈I and F′(x)=f(x) for all x∈I.

form.wave2.analysis.indefinite-integral-.context: Elementary real calculus: full antiderivative family on a connected interval
form.wave2.analysis.indefinite-integral-.text: If f:I→R has an antiderivative F on an interval I, its indefinite integral, written ∫f(x)dx, denotes the family of functions {F+C:C∈R} on I. This is not a single numerical definite integral.

form.wave2.analysis.orthogonal-polynomia.context: DLMF countably infinite discrete support with positive summable weights
form.wave2.analysis.orthogonal-polynomia.text: Let X⊆R be a countably infinite set of distinct points and assign each x∈X a weight w_x>0 with Σ_{x∈X}|x|^k w_x<∞ for every integer k≥0. A system (p_n)_{n≥0} with deg(p_n)=n is orthogonal on X when Σ_{x∈X}p_n(x)p_m(x)w_x=0 for n≠m.

form.wave2.analysis.orthogonal-polynomia.context: DLMF finite set of N+1 distinct points with strictly positive weights
form.wave2.analysis.orthogonal-polynomia.text: Let X⊆R consist of N+1 distinct points with weights w_x>0. Polynomials p_0,…,p_N, with deg(p_n)=n, form a finite orthogonal polynomial system on X if Σ_{x∈X}p_n(x)p_m(x)w_x=0 for all distinct n,m in {0,…,N}.

form.wave2.analysis.orthogonal-polynomia.context: DLMF continuous real interval with admissible nonnegative weight
form.wave2.analysis.orthogonal-polynomia.text: Let (a,b) be a real interval and w≥0 an integrable weight with 0<∫_a^b w(x)dx<∞ and ∫_a^b |x|^k w(x)dx<∞ for every positive integer k. A polynomial system (p_n)_{n≥0}, with deg(p_n)=n, is orthogonal relative to w when ∫_a^b p_n(x)p_m(x)w(x)dx=0 whenever n≠m.

form.wave2.analysis.orthogonal-polynomia.context: DLMF Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure with infinitely many points of increase
form.wave2.analysis.orthogonal-polynomia.text: Let μ be a nonnegative Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure arising from an admissible bounded nondecreasing function with infinitely many points of increase and finite moments ∫|x|^k dμ(x)<∞ for all integers k≥0. A polynomial family p_n of degree n is orthogonal with respect to μ when ∫p_n(x)p_m(x)dμ(x)=0 for n≠m.

form.wave2.analysis.real-absolute-value.display_term: absolute value of a real number
form.wave2.analysis.real-absolute-value.context: OpenStax elementary real algebra: piecewise absolute-value function
form.wave2.analysis.real-absolute-value.text: For each real number x, its absolute value |x| is x if x≥0 and −x if x<0. Consequently |x|≥0 and for real a,b the quantity |a−b| is their usual distance on the real line.

form.wave2.analysis.real-derivative-poin.display_term: derivative of a real function at an interior point
form.wave2.analysis.real-derivative-poin.context: OpenStax calculus: finite two-sided real derivative on an open interval
form.wave2.analysis.real-derivative-poin.text: Let f:I→R be a function on an open real interval I containing a∈I. If the finite limit exists, the derivative of f at a is f′(a)=lim_{h→0}(f(a+h)−f(a))/h, where h≠0 and a+h∈I.

form.wave2.analysis.real-limit-punctured.display_term: finite limit of a real function
form.wave2.analysis.real-limit-punctured.context: Real functions defined on a full punctured neighborhood of the approach point
form.wave2.analysis.real-limit-punctured.text: Suppose a,L∈R and f is defined for every x≠a in some open interval containing a. Then lim_{x→a}f(x)=L if for every ε>0 there exists δ>0 such that for all x with 0<|x−a|<δ in that interval, one has |f(x)−L|<ε.

form.wave2.analysis98.complex-inner-prod.context: Positive-definite Hermitian complex inner-product space, first argument linear
form.wave2.analysis98.complex-inner-prod.text: A complex inner-product space is a complex vector space V equipped with a positive-definite Hermitian form ⟨·,·⟩:V×V→ℂ, linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second.

form.wave2.analysis98.metric-space.context: Nonempty metric space, canonical metric topology
form.wave2.analysis98.metric-space.text: A metric space is a pair (X,d) where X is a nonempty set and d:X×X→ℝ satisfies d(x,x)=0, symmetry d(x,y)=d(y,x), the triangle inequality d(x,z)≤d(x,y)+d(y,z), and d(x,y)>0 whenever x≠y.

form.wave2.analysis98.metric-space.compa.context: Nonempty metric space, canonical metric topology
form.wave2.analysis98.metric-space.compa.text: For a nonempty set X with a metric d, the balls B_d(x,r)={y in X:d(x,y)<r}, r>0, generate a canonical topology τ_d. The metric-space data (X,d) determine the compatible triple (X,τ_d,d), and conversely a triple (X,τ,d) with τ=τ_d determines (X,d). A metrizable topology alone does not specify a unique metric.

form.wave2.analysis98.norm-over-normed-d.context: Vector norm over a normed division ring
form.wave2.analysis98.norm-over-normed-d.text: For a vector space V over a normed division ring K, a norm is a function ∥·∥:V→ℝ≥0 such that ∥v∥=0 iff v=0, ∥av∥=|a|_K∥v∥, and ∥v+w∥≤∥v∥+∥w∥.

form.wave2.analysis98.norm-over-real-or-.context: Vector norm over the real or complex field
form.wave2.analysis98.norm-over-real-or-.text: For a vector space V over ℝ or ℂ, a norm is a map ∥·∥:V→ℝ≥0 satisfying positive definiteness, ∥av∥=|a|∥v∥ for every scalar a, and the triangle inequality.

form.wave2.analysis98.normed-vector-spac.context: Vector space over a normed division ring equipped with a norm
form.wave2.analysis98.normed-vector-spac.text: A normed vector space is a vector space V over a normed division ring K together with a specified norm ∥·∥:V→ℝ≥0 satisfying the norm axioms. The structure can be written (V,∥·∥).

form.wave2.analysis98.real-inner-product.context: Positive-definite symmetric bilinear real inner-product space
form.wave2.analysis98.real-inner-product.text: A real inner-product space is a real vector space V equipped with a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form ⟨·,·⟩:V×V→ℝ.

form.wave2.branch129.indexed-product-top.display_term: product topology of a family of topological spaces
form.wave2.branch129.indexed-product-top.context: Indexed product topology with finite-support restrictions
form.wave2.branch129.indexed-product-top.text: Let {(X_i,τ_i)}_{i∈I} be topological spaces and X=∏_{i∈I}X_i, with projection π_i:X→X_i. The product topology on X is the topology generated by the subbasis {π_i⁻¹(U):i∈I,U∈τ_i}.

form.wave2.branch129.indexed-product-top.display_term: product topology of a family of topological spaces
form.wave2.branch129.indexed-product-top.context: Indexed product topology with finite-support restrictions
form.wave2.branch129.indexed-product-top.text: For the same indexed topological spaces, the product topology is generated by the basis of all products ∏_{i∈I}U_i with each U_i open in X_i and U_i=X_i for all but finitely many i∈I.

form.wave2.branch129.nonempty-connected-.context: Connected nonempty simple undirected graph by walks
form.wave2.branch129.nonempty-connected-.text: A nonempty simple undirected graph G=(V,E) is connected if for all u,v∈V there exists a finite walk from u to v, allowing the length-zero walk when u=v.

form.wave2.branch129.operator-eigenvalue.context: Eigenvalue of a K-linear endomorphism without finite-dimensionality assumption
form.wave2.branch129.operator-eigenvalue.text: For a K-vector space V and K-linear operator A:V→V, λ∈K is an eigenvalue of A if ker(A−λI_V)≠{0_V}, where I_V is the identity map of V.

form.wave2.branch129.operator-eigenvalue.context: Eigenvalue of a K-linear endomorphism without finite-dimensionality assumption
form.wave2.branch129.operator-eigenvalue.text: Equivalently, for such a K-linear endomorphism A, λ∈K is an eigenvalue exactly if some nonzero v∈V satisfies A(v)=λv.

form.wave2.branch129.real-convergent-egf.display_term: exponential generating function of a real sequence
form.wave2.branch129.real-convergent-egf.context: Analytic exponential generating function of a real sequence
form.wave2.branch129.real-convergent-egf.text: For a real sequence (a_n)_{n≥0}, let D={z∈ℝ:∑_{n=0}^∞(a_n/n!)z^n converges}. Its exponential generating function E_A:D→ℝ is E_A(z)=∑_{n=0}^∞(a_n/n!)z^n.

form.wave2.bridge136.convex-real.1.display_term: convex subset of a real vector space
form.wave2.bridge136.convex-real.1.context: Real-vector-space convex subset with equivalent two-point and Minkowski-set conditions
form.wave2.bridge136.convex-real.1.text: Let V be a vector space over ℝ and C⊆V. The subset C is convex if for every x,y∈C and t∈[0,1], the vector tx+(1−t)y belongs to C.

form.wave2.bridge136.convex-real.2.display_term: convex subset of a real vector space
form.wave2.bridge136.convex-real.2.context: Real-vector-space convex subset with equivalent two-point and Minkowski-set conditions
form.wave2.bridge136.convex-real.2.text: For a real vector space V and C⊆V, C is convex if tC+(1−t)C⊆C for every t∈[0,1], where tC+(1−t)C={tx+(1−t)y:x,y∈C}.

form.wave2.bridge136.falling-real-nonneg.display_term: falling factorial of a real number
form.wave2.bridge136.falling-real-nonneg.context: Real falling factorial x under nonnegative index, zero as empty product
form.wave2.bridge136.falling-real-nonneg.text: For x∈ℝ and n∈ℕ₀, define x^{\underline n}=∏_{j=0}^{n−1}(x−j), with the empty-product convention x^{\underline 0}=1. Thus for n≥1 it equals x(x−1)⋯(x−n+1).

form.wave2.bridge136.numeric-delta.1.display_term: numeric Kronecker delta on a set
form.wave2.bridge136.numeric-delta.1.context: Numeric Kronecker delta as equality indicator on any set
form.wave2.bridge136.numeric-delta.1.text: For any set Γ, the numerical Kronecker delta is δ:Γ×Γ→{0,1} defined by δ(a,b)=1 when a=b and δ(a,b)=0 when a≠b.

form.wave2.bridge136.numeric-delta.2.display_term: numeric Kronecker delta on a set
form.wave2.bridge136.numeric-delta.2.context: Numeric Kronecker delta as equality indicator on any set
form.wave2.bridge136.numeric-delta.2.text: For a,b∈Γ, the numerical Kronecker delta satisfies δ(a,b)=[a=b], where the Iverson indicator is 1 if the statement a=b is true and 0 otherwise.

form.wave2.bridge136.simple-bipartite.1.context: Simple undirected bipartite graph by two-part cover or proper non-surjective two-coloring
form.wave2.bridge136.simple-bipartite.1.text: A simple undirected graph G=(V,E) is bipartite if there are disjoint subsets A,B⊆V with A∪B=V and every edge {u,v}∈E has one endpoint in A and the other in B; either part may be empty.

form.wave2.bridge136.simple-bipartite.2.context: Simple undirected bipartite graph by two-part cover or proper non-surjective two-coloring
form.wave2.bridge136.simple-bipartite.2.text: A simple undirected graph G=(V,E) is bipartite if there exists a function c:V→{0,1} such that c(u)≠c(v) for every edge {u,v}∈E; surjectivity of c is not required.

form.wave2.broad67.compact-open-cover.context: General topology: compactness by finite open subcovers or closed-set finite intersection property; no Hausdorff assumption
form.wave2.broad67.compact-open-cover.text: A topological space X is compact if every open cover of X contains a finite subfamily whose union is X.

form.wave2.broad67.compact-closed-fip.context: General topology: compactness by finite open subcovers or closed-set finite intersection property; no Hausdorff assumption
form.wave2.broad67.compact-closed-fip.text: Equivalently, X is compact if every nonempty family of closed subsets of X that has the finite intersection property has nonempty total intersection.

form.wave2.conv126.eigenvector-linear-op.context: Nonzero eigenvector of a K-linear endomorphism for its eigenvalue
form.wave2.conv126.eigenvector-linear-op.text: Let K be a field, V a K-vector space, A:V→V a K-linear operator and λ∈K an eigenvalue of A. A vector v∈V is an eigenvector for λ when v≠0 and A(v)=λv.

form.wave2.conv126.eigenvector-linear-op.context: Nonzero eigenvector of a K-linear endomorphism for its eigenvalue
form.wave2.conv126.eigenvector-linear-op.text: Under the same K-linear operator A:V→V and eigenvalue λ∈K, v is a corresponding eigenvector if v≠0 and v∈ker(A−λI_V), where I_V is the identity map of V.

form.wave2.conv126.locally-uniform-metri.context: Locally uniform convergence on topological source to metric target
form.wave2.conv126.locally-uniform-metri.text: Let X be a topological space, (M,d) a metric space and f_n,f:X→M. The sequence f_n converges locally uniformly to f if each x∈X has a neighborhood U_x⊆X on which f_n|U_x converges uniformly to f|U_x.

form.wave2.conv126.pointwise-real.context: Pointwise convergence on a real-function domain, point-dependent cutoff
form.wave2.conv126.pointwise-real.text: Let D⊆ℝ and f_n,f:D→ℝ. The sequence f_n converges pointwise to f on D if for every x∈D and ε>0 there is N_x,ε∈ℕ such that for all n≥N_x,ε, |f_n(x)−f(x)|<ε.

form.wave2.conv126.pointwise-topological.context: Pointwise convergence to map into arbitrary topological target via product topology
form.wave2.conv126.pointwise-topological.text: For a set D, a topological space T, functions f_n,f:D→T, the sequence f_n converges pointwise to f if and only if it converges to f as a sequence of elements of the product space T^D with its product topology.

form.wave2.conv126.uniform-metric.context: Uniform convergence on a set to metric-valued function, one cutoff for all inputs
form.wave2.conv126.uniform-metric.text: Let S be a set, (M,d) a metric space and f_n,f:S→M. The sequence f_n converges uniformly to f on S if for every ε>0 there exists N_ε∈ℕ such that for all n≥N_ε and all x∈S, d(f_n(x),f(x))<ε.

form.wave2.conv126.uniform-real.context: Uniform convergence of real-valued functions on real domain
form.wave2.conv126.uniform-real.text: Let D⊆ℝ and f_n,f:D→ℝ. The sequence f_n converges uniformly to f if for each ε>0 there is N_ε∈ℕ such that every n≥N_ε and every x∈D satisfy |f_n(x)−f(x)|<ε.

form.wave2.cross104.independent-rv-count.context: Mutual independence of a sequence of measurable-space-valued random variables
form.wave2.cross104.independent-rv-count.text: Let (Ω,F,P) be a probability space, (S,Σ_S) a measurable target space, and X_n:Ω→S measurable for each n. The sequence (X_n) is mutually independent if the σ-algebras σ(X_n)={X_n⁻¹(B):B∈Σ_S} form a mutually independent sequence of sub-σ-algebras of F.

form.wave2.cross104.independent-sigma-co.context: Mutual independence of a countably indexed family of sub-sigma-algebras
form.wave2.cross104.independent-sigma-co.text: For (Ω,F,P) and a sequence (G_n) of sub-σ-algebras of F, the sequence is mutually independent if for every finite set of distinct indices i₁,…,i_m (m≥1) and every A_j∈G_{i_j}, P(⋂_{j=1}^m A_j)=∏_{j=1}^m P(A_j).

form.wave2.cross104.independent-sigma-pa.text: For a probability space (Ω,F,P) and sub-σ-algebras G₁,G₂⊆F, the pair is independent if P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B) for every A∈G₁ and B∈G₂.

form.wave2.cross104.lipschitz-at-point-a.context: Lipschitz bound anchored at one point, not neighborhood-local Lipschitz
form.wave2.cross104.lipschitz-at-point-a.text: For a∈X and f:(X,d_X)→(Y,d_Y), the source's Lipschitz-at-a condition is the existence of L≥0 such that d_Y(f(x),f(a))≤L d_X(x,a) for every x∈X; only one input is fixed at a.

form.wave2.cross104.lipschitz-global.context: Globally Lipschitz mapping of metric spaces
form.wave2.cross104.lipschitz-global.text: Let (X,d_X) and (Y,d_Y) be metric spaces and f:X→Y. The map f is globally Lipschitz on X if there exists L≥0 such that d_Y(f(x),f(y))≤L d_X(x,y) for every x,y∈X.

form.wave2.cross104.tree-unrooted.1.context: Unrooted simple connected graph with no circuits or cycles
form.wave2.cross104.tree-unrooted.1.text: An (unrooted) tree is a simple connected graph that contains no circuits (nontrivial closed edge-trails).

form.wave2.cross104.tree-unrooted.2.context: Unrooted simple connected graph with no circuits or cycles
form.wave2.cross104.tree-unrooted.2.text: Equivalently, an (unrooted) tree is a simple connected graph containing no cycles.

form.wave2.cross107.derivative-function-.display_term: derivative function on open real interval
form.wave2.cross107.derivative-function-.context: Derivative as a real-valued function on an open interval, not a single point value
form.wave2.cross107.derivative-function-.text: Let I⊆ℝ be an open interval and f:I→ℝ differentiable at each x∈I. Its derivative function f′:I→ℝ is defined by f′(x)=lim_{h→0, h≠0}(f(x+h)−f(x))/h, with x+h∈I.

form.wave2.cross107.field-vector-linear-.context: Kernel or null space of a linear map between vector spaces over a common field
form.wave2.cross107.field-vector-linear-.text: For vector spaces V,W over a common field K and a K-linear transformation T:V→W, its kernel (null space) is ker T={v∈V:T(v)=0_W}=T⁻¹({0_W}), the preimage of the zero vector in W.

form.wave2.cross107.module-linear-kernel.context: Kernel of a linear map between left R-modules
form.wave2.cross107.module-linear-kernel.text: Let φ:M→N be an R-linear map between left R-modules over the same associative ring R. The kernel is ker φ=φ⁻¹({0_N})={m∈M:φ(m)=0_N}, where 0_N is the identity of the additive group of N.

form.wave2.cross107.topological-boundary.display_term: boundary of a subset in a topological space
form.wave2.cross107.topological-boundary.context: Boundary of a subset relative to a specified topological ambient space
form.wave2.cross107.topological-boundary.text: For a subset A of a topological space X, its boundary is ∂_X A=cl_X(A)\int_X(A), the points in the closure of A that are not interior to A.

form.wave2.cross107.topological-boundary.display_term: boundary of a subset in a topological space
form.wave2.cross107.topological-boundary.context: Boundary of a subset relative to a specified topological ambient space
form.wave2.cross107.topological-boundary.text: Equivalently, for A⊆X in a topological space, the boundary is ∂_X A=cl_X(A)∩cl_X(X\A), where X\A is the complement relative to the given ambient X.

form.wave2.cross107.topological-closure..display_term: closure of a subset in a topological space
form.wave2.cross107.topological-closure..context: Closure of a subset in an arbitrary topological space
form.wave2.cross107.topological-closure..text: For a topological space (X,τ) and A⊆X, the closure cl_X(A) is the intersection of all τ-closed subsets F⊆X that contain A: cl_X(A)=⋂{F⊆X:A⊆F and X\F∈τ}.

form.wave2.cross107.topological-closure..display_term: closure of a subset in a topological space
form.wave2.cross107.topological-closure..context: Closure of a subset in an arbitrary topological space
form.wave2.cross107.topological-closure..text: For a subset A of a topological space X, its closure cl_X(A) is the smallest closed subset of X containing A (equivalently, the unique least element under inclusion of the family of closed supersets of A).

form.wave2.cross110.field-vector-linear.context: Linear transformation of vector spaces over one field
form.wave2.cross110.field-vector-linear.text: Let V,W be vector spaces over the same field K. A map T:V→W is K-linear when T(av+w)=aT(v)+T(w) for every a∈K and v,w∈V.

form.wave2.cross110.finite-image-rank.context: Finite rank of field-vector-space linear transformation
form.wave2.cross110.finite-image-rank.text: For a K-linear transformation T:V→W between vector spaces over the same field K, if im(T) is finite-dimensional, its rank is rank(T)=dim_K(im(T)), a finite nonnegative integer.

form.wave2.cross110.image-of-mapping.1.context: Set-theoretic full image of a total mapping
form.wave2.cross110.image-of-mapping.1.text: For a total map f:S→T, the image im(f) is {t∈T:there exists s∈S with f(s)=t}, the set of values actually attained by f.

form.wave2.cross110.image-of-mapping.2.context: Set-theoretic full image of a total mapping
form.wave2.cross110.image-of-mapping.2.text: Equivalently, for a total map f:S→T the image is f[S]={f(s):s∈S}, the direct image of the entire domain S.

form.wave2.cross110.module-linear.text: Let R be an associative ring and M,N left R-modules. A map T:M→N is R-linear if T(m+m′)=T(m)+T(m′) for all m,m′∈M and T(rm)=rT(m) for every r∈R,m∈M.

form.wave2.cross110.sequence-accumulatio.context: Accumulation point of an indexed topological sequence
form.wave2.cross110.sequence-accumulatio.text: For a sequence (x_n) indexed by n∈ℕ in a topological space (X,τ), a point x∈X is a sequence accumulation point if for every open U∈τ containing x, the index set {n∈ℕ:x_n∈U} is infinite.

form.wave2.cross110.set-accumulation.context: Derived-set accumulation point of a subset in a topological space
form.wave2.cross110.set-accumulation.text: For A⊆X in a topological space X and x∈X, x is an accumulation point of A if x∈cl_X(A\{x}); equivalently every open neighborhood of x meets A at some point other than x.

form.wave2.cross133.bell-number.context: Bell number B_n counts all partitions of n-element sets including n=0
form.wave2.cross133.bell-number.text: For n∈ℕ₀, the Bell number B_n is the number of distinct partitions of any set S with |S|=n into nonempty pairwise disjoint blocks whose union is S; in particular B_0=1.

form.wave2.cross133.convex-hull-real.1.display_term: convex hull of a subset of a real vector space
form.wave2.cross133.convex-hull-real.1.context: Convex hull in a real vector space, finite combinations and least convex superset
form.wave2.cross133.convex-hull-real.1.text: For a real vector space V and U⊆V, conv(U) is the set of sums ∑_{j=1}^m λ_j u_j with m≥1, u_j∈U, λ_j>0 for all j, and ∑_{j=1}^m λ_j=1; conv(∅)=∅.

form.wave2.cross133.convex-hull-real.2.display_term: convex hull of a subset of a real vector space
form.wave2.cross133.convex-hull-real.2.context: Convex hull in a real vector space, finite combinations and least convex superset
form.wave2.cross133.convex-hull-real.2.text: For a real vector space V and U⊆V, conv(U)=⋂{C⊆V:C is convex and U⊆C}, the intersection of every convex subset containing U.

form.wave2.cross133.convex-hull-real.3.display_term: convex hull of a subset of a real vector space
form.wave2.cross133.convex-hull-real.3.context: Convex hull in a real vector space, finite combinations and least convex superset
form.wave2.cross133.convex-hull-real.3.text: For a real vector space V and U⊆V, conv(U) is the unique least (by inclusion) convex subset C⊆V with U⊆C; every convex D containing U contains C.

form.wave2.cross133.stirling-second-kind.display_term: Stirling numbers of the second kind
form.wave2.cross133.stirling-second-kind.context: Second-kind Stirling numbers by recurrence and falling factorial polynomial coefficients
form.wave2.cross133.stirling-second-kind.text: For n,k∈ℕ₀, the Stirling numbers of the second kind S(n,k) satisfy S(n,0)=δ_{n,0}, S(0,k)=δ_{0,k}, and for n,k≥1, S(n,k)=S(n−1,k−1)+k S(n−1,k), where δ is Kronecker's delta.

form.wave2.cross133.stirling-second-kind.display_term: Stirling numbers of the second kind
form.wave2.cross133.stirling-second-kind.context: Second-kind Stirling numbers by recurrence and falling factorial polynomial coefficients
form.wave2.cross133.stirling-second-kind.text: For each n∈ℕ₀, the Stirling numbers S(n,k) are the unique coefficients in the polynomial identity x^n=∑_{k=0}^n S(n,k)x^{\underline{k}}, where x^{\underline{0}}=1 and x^{\underline{k}}=x(x−1)⋯(x−k+1) for k≥1.

form.wave2.cross133.vertex-degree-simple.display_term: degree of a vertex in a simple undirected graph
form.wave2.cross133.vertex-degree-simple.context: Degree of vertex in loopless simple undirected graph, incidence and neighbor counts
form.wave2.cross133.vertex-degree-simple.text: For a simple undirected graph G=(V,E) and v∈V, deg_G(v) is the cardinality of the set {e∈E:v∈e} of edges incident to v.

form.wave2.cross133.vertex-degree-simple.display_term: degree of a vertex in a simple undirected graph
form.wave2.cross133.vertex-degree-simple.context: Degree of vertex in loopless simple undirected graph, incidence and neighbor counts
form.wave2.cross133.vertex-degree-simple.text: For a simple undirected graph G=(V,E) and v∈V, deg_G(v)=|{u∈V:{u,v}∈E}|, the number or cardinality of distinct vertices adjacent to v.

form.wave2.directional113.closed-metric.context: Closed ball in a metric space with positive radius
form.wave2.directional113.closed-metric.text: For a metric space (X,d), a center a∈X and a radius r>0, the closed metric ball is C_d(a,r)={x∈X:d(x,a)≤r}.

form.wave2.directional113.closed-norm.context: Closed ball in a normed vector space with positive radius
form.wave2.directional113.closed-norm.text: For a normed vector space (V,∥·∥), center a∈V and radius r>0, the closed norm ball is C(a,r)={v∈V:∥v−a∥≤r}.

form.wave2.directional113.directional-di.context: Directional derivative of a differentiable function in Euclidean space
form.wave2.directional113.directional-di.text: Let f:ℝⁿ→ℝ be differentiable at a∈ℝⁿ and let u∈ℝⁿ be a unit vector. The directional derivative in direction u is D_u f(a)=lim_{t→0,t≠0}[f(a+tu)−f(a)]/t.

form.wave2.directional113.homeomorphism-.text: For topological spaces X and Y, a map f:X→Y is a homeomorphism if f is bijective, f is continuous and its inverse map f⁻¹:Y→X is continuous.
Equivalently, a bijection f:X→Y between topological spaces is a homeomorphism if for every U⊆X, U is open in X exactly when f[U] is open in Y.

form.wave2.directional113.open-metric.context: Open ball in a metric space with positive radius
form.wave2.directional113.open-metric.text: For a metric space (X,d), a center a∈X and a radius r>0, the open metric ball is B_d(a,r)={x∈X:d(x,a)<r}.

form.wave2.directional113.open-norm.context: Open ball in a normed vector space with positive radius
form.wave2.directional113.open-norm.text: For a normed vector space (V,∥·∥), center a∈V and radius r>0, the open norm ball is B(a,r)={v∈V:∥v−a∥<r}.

form.wave2.found85.adapted-continuous.context: Real-time indexed stochastic process adapted to a filtration indexed by t≥0
form.wave2.found85.adapted-continuous.text: A real-valued process (X_t)_{t≥0} adapted to a filtration (F_t)_{t≥0} satisfies that X_t is F_t-measurable for every real t≥0.

form.wave2.found85.adapted-discrete.context: Discrete-time stochastic process adapted to a filtration indexed by n≥0
form.wave2.found85.adapted-discrete.text: A real-valued process (X_n)_{n≥0} adapted to a filtration (F_n)_{n≥0} satisfies that X_n is F_n-measurable for every nonnegative integer n.

form.wave2.found85.conditional-expectati.context: Conditional expectation with respect to a sub-sigma-algebra
form.wave2.found85.conditional-expectati.text: For an integrable real random variable X on (Ω,F,P) and a sub-σ-algebra G⊆F, a version of E[X|G] is an integrable G-measurable random variable Z satisfying ∫_A Z dP = ∫_A X dP for every A∈G.

form.wave2.found85.discrete-filtration.context: Discrete time: increasing sub-sigma-algebras indexed by n≥0
form.wave2.found85.discrete-filtration.text: For a measurable space (Ω,F), a discrete-time filtration is a family (F_n)_{n≥0} of sub-σ-algebras of F such that F_n⊆F_m whenever n≤m.

form.wave2.found85.proper-coloring.context: Proper vertex coloring of a simple undirected graph
form.wave2.found85.proper-coloring.text: A proper vertex k-coloring of a simple graph G=(V,E) is a map c:V→{1,…,k} such that c(u)≠c(v) for every edge {u,v}∈E.

form.wave2.found85.stochastic-process.context: General measurable-state-valued stochastic process indexed by a set
form.wave2.found85.stochastic-process.text: For a probability space (Ω,F,P), a measurable state space (E,Ecal), and an index set I, a stochastic process is an I-indexed family (X_i)_{i∈I} of E-valued random variables on Ω.

form.wave2.foundation.abelian-group.text: An abelian group is a group (G,*) for which a*b = b*a for every a,b∈G.

form.wave2.foundation.associative-ring-i.context: ProofWiki abstract ring convention: associative multiplication, no required multiplicative identity
form.wave2.foundation.associative-ring-i.text: An associative ring R is a set with operations + and · for which (R,+) is an abelian group, (R,·) is associative, and multiplication distributes over addition on both sides. A multiplicative identity is not part of this particular source's general ring axioms.

form.wave2.foundation.binary-operation-g.context: Two-input operation between potentially distinct sets
form.wave2.foundation.binary-operation-g.text: For sets S,T,U, a binary operation with input sets S and T and values in U is a function ⋆:S×T→U, assigning exactly one output in U to each ordered pair (s,t)∈S×T.

form.wave2.foundation.binary-operation-i.context: Internal binary operation closed on a set
form.wave2.foundation.binary-operation-i.text: An internal binary operation on a set S is a function ⋆:S×S→S, assigning to each pair (a,b)∈S×S a uniquely determined element a⋆b∈S.

form.wave2.foundation.binary-relation-su.context: Binary relation identified with its graph subset
form.wave2.foundation.binary-relation-su.text: Given sets S and T, a binary relation from S to T may instead mean a subset R⊆S×T. The relation holds between s∈S and t∈T exactly when (s,t) belongs to R.

form.wave2.foundation.binary-relation-ty.context: Typed relation with explicit domain and codomain
form.wave2.foundation.binary-relation-ty.text: A binary relation from a set S to a set T may be defined as an ordered triple (S,T,R), where R is a subset of S×T. For s∈S and t∈T, write sRt precisely when (s,t)∈R.

form.wave2.foundation.cartesian-product-.context: Set theory: Cartesian product of exactly two sets
form.wave2.foundation.cartesian-product-.text: For sets S and T, their Cartesian product is S×T = {(s,t) : s∈S and t∈T}, the set of all ordered pairs whose first entry belongs to S and whose second belongs to T.

form.wave2.foundation.category-functor.context: Stacks 4.2.8 ordinary strict covariant functor, not a weak pseudofunctor
form.wave2.foundation.category-functor.text: A covariant functor F:A→B between small categories assigns to every object x of A an object F(x) of B and to every arrow f:x→y an arrow F(f):F(x)→F(y). For composable arrows f,g it satisfies F(g∘f)=F(g)∘F(f), and F(id_x)=id_{F(x)}.

form.wave2.foundation.commutative-maxima.display_term: maximal ideal of a commutative unital ring
form.wave2.foundation.commutative-maxima.context: Commutative algebra: proper maximal ring ideal, not a general noncommutative maximal left or right ideal
form.wave2.foundation.commutative-maxima.text: Let R be a commutative ring with identity. An ideal m of R is maximal if m is properly contained in R and every ideal J with m⊆J⊆R satisfies J=m or J=R.

form.wave2.foundation.commutative-prime-.display_term: prime ideal of a commutative unital ring
form.wave2.foundation.commutative-prime-.context: Prime ideal in a commutative ring with multiplicative identity
form.wave2.foundation.commutative-prime-.text: Let R be a commutative ring with identity. An ideal P⊊R is prime if, for all a,b∈R, ab∈P implies a∈P or b∈P.

form.wave2.foundation.field-commutative-.context: Stacks 9.2.1 with Stacks 10.2 commutative-unital ring convention
form.wave2.foundation.field-commutative-.text: A field is a commutative ring k with identity 1_k, with 0≠1_k, such that for every a∈k with a≠0 there exists b∈k satisfying ab=1_k (and hence ba=1_k).

form.wave2.foundation.fixed-target-morph.display_term: indexed family of morphisms with fixed target
form.wave2.foundation.fixed-target-morph.context: Stacks Definition 7.6.1, set-indexed arrows with a common target and possible empty indexing set
form.wave2.foundation.fixed-target-morph.text: Let C be a small category and U an object of C. An indexed family of morphisms with fixed target U consists of a set I and, for every i∈I, an object U_i and a morphism f_i:U_i→U. The indexing set I may be empty; repeated arrows with different indices are still different family occurrences.

form.wave2.foundation.grothendieck-site-.context: Stacks Definition 7.6.2, category with distinguished covering families and base-change/refinement axioms
form.wave2.foundation.grothendieck-site-.text: A site in the Stacks covering-family convention is a small category C together with a set Cov(C) of indexed families of morphisms with fixed target, called covering families. Singleton families of isomorphisms are coverings; compositions/refinements of covering families are coverings; and coverings pull back along arrows with the necessary fiber products existing.

form.wave2.foundation.group.context: Abstract group, with a two-sided identity and inverses; arbitrary binary operation
form.wave2.foundation.group.text: A group is a set G with a binary operation *: G×G→G such that (a*b)*c = a*(b*c) for all a,b,c∈G, an element e∈G satisfies e*a = a = a*e for each a∈G, and every a∈G has b∈G with a*b = e = b*a.

form.wave2.foundation.integral-domain.context: Stacks commutative algebra: nonzero commutative ring with 1 and no nonzero zero divisors
form.wave2.foundation.integral-domain.text: An integral domain in the Stacks commutative-unital convention is a nonzero commutative ring R with identity 1_R in which ab=0 implies a=0 or b=0 for every a,b in R.

form.wave2.foundation.integral-over-idea.context: Stacks Definition 10.38.1: integrality over an ideal along a commutative ring homomorphism
