form.wave2.foundation.integral-over-idea.text: Let φ:R→S be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let I⊆R be an ideal. An element g∈S is integral over I if there are d≥1 and a monic polynomial P(T)=T^d+Σ_{j=0}^{d−1}a_jT^j, where a_j∈I^{d−j}, such that φ(P)(g)=0 in S.

form.wave2.foundation.left-module-nonuni.display_term: left module over a ring, optionally nonunital
form.wave2.foundation.left-module-nonuni.context: General left R-module over an associative ring; unitality a separate condition
form.wave2.foundation.left-module-nonuni.text: Let R be an associative ring and (M,+) an abelian group. A left R-module structure on M is an action R×M→M, (r,m)↦rm, satisfying r(m+n)=rm+rn, (r+s)m=rm+sm, and (rs)m=r(sm). When R has identity, a unital left module additionally satisfies 1_R m=m for all m∈M.

form.wave2.foundation.local-ring-fibre-a.display_term: local ring of a fibre at a prime
form.wave2.foundation.local-ring-fibre-a.context: Stacks Definition 10.112.5: local ring of fibre at prime q lying above prime p
form.wave2.foundation.local-ring-fibre-a.text: Let R→S be a homomorphism of commutative rings. For a prime ideal q⊆S with contraction p=q∩R, the local ring of the fibre at q is S_q/pS_q. Equivalently, it is the localization of the fibre ring S⊗_Rκ(p) at the prime corresponding to q.

form.wave2.foundation.mapping-bare-graph.context: Graph-only function convention relative to specified sets X,Y
form.wave2.foundation.mapping-bare-graph.text: With ambient sets X and Y fixed, a graph-only mapping can be represented by a subset G⊆X×Y such that, for every x∈X, there is exactly one y∈Y with (x,y)∈G. As bare data G need not determine the codomain Y uniquely.

form.wave2.foundation.mapping-element-as.context: Foundational mapping as total single-valued assignment X→Y
form.wave2.foundation.mapping-element-as.text: Given sets X and Y, a mapping f:X→Y assigns to every x∈X exactly one value f(x)∈Y. Equivalently, for each x∈X there exists a unique y∈Y that the assignment associates with x.

form.wave2.foundation.mapping-typed-grap.text: For sets X and Y, a mapping f:X→Y can be defined as a typed relation (X,Y,G) where G⊆X×Y and, for every x∈X, there exists exactly one y∈Y with (x,y)∈G. The graph is G; X and Y are part of the mapping data.

form.wave2.foundation.monoid.context: Algebra: associative internally closed operation with two-sided identity
form.wave2.foundation.monoid.text: A monoid is a pair (M,⋆) consisting of a set M and an operation ⋆:M×M→M for which (a⋆b)⋆c=a⋆(b⋆c) for all a,b,c∈M and some e∈M satisfies e⋆a=a=a⋆e for every a∈M.

form.wave2.foundation.nonnegative-measur.context: Measure theory: extended nonnegative countably additive set function on a sigma-algebra
form.wave2.foundation.nonnegative-measur.text: Let Σ be a sigma-algebra of subsets of X. A nonnegative measure on (X,Σ) is a function μ:Σ→[0,+∞] with μ(∅)=0 and μ(⋃_{n≥1}E_n)=∑_{n≥1}μ(E_n) for every sequence (E_n) of pairwise disjoint sets in Σ.

form.wave2.foundation.nonzero-polynomial.display_term: degree of a nonzero univariate polynomial
form.wave2.foundation.nonzero-polynomial.context: Formal algebra: nonzero polynomial in R[X] over a commutative unital ring
form.wave2.foundation.nonzero-polynomial.text: Let R be a commutative ring with multiplicative identity and let P=∑_{k=0}^n a_kX^k∈R[X] be nonzero. Its degree deg(P) is the greatest integer k≥0 for which a_k≠0_R. This definition does not assign a finite degree to the zero polynomial.

form.wave2.foundation.ordered-pair-kurat.context: Set theory: Kuratowski realization with coordinatewise equality
form.wave2.foundation.ordered-pair-kurat.text: For arbitrary sets a and b, the Kuratowski ordered pair is (a,b):={{a},{a,b}}. This set-theoretic construction has the defining property (a,b)=(c,d) if and only if a=c and b=d.

form.wave2.foundation.orthogonality-meas.display_term: nth raw moment of an orthogonality measure
form.wave2.foundation.orthogonality-meas.context: DLMF orthogonal-polynomial analysis: raw power moment with respect to a positive measure
form.wave2.foundation.orthogonality-meas.text: Let μ be a nonnegative Borel or Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure on a real interval (a,b) and let n be a nonnegative integer such that x↦x^n is μ-integrable. The nth raw moment of μ is μ_n=∫_a^b x^n dμ(x). It is finite only when the integral is finite.

form.wave2.foundation.pseudofunctor-to-s.context: Stacks Definition 4.29.5: ordinary source category and strict 2-category target, with invertible comparison 2-cells
form.wave2.foundation.pseudofunctor-to-s.text: A pseudofunctor P:A→C from an ordinary category A to a strict 2-category C assigns objects P(x) and 1-morphisms P(f), invertible comparison 2-cells η_x:id_{P(x)}⇒P(id_x) and κ_{g,f}:P(g∘f)⇒P(g)∘P(f), and satisfies the unit identities κ_{id_y,f}=η_y⋆id_{P(f)}, κ_{f,id_x}=id_{P(f)}⋆η_x and the associativity coherence (id_{P(h)}⋆κ_{g,f})∘κ_{h,g∘f}=(κ_{h,g}⋆id_{P(f)})∘κ_{h∘g,f} for composable f,g,h.

form.wave2.foundation.reduced-ring.context: Algebra: associative ring, not necessarily unital, with no nonzero nilpotent elements
form.wave2.foundation.reduced-ring.text: An associative ring R is reduced if for every r∈R and every positive integer n, the equality r^n=0 implies r=0. Equivalently, its only nilpotent element is zero.

form.wave2.foundation.regular-noetherian.context: Noetherian commutative regular rings defined through regular localizations
form.wave2.foundation.regular-noetherian.text: A Noetherian commutative ring R is regular if R_p is a regular local ring for every prime ideal p of R.

form.wave2.foundation.ring-map-general.context: Additive/multiplicative homomorphism between associative rings; no required preservation of unity
form.wave2.foundation.ring-map-general.text: A ring homomorphism φ:R→S between associative rings is a mapping satisfying φ(a+b)=φ(a)+φ(b) and φ(ab)=φ(a)φ(b) for all a,b∈R. If both rings carry identity elements, this definition alone does not require φ(1_R)=1_S.

form.wave2.foundation.ring-map-unital.context: Unital ring homomorphism, with preservation of multiplicative identities
form.wave2.foundation.ring-map-unital.text: For rings R and S with specified identities, a unital ring homomorphism φ:R→S is an additive and multiplicative homomorphism additionally satisfying φ(1_R)=1_S.

form.wave2.foundation.sigma-algebra.context: Measure theory: family of subsets closed under relative complements and countable unions
form.wave2.foundation.sigma-algebra.text: Let X be a set. A sigma-algebra on X is a family Σ⊆P(X) containing X, closed under taking complements X\A for A∈Σ, and closed under countable unions ⋃_{n≥1}A_n of members A_n∈Σ.

form.wave2.broad67.sigma-difference-disj.context: Measure theory: family of subsets closed under relative complements and countable unions
form.wave2.broad67.sigma-difference-disj.text: Equivalently, a family Σ⊆P(X) is a σ-algebra if X∈Σ, it is closed under differences A\B for A,B∈Σ, and it is closed under countable unions of pairwise disjoint members.

form.wave2.foundation.small-category.context: Stacks Project Definition 4.2.1: categories with a set of objects and a set of morphisms for each ordered pair
form.wave2.foundation.small-category.text: A small category C has a set Ob(C) of objects, sets Hom_C(x,y) for every ordered pair of objects, composition maps Hom_C(y,z)×Hom_C(x,y)→Hom_C(x,z), and arrows id_x∈Hom_C(x,x); compositions are associative and identities act as left and right units.

form.wave2.foundation.small-groupoid.context: Stacks 4.2.5, a small category in which every arrow is an isomorphism
form.wave2.foundation.small-groupoid.text: A groupoid is a small category G such that for every morphism f:x→y there is a morphism g:y→x with g∘f=id_x and f∘g=id_y.

form.wave2.foundation.strongly-transcend.display_term: strongly transcendental element over a subring
form.wave2.foundation.strongly-transcend.context: Stacks 10.123.7: strong transcendence under a commutative ring inclusion, with annihilators and potential zero divisors
form.wave2.foundation.strongly-transcend.text: Let R⊆S be an inclusion of commutative rings with identity, and let x∈S. The element x is strongly transcendental over R if for every integer n≥0, coefficients a_0,…,a_n∈R, and u∈S, the equation u(a_0+a_1x+⋯+a_nx^n)=0 implies ua_i=0 for every i=0,…,n.

form.wave2.foundation.subset-nonstrict.context: Set theory: non-strict subset relation for sets
form.wave2.foundation.subset-nonstrict.text: For sets A and B, A is a subset of B, written A⊆B, if and only if for every x, x∈A implies x∈B. Equality A=B is allowed in this non-strict inclusion relation.

form.wave2.foundation.subset-proper.context: Set theory: strict set inclusion requiring inequality
form.wave2.foundation.subset-proper.text: For sets A and B, A is a proper subset of B, written A⊊B, if and only if A⊆B and A≠B. Equivalently, every member of A belongs to B and at least one member of B does not belong to A.

form.wave2.foundation.subspace-topology-.context: General topological subspace including the empty subset when allowed
form.wave2.foundation.subspace-topology-.text: For a topological space (X,τ) and any subset A⊆X, the subspace topology on A is τ_A={A∩U:U∈τ}; the pair (A,τ_A) is the resulting topological subspace. This includes A=∅.
If a topological-space convention requires nonempty spaces, a topological subspace of (X,τ) is a nonempty subset A⊆X equipped with τ_A={A∩U:U∈τ}. Empty A is excluded only by this source convention.

form.wave2.foundation.tagged-riemann-int.display_term: proper Riemann integral on a compact interval
form.wave2.foundation.tagged-riemann-int.context: Classical real analysis: universal sufficiently fine tagged partition integral
form.wave2.foundation.tagged-riemann-int.text: Let f:[a,b]→R be bounded with a<b. For a finite partition a=x_0<⋯<x_n=b and arbitrary tags ξ_i∈[x_{i−1},x_i], let S=Σ_{i=1}^n f(ξ_i)(x_i−x_{i−1}) and mesh=max_i(x_i−x_{i−1}). The function f is Riemann integrable on [a,b] with integral L∈R if for every ε>0 there exists δ>0 such that |S−L|<ε for every tagged partition with mesh<δ.

form.wave2.foundation.topological-space.context: Open-set axioms for arbitrary topological spaces, including the empty space
form.wave2.foundation.topological-space.text: A topological space is a pair (X,τ) with τ⊆P(X) such that ∅∈τ and X∈τ, any union of members of τ is in τ, and intersections of finitely many members of τ are in τ. Members of τ are the open subsets of X.

form.wave2.foundation.two-sided-ideal.context: Two-sided ring ideal; multiplication need not be commutative
form.wave2.foundation.two-sided-ideal.text: Let R be a ring. A subset I⊆R is a two-sided ideal if (I,+) is an additive subgroup of (R,+) and, for every r∈R and i∈I, both ri and ir belong to I.

form.wave2.foundation.uniformizer-dvr.display_term: uniformizer of a discrete valuation ring
form.wave2.foundation.uniformizer-dvr.context: Commutative algebra, Stacks 10.119.8: generator of maximal ideal of discrete valuation ring
form.wave2.foundation.uniformizer-dvr.text: Let A be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal m. An element π∈A is a uniformizer of A if the principal ideal (π) generated by π equals m.

form.wave2.foundation.unit-of-ring.context: Associative ring with 1: two-sided multiplicative invertibility; distinct from the unity 1_R
form.wave2.foundation.unit-of-ring.text: Let R be an associative ring with identity 1_R. An element u in R is a unit if there exists v in R such that uv=1_R=vu. The identity is required, but u itself need not equal 1_R.

form.wave2.foundation.well-ordered-set.context: Order theory: total order with a least element in every nonempty subset
form.wave2.foundation.well-ordered-set.text: A well-ordered set is a pair (S,≤) in which ≤ is a total order and every nonempty subset A⊆S has a least element: there exists a∈A such that a≤x for all x∈A.

form.wave2.foundation13.abelian-group-ho.context: Concrete additive subgroup kernel of a homomorphism of abelian groups
form.wave2.foundation13.abelian-group-ho.text: Given a group homomorphism f:A→B of abelian groups (written additively), its kernel is ker(f)={a∈A : f(a)=0_B}, an additive subgroup of A. The canonical inclusion ker(f)→A makes this subgroup the usual kernel object in the category of abelian groups.

form.wave2.foundation13.exact-sequence-a.context: Complex exact at interior objects of an abelian category, where images and kernels exist
form.wave2.foundation13.exact-sequence-a.text: A sequence of arrows in an additive category is a complex when each consecutive composite is zero. When the category is abelian, a complex X→Y→Z is exact at Y if im(X→Y)=ker(Y→Z) as subobjects of Y. An exact complex is exact at every applicable position; a short exact sequence has form 0→A→B→C→0.

form.wave2.foundation13.preadditive-cate.context: Universal-property cokernel of a morphism in a preadditive category, existence conditional
form.wave2.foundation13.preadditive-cate.text: For a morphism f:X→Y in a preadditive category, a cokernel is a morphism p:Y→C satisfying p∘f=0, such that for every q:Y→Z with q∘f=0 there is exactly one h:C→Z with q=h∘p. A cokernel is asserted only when such a universal morphism exists.

form.wave2.foundation13.preadditive-cate.context: Universal-property kernel of a morphism in a preadditive category, existence conditional
form.wave2.foundation13.preadditive-cate.text: For a morphism f:X→Y in a preadditive category, a kernel is a morphism i:K→X satisfying f∘i=0, such that for every j:Z→X with f∘j=0 there is exactly one h:Z→K with j=i∘h. A kernel is asserted only when such a universal morphism exists.

form.wave2.foundation15.abelian-category.context: Stacks Definition 12.5.1: additive category with kernels, cokernels, and coimage-image isomorphisms
form.wave2.foundation15.abelian-category.text: An abelian category C is an additive category in which every morphism f has a kernel and a cokernel and, for every such f, the canonical comparison morphism Coim(f)→Im(f) is an isomorphism.

form.wave2.foundation15.additive-categor.context: Stacks Definition 12.3.8: preadditive category with all finite products
form.wave2.foundation15.additive-categor.text: An additive category C is a preadditive category in which all finite products exist, including an empty product. Equivalently in a preadditive category, it has a zero object and finite direct sums.

form.wave2.foundation15.preadditive-cate.context: Stacks Definition 12.3.1: abelian-group hom-sets and bilinear composition
form.wave2.foundation15.preadditive-cate.text: A preadditive category C is a category such that for every pair of objects X,Y the morphism set Hom_C(X,Y) is an abelian group, and composition Hom_C(Y,Z)×Hom_C(X,Y)→Hom_C(X,Z) is bilinear in its two morphism variables.

form.wave2.foundation76.continuous-topol.context: Mapping between topological spaces, equivalent global and pointwise forms
form.wave2.foundation76.continuous-topol.text: A map f:X→Y between topological spaces is continuous when, for every open subset V⊆Y, the inverse image f^{-1}(V) is open in X.

form.wave2.foundation76.continuous-topol.context: Mapping between topological spaces, equivalent global and pointwise forms
form.wave2.foundation76.continuous-topol.text: A map f:X→Y is continuous when for each x∈X and each open neighborhood V of f(x) in Y there exists an open neighborhood U of x in X such that f(U)⊆V.

form.wave2.foundation76.discrete-topolog.context: Topology P(S) on a nonempty set S (source scope)
form.wave2.foundation76.discrete-topolog.text: For a nonempty set S, the discrete topology is τ=P(S), the family of every subset of S; thus every subset is open in the resulting topological space (S,τ).

form.wave2.foundation76.noetherian-modul.context: Modules over commutative unital rings; equivalent finiteness axioms
form.wave2.foundation76.noetherian-modul.text: A module M over a commutative ring A with identity is Noetherian when every A-submodule of M is finitely generated.

form.wave2.foundation76.noetherian-modul.context: Modules over commutative unital rings; equivalent finiteness axioms
form.wave2.foundation76.noetherian-modul.text: A module M over a commutative unital ring A is Noetherian when every ascending sequence M_1⊆M_2⊆⋯ of A-submodules becomes constant from some index onward.

form.wave2.foundation76.noetherian-modul.context: Modules over commutative unital rings; equivalent finiteness axioms
form.wave2.foundation76.noetherian-modul.text: A module M over a commutative unital ring A is Noetherian when every nonempty collection of its A-submodules has an inclusion-maximal member.

form.wave2.foundation76.submodule.01.context: R-linear subgroup of a module stable under scalar multiplication
form.wave2.foundation76.submodule.01.text: For a left R-module M, a subset N⊆M is a submodule when N is an additive subgroup of M and rn∈N for every r∈R and n∈N, with the addition and scalar multiplication restricted from M.

form.wave2.graph42.loopless-undirected-m.context: Multiset of unordered vertex doubletons allows parallel undirected edges but no loops; does not demand finite vertices
form.wave2.graph42.loopless-undirected-m.text: A loopless undirected multigraph is a pair G=(V,E), where V is a set of vertices and E is a multiset of two-element subsets of V. Two copies of {u,v} represent parallel edges joining u and v; the graph is simple exactly when each edge multiplicity is at most one.

form.wave2.graph42.simple-undirected.context: Set-based undirected graph with edges as two-element vertex subsets, no loops or parallel edges, finite and infinite V allowed
form.wave2.graph42.simple-undirected.text: A simple undirected graph is a pair G=(V,E), where V is a set of vertices and E⊆{e⊆V:|e|=2}. Thus each edge {u,v} has distinct vertices u≠v, has no direction, and occurs at most once.

form.wave2.group116.group-orbit.1.display_term: orbit of an element under a group action
form.wave2.group116.group-orbit.1.context: Orbit of an element under a left group action
form.wave2.group116.group-orbit.1.text: Let G be a group acting on a set X on the left and x∈X. The orbit of x is G·x={g·x:g∈G}={y∈X:there exists g∈G with y=g·x}.

form.wave2.group116.group-orbit.2.display_term: orbit of an element under a group action
form.wave2.group116.group-orbit.2.context: Orbit of an element under a left group action
form.wave2.group116.group-orbit.2.text: For a left G-action on X, define x∼_G y when some g∈G satisfies y=g·x. The orbit of x is its equivalence class [x] under this action-induced equivalence relation.

form.wave2.group116.group-stabilizer.display_term: stabilizer of an element under a group action
form.wave2.group116.group-stabilizer.context: Point stabilizer of a specified left group action
form.wave2.group116.group-stabilizer.text: Let G act on X on the left and x∈X. The stabilizer of x in G is Stab_G(x)={g∈G:g·x=x}, the set of all elements of G fixing x under the given action.

form.wave2.group116.measure-pushforward.context: Pushforward of a nonnegative measure by a measurable map
form.wave2.group116.measure-pushforward.text: Let (X,Σ) and (Y,Τ) be measurable spaces, μ:Σ→[0,+∞] a measure, and f:X→Y a (Σ,Τ)-measurable map. The pushforward measure f_*μ on (Y,Τ) is defined for every B∈Τ by (f_*μ)(B)=μ(f⁻¹(B)).

form.wave2.group116.set-partition.1.context: Partition into nonempty disjoint blocks, arbitrary base set
form.wave2.group116.set-partition.1.text: For a set S, a partition P is a collection of nonempty subsets B⊆S such that ⋃_{B∈P}B=S and B∩C=∅ whenever B,C∈P are distinct.

form.wave2.group116.set-partition.2.context: Partition into nonempty disjoint blocks, arbitrary base set
form.wave2.group116.set-partition.2.text: Equivalently, a partition P of S is a collection of nonempty subsets of S such that for each s∈S there exists exactly one B∈P with s∈B.

form.wave2.integer59.fraction-field-inte.display_term: fraction field of an integral domain
form.wave2.integer59.fraction-field-inte.context: Integral-domain fraction field: concrete fraction-equivalence construction
form.wave2.integer59.fraction-field-inte.text: For a commutative integral domain D, the fraction field Frac(D) is constructed from pairs (a,b) with a∈D and 0≠b∈D, where (a,b)∼(c,d) iff ad=bc. The class of (a,b) is written a/b; addition and multiplication are defined on such classes so that D embeds into the resulting field.

form.wave2.integer59.fraction-field-univ.display_term: fraction field of an integral domain
form.wave2.integer59.fraction-field-univ.context: Integral-domain fraction field: concrete fraction-equivalence construction
form.wave2.integer59.fraction-field-univ.text: Equivalently, a fraction field of an integral domain D is a field F with an injective ring map i:D→F satisfying: for every field K and injective ring map j:D→K, there exists a unique field homomorphism h:F→K for which h∘i=j.

form.wave2.integer59.integer-equivalence.text: An integer is an equivalence class [a,b] of pairs of natural numbers, where (a,b)∼(c,d) exactly when a+d=b+c. The integers may be realized as the quotient set (N×N)/∼, with [a,b] understood as the formal difference of a and b.

form.wave2.integer59.integer-ring.context: Algebraic integer ring Z under its usual addition and multiplication
form.wave2.integer59.integer-ring.text: The ring of integers is the structure (Z,+,·) formed by the set of integers together with integer addition and integer multiplication.

form.wave2.module94.right-module-nonunit.context: General right R-module over an associative ring, unity not demanded
form.wave2.module94.right-module-nonunit.text: Let R be an associative ring and (M,+) an abelian group. A right R-module structure on M is a scalar action M×R→M, (m,r)↦mr, such that (m+n)r=mr+nr, m(r+s)=mr+ms, and (mr)s=m(rs) for all m,n∈M and r,s∈R.

form.wave2.module94.unital-left-module.context: Unital left R-module over a ring with identity
form.wave2.module94.unital-left-module.text: Let R be a ring with identity 1 and let (M,+) be an abelian group. A unital left R-module is an action R×M→M satisfying r(m+n)=rm+rn, (r+s)m=rm+sm, (rs)m=r(sm), and 1m=m for all r,s∈R and m,n∈M.

form.wave2.module94.unital-right-module.context: Unital right R-module over a ring with identity
form.wave2.module94.unital-right-module.text: Let R be a ring with identity 1 and let (M,+) be an abelian group. A unital right R-module is an action M×R→M satisfying (m+n)r=mr+nr, m(r+s)=mr+ms, (mr)s=m(rs), and m1=m for all r,s∈R and m,n∈M.

form.wave2.pop139.congruence-multiple.context: Elementary number theory: congruence of integers modulo a fixed positive integer
form.wave2.pop139.congruence-multiple.text: For m∈ℤ with m>0 and a,b∈ℤ, define a≡b (mod m) if and only if there exists k∈ℤ such that a−b=km. The modulus m is fixed and strictly positive.

form.wave2.pop139.congruence-remainder.context: Elementary number theory: congruence of integers modulo a fixed positive integer
form.wave2.pop139.congruence-remainder.text: Let m be a positive integer. For a,b∈ℤ write a≡b (mod m) precisely when the least nonnegative remainders of a and b upon division by m coincide.

form.wave2.pop139.matrix-trace.context: Finite-dimensional linear algebra: n-by-n square matrices over a field K, n≥1
form.wave2.pop139.matrix-trace.text: Let K be a field, n≥1, and A=(aᵢⱼ)∈Mₙ(K). The trace of A is tr(A)=∑ᵢ₌₁ⁿ aᵢᵢ ∈ K, the finite sum of diagonal entries.

form.wave2.pop140.affine-hull-combinatio.context: Finite-dimensional real affine geometry: subsets of R^d, integer d≥1, with empty hull allowed
form.wave2.pop140.affine-hull-combinatio.text: For an integer d≥1 and a set S⊆ℝ^d, aff(S) is the set of all vectors ∑_{i=1}^{k} αᵢxᵢ with k≥1, xᵢ∈S, αᵢ∈ℝ and ∑_{i=1}^{k} αᵢ=1. In particular aff(∅)=∅.

form.wave2.pop140.affine-hull-intersecti.context: Finite-dimensional real affine geometry: subsets of R^d, integer d≥1, with empty hull allowed
form.wave2.pop140.affine-hull-intersecti.text: Let d≥1 and S⊆ℝ^d. Define aff(S) as the intersection of all affine-closed subsets C⊆ℝ^d containing S, where affine-closed means containing every finite affine combination of its members; the empty set is affine-closed.

form.wave2.pop140.independent-pair.context: Probability theory: two measurable events in a probability space, including probability-zero cases
form.wave2.pop140.independent-pair.text: For measurable A,B in a probability space (Ω,Σ,P), the events A and B are independent if and only if P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B). No positive-probability assumption is required for this product-rule definition.

form.wave2.pop140.mutually-independent.context: Probability theory: joint independence of an arbitrary indexed family of measurable events
form.wave2.pop140.mutually-independent.text: For a probability space (Ω,Σ,P) and indexed measurable events (Aᵢ)_{i∈I}, the family is mutually independent if for every finite J⊆I, P(⋂_{j∈J} Aⱼ)=∏_{j∈J}P(Aⱼ), with the empty intersection Ω and empty product 1.

form.wave2.pop140.pairwise-independent.context: Probability theory: pairwise but not necessarily jointly independent indexed measurable events
form.wave2.pop140.pairwise-independent.text: Let (Aᵢ)_{i∈I} be measurable events on one probability space. The family is pairwise independent if for every i,j∈I with i≠j, P(Aᵢ∩Aⱼ)=P(Aᵢ)P(Aⱼ). This does not in general imply joint independence for three or more events.

form.wave2.pop140.simple-graph-cycle.display_term: cycle in a simple undirected graph
form.wave2.pop140.simple-graph-cycle.context: Graph theory: a finite cycle in a loopless simple undirected graph; length at least three
form.wave2.pop140.simple-graph-cycle.text: For a simple loopless undirected graph G=(V,E), a cycle is a finite cyclic sequence v₀,v₁,…,v_{k−1},v₀ with k≥3, the vertices v₀,…,v_{k−1} pairwise distinct, and {vᵢ,v_{(i+1) mod k}}∈E for every 0≤i<k.

form.wave2.pop141.connected-no-separatio.context: Point-set topology: connectedness of any topological space, including the empty space
form.wave2.pop141.connected-no-separatio.text: A topological space (X,τ) is connected if there do not exist U,V∈τ with U≠∅, V≠∅, U∩V=∅ and U∪V=X.

form.wave2.pop141.connected-clopen.context: Point-set topology: connectedness of any topological space, including the empty space
form.wave2.pop141.connected-clopen.text: A topological space (X,τ) is connected if every subset C⊆X that is both open and closed in X satisfies C=∅ or C=X.

form.wave2.pop141.left-action.context: Abstract algebra: left action of a group G on an arbitrary set X
form.wave2.pop141.left-action.text: Let (G,·) be a group with identity e and let X be a set. A left action is a map α:G×X→X such that α(e,x)=x and α(g,α(h,x))=α(g·h,x) for all g,h∈G and x∈X.

form.wave2.pop141.metric-outer-measure.context: Measure theory on a nonempty metric space (X,d): metric additivity strengthening of a full-power-set outer measure
form.wave2.pop141.metric-outer-measure.text: Let (X,d) be a nonempty metric space and let μ*:𝒫(X)→[0,+∞] be an outer measure. It is a metric outer measure if μ*(A∪B)=μ*(A)+μ*(B) whenever A,B⊆X and inf{d(a,b):a∈A,b∈B}>0, taking inf∅=+∞ when one set is empty.

form.wave2.pop141.outer-measure-full.context: Measure theory: extended nonnegative outer measure on the full power set of an arbitrary set X
form.wave2.pop141.outer-measure-full.text: Let X be a set. A function μ*:𝒫(X)→[0,+∞] is an outer measure on X when μ*(∅)=0, A⊆B implies μ*(A)≤μ*(B), and μ*(⋃_{n=1}^∞ Aₙ)≤∑_{n=1}^∞ μ*(Aₙ) for every sequence (Aₙ) of subsets of X.

form.wave2.pop141.right-action.context: Abstract algebra: right action of a group G on an arbitrary set X
form.wave2.pop141.right-action.text: Let (G,·) be a group with identity e and let X be a set. A right action is a map β:X×G→X such that β(x,e)=x and β(β(x,g),h)=β(x,g·h) for all g,h∈G and x∈X.

form.wave2.pop142.bounded-linear.context: Functional analysis: linear map X→Y between real or complex normed spaces with one global bound
form.wave2.pop142.bounded-linear.text: Let X,Y be normed vector spaces over the same field F∈{ℝ,ℂ} and T:X→Y a linear map. T is bounded if there exists a real M≥0 such that ||Tx||_Y≤M||x||_X for every x∈X.

form.wave2.pop142.operator-norm-ball.display_term: norm of a bounded linear transformation
form.wave2.pop142.operator-norm-ball.context: Functional analysis: operator norm on real/complex bounded linear maps between normed spaces
form.wave2.pop142.operator-norm-ball.text: For a bounded linear T:X→Y between real or complex normed vector spaces, define ||T||=sup{||Tx||_Y : x∈X, ||x||_X≤1}. This is a finite nonnegative real number.

form.wave2.pop142.operator-norm-inf.display_term: norm of a bounded linear transformation
form.wave2.pop142.operator-norm-inf.context: Functional analysis: operator norm on real/complex bounded linear maps between normed spaces
form.wave2.pop142.operator-norm-inf.text: For bounded linear T:X→Y between real or complex normed spaces, equivalently ||T||=inf{M>0 : ||Tx||_Y≤M||x||_X for all x∈X}, with infimum taken in [0,+∞].

form.wave2.pop142.contraction-map.context: Metric spaces: globally Lipschitz mapping with a constant strictly below one
form.wave2.pop142.contraction-map.text: Let (X,d_X) and (Y,d_Y) be nonempty metric spaces and f:X→Y. The map f is a contraction if there exists q∈[0,1) such that d_Y(f(x),f(y))≤q·d_X(x,y) for all x,y∈X.

form.wave2.pop142.proper-vertex-k-color.context: Graph theory: fixed integer k≥1, loopless simple undirected graph; coloring need not use every palette color
form.wave2.pop142.proper-vertex-k-color.text: Let G=(V,E) be a loopless simple undirected graph and let k≥1 be an integer. A proper vertex k-coloring of G is a map c:V→{1,…,k} such that for every edge {u,v}∈E, c(u)≠c(v). Surjectivity is not required.

form.wave2.prereq122.left-coset.context: Left coset gH of a subgroup in a group
form.wave2.prereq122.left-coset.text: For a group G, subgroup H≤G and g∈G, the left coset of H represented by g is gH={gh:h∈H}, a subset of G.

form.wave2.prereq122.real-centered-power.context: Real coefficient power series about specified real center, convergence not assumed
form.wave2.prereq122.real-centered-power.text: Given a real center ξ∈ℝ and coefficients (a_n)_{n≥0}⊆ℝ, the real power series centered at ξ is the formal series expression ∑_{n=0}^∞a_n(x−ξ)^n in the real variable x; convergence at x is not assumed.

form.wave2.prereq122.real-series-converg.context: Real infinite series with finite limit of partial sums
form.wave2.prereq122.real-series-converg.text: For a real sequence (a_n)_{n≥0}, the series ∑_{n=0}^∞a_n converges if there exists s∈ℝ such that the finite partial sums s_N=∑_{n=0}^N a_n tend to s as N→∞; then its sum equals s.

form.wave2.prereq122.right-coset.context: Right coset Hg of a subgroup in a group
form.wave2.prereq122.right-coset.text: For a group G, subgroup H≤G and g∈G, the right coset of H represented by g is Hg={hg:h∈H}, a subset of G.

form.wave2.prereq122.subgroup.context: Subgroup with inherited operation of an ambient group
form.wave2.prereq122.subgroup.text: Let (G,*) be a group and let H⊆G. The subset H is a subgroup of G if H equipped with the restriction of * to H×H is itself a group; the same binary operation is used.

form.wave2.prob90.measurable-space.context: A set equipped with a sigma-algebra, no measure required
form.wave2.prob90.measurable-space.text: A measurable space is a pair (X,Σ), where X is a set and Σ is a σ-algebra of subsets of X.

form.wave2.prob90.probability-space.context: Normalized measure space with total mass one
form.wave2.prob90.probability-space.text: A probability space is a triple (Ω,Σ,P) where (Ω,Σ) is a measurable space and P is a countably additive measure on Σ satisfying P(Ω)=1.

form.wave2.prob90.random-variable-genera.context: Random variable with values in an arbitrary measurable space
form.wave2.prob90.random-variable-genera.text: Given a probability space (Ω,F,P) and a measurable space (S,SigmaS), a random variable with values in S is an (F,SigmaS)-measurable map X:Ω→S.

form.wave2.prob90.random-variable-real.context: Real-valued random variable with Borel-measurable codomain
form.wave2.prob90.random-variable-real.text: A real-valued random variable on (Ω,F,P) is an F/B(R)-measurable map X:Ω→R, where B(R) is the Borel σ-algebra; equivalently the preimage of every interval (−∞,a] belongs to F.

form.wave2.quot119.normal-subgroup.1.context: Normal subgroup of a group; three equivalent group-theoretic criteria
form.wave2.quot119.normal-subgroup.1.text: For a group G and a subgroup N≤G, N is normal in G if gN=Ng for every element g∈G, where gN={gn:n∈N} and Ng={ng:n∈N}.

form.wave2.quot119.normal-subgroup.2.context: Normal subgroup of a group; three equivalent group-theoretic criteria
form.wave2.quot119.normal-subgroup.2.text: For a group G and subgroup N≤G, N is normal precisely when gNg⁻¹=N for every g∈G, with gNg⁻¹={gng⁻¹:n∈N}.

form.wave2.quot119.normal-subgroup.3.context: Normal subgroup of a group; three equivalent group-theoretic criteria
form.wave2.quot119.normal-subgroup.3.text: For a group G and subgroup N≤G, N is normal if gNg⁻¹⊆N for every g∈G; demanding this inclusion for every g, including its inverse, forces equality.

form.wave2.quot119.ordinary-real-ogf.display_term: ordinary generating function of a real sequence
form.wave2.quot119.ordinary-real-ogf.context: Convergent ordinary generating function of a real sequence on its real convergence domain
form.wave2.quot119.ordinary-real-ogf.text: For a real sequence (a_n)_{n≥0}, let D={z∈ℝ:∑_{n=0}^∞a_nz^n converges}. Its ordinary generating function is G_A:D→ℝ, defined by G_A(z)=∑_{n=0}^∞a_nz^n.

form.wave2.quot119.quotient-group.context: Quotient group of G by normal subgroup N with coset product
form.wave2.quot119.quotient-group.text: Let G be a group and N◁G a normal subgroup. The quotient group G/N is the set of left cosets {gN:g∈G}, with well-defined product (aN)(bN)=(ab)N for a,b∈G.

form.wave2.quot119.simple-graph-isomorph.context: Isomorphism between simple undirected graphs preserving and reflecting adjacency
form.wave2.quot119.simple-graph-isomorph.text: Let G=(V_G,E_G) and H=(V_H,E_H) be simple undirected graphs. An isomorphism is a bijection f:V_G→V_H such that for all distinct u,v∈V_G, {u,v}∈E_G if and only if {f(u),f(v)}∈E_H.

form.wave2.rational55.rational-absolute-.display_term: absolute value of a rational number
form.wave2.rational55.rational-absolute-.context: Rational-field modulus based on sign, not the real square-root definition
form.wave2.rational55.rational-absolute-.text: For q in Q with its usual total order, the rational absolute value |q| is q if q≥0 and −q if q<0. This gives a function |·|:Q→Q_{≥0} without presupposing real numbers or square roots.

form.wave2.rational55.rational-number.context: Rational arithmetic: field of integer fractions, constructed without R
form.wave2.rational55.rational-number.text: A rational number is an element of Q, the field of fractions of Z. Concretely, every rational number can be represented as p/q for integers p and nonzero q, with p/q=r/s precisely when ps=rq for nonzero q,s.

form.wave2.rational55.rational-sequence.context: Infinite rational-valued function indexed by positive integers, not a rational limit
form.wave2.rational55.rational-sequence.text: A rational sequence indexed by the positive integers is a function a:N_{>=1}→Q. Its nth term is a_n=a(n). More generally, a sequence of rational numbers may have a specified subset of N as its index set; the infinite Cauchy construction uses all positive-integer indices.

form.wave2.rational55.strictly-positive-.context: Strict rational positivity for epsilon quantifiers; excludes zero
form.wave2.rational55.strictly-positive-.text: A rational number ε is strictly positive if ε>0 in the usual order on Q. The collection of such numbers is Q_{>0}={q in Q:q>0}; zero is excluded.

form.wave2.real45.complete-ordered-real-.context: Axiomatic real arithmetic: totally ordered commutative field complete for nonempty upper-bounded subsets
form.wave2.real45.complete-ordered-real-.text: A real number system is a totally ordered field R such that every nonempty A⊆R bounded above has a least upper bound in R. It is characterized up to ordered-field isomorphism, not by literal equality of underlying sets.

form.wave2.real45.dedekind-supremum.context: Order theory: supremum for all nonempty upper-bounded subsets of a partially ordered set
form.wave2.real45.dedekind-supremum.text: An ordered set (S,≤) has the Dedekind completeness property if every nonempty subset A⊆S that has an upper bound in S possesses a least upper bound sup(A)∈S. The requirement excludes the empty subset and does not demand a supremum for sets lacking upper bounds.

form.wave2.real45.totally-ordered-field.context: Abstract field equipped with a compatible total order; no completeness assumed
form.wave2.real45.totally-ordered-field.text: A totally ordered field is a field F equipped with a total order ≤ such that, for all x,y,z∈F, x<y implies x+z<y+z and, if 0<z, also xz<yz. Dedekind completeness is not required.

form.wave2.real50.cut-model-reals.context: Concrete Dedekind-cut realization: real numbers represented by rational lower cuts
form.wave2.real50.cut-model-reals.text: In the Dedekind-cut construction, the underlying set R_D consists of all lower Dedekind cuts A of Q. Define the order by A≤B if and only if A⊆B. Each rational q has the canonical representation {r∈Q:r<q}. Defining arithmetic on cuts and proving the ordered-field axioms and the least-upper-bound property then gives a concrete realization of a real-number system.

form.wave2.real50.dedekind-rational-lowe.display_term: Dedekind cut of the rational numbers
form.wave2.real50.dedekind-rational-lowe.context: Real construction from Q: nonempty proper lower set without greatest element
form.wave2.real50.dedekind-rational-lowe.text: A (lower) Dedekind cut of the rational numbers is a subset A of Q such that A is nonempty, A is not all of Q, if a belongs to A then every rational q<a also belongs to A, and A has no largest element.

form.wave2.real51.rational-cauchy.context: Cauchy criterion using rational arithmetic before constructing real numbers
form.wave2.real51.rational-cauchy.text: A sequence (a_n) of rational numbers is Cauchy if for every positive rational epsilon there is N such that |a_m−a_n|<epsilon whenever m and n are at least N.

form.wave2.real51.rational-cauchy-equiva.context: Difference tends to rational zero; equivalence precedes the real-number quotient construction
form.wave2.real51.rational-cauchy-equiva.text: Two rational Cauchy sequences (a_n) and (b_n) are equivalent, written (a_n)∼(b_n), if for each positive rational epsilon there is N such that |a_n−b_n|<epsilon for every n≥N.

form.wave2.real52.cauchy-quotient-reals.context: Concrete quotient model of the reals: rational Cauchy sequences modulo zero difference
form.wave2.real52.cauchy-quotient-reals.text: Let C_Q be the set of all rational Cauchy sequences and let a∼b mean that a_n−b_n tends to rational zero. The Cauchy-sequence model of the real numbers has underlying set R_C=C_Q/∼, whose elements are equivalence classes [a_n]. On classes one defines [a_n]+[b_n]=[a_n+b_n] and [a_n]·[b_n]=[a_n b_n], and embeds each rational q as the class of the constant sequence q.

form.wave2.real52.positive-cauchy-class.context: Positive cone of rational-Cauchy quotient field, with an eventual uniform rational margin
form.wave2.real52.positive-cauchy-class.text: A Cauchy-equivalence class [a_n] is called positive when there is a positive rational δ and an index N such that a_n≥δ for all n≥N. This condition is independent of the representative: if b_n−a_n tends to zero, then b_n is eventually bounded below by δ/2.

form.wave2.research81.chromatic-proper-c.context: Finite simple undirected graph with nonempty vertex set: least proper vertex coloring palette size
form.wave2.research81.chromatic-proper-c.text: For a finite simple undirected graph G having at least one vertex, the chromatic number χ(G) is the smallest positive integer k for which there exists c:V(G)→{1,…,k} with c(u)≠c(v) for every edge {u,v}∈E(G).

form.wave2.research81.martingale-continu.context: Real-valued martingale indexed by continuous time t≥0; no assumption of continuous sample paths
form.wave2.research81.martingale-continu.text: A real-valued process (X_t)_{t≥0} adapted to a filtration (F_t)_{t≥0}, with E|X_t|<∞ for every t≥0, is a martingale if E[X_t|F_s]=X_s almost surely whenever 0≤s≤t.

form.wave2.research81.martingale-discret.context: Filtered probability space, integrable adapted real-valued discrete-time process indexed by nonnegative integers
form.wave2.research81.martingale-discret.text: A real-valued discrete-time process (X_n)_{n≥0}, adapted to a filtration (F_n)_{n≥0} and satisfying E|X_n|<∞ for every n, is a martingale if E[X_{n+1}|F_n]=X_n almost surely for each n≥0.

form.wave2.research81.martingale-discret.context: Filtered probability space, integrable adapted real-valued discrete-time process indexed by nonnegative integers
form.wave2.research81.martingale-discret.text: An integrable adapted real-valued discrete-time process (X_n,F_n)_{n≥0} is a martingale if E[X_m|F_n]=X_n almost surely whenever 0≤n≤m are integers.

form.wave2.scalar101.division-ring.context: Associative unital division ring, not necessarily commutative
form.wave2.scalar101.division-ring.text: A division ring D is a nonzero associative unital ring whose nonzero elements form a group under multiplication. Its addition is an abelian group, multiplication distributes over addition on both sides, and every nonzero element has a two-sided multiplicative inverse.

form.wave2.scalar101.division-ring-multi.display_term: multiplicative norm on a division ring
form.wave2.scalar101.division-ring-multi.context: Real-valued multiplicative norm on an associative division ring
form.wave2.scalar101.division-ring-multi.text: Let D be an associative division ring. A multiplicative norm is a map |·|_D:D→ℝ_{≥0} satisfying |a|_D=0 iff a=0, |ab|_D=|a|_D|b|_D for all a,b∈D, and |a+b|_D≤|a|_D+|b|_D for all a,b∈D.

form.wave2.scalar101.left-vector-over-di.display_term: left vector space over a division ring
form.wave2.scalar101.left-vector-over-di.context: Unital left vector space over an associative division ring
form.wave2.scalar101.left-vector-over-di.text: For an associative division ring D, a left D-vector space is an abelian group (V,+) with scalar action D×V→V, (a,v)↦av, satisfying a(v+w)=av+aw, (a+b)v=av+bv, (ab)v=a(bv), and 1_Dv=v.

form.wave2.scalar101.normed-division-rin.context: Associative division ring equipped with a specified multiplicative real-valued norm
form.wave2.scalar101.normed-division-rin.text: A normed division ring is a pair (D,|·|_D), where D is an associative unital division ring and |·|_D:D→ℝ_{≥0} is a specified multiplicative norm satisfying positive definiteness and the triangle inequality.

form.wave2.scalar101.right-vector-over-d.display_term: right vector space over a division ring
form.wave2.scalar101.right-vector-over-d.context: Unital right vector space over an associative division ring
form.wave2.scalar101.right-vector-over-d.text: For an associative division ring D, a right D-vector space is an abelian group (V,+) with scalar action V×D→V, (v,a)↦va, satisfying (v+w)a=va+wa, v(a+b)=va+vb, (va)b=v(ab), and v1_D=v.

form.wave2.set63.natural-including-zero.text: With the zero-inclusive convention, N is the collection of natural numbers 0,1,2,3,…; its positive subset N_{>0} consists of those elements different from 0.

form.wave2.set63.natural-positive-conven.text: Under the positive-counting convention, the natural numbers are 1,2,3,…, denoted N_{>0} when N is defined to include 0.

form.wave2.set63.relation-reflexive-symm.context: Binary equivalence relation on a set
form.wave2.set63.relation-reflexive-symm.text: An equivalence relation ∼ on S is a subset of S×S such that x∼x for every x∈S; x∼y implies y∼x; and x∼y and y∼z together imply x∼z for all x,y,z∈S.

form.wave2.set63.set-of-equivalence-clas.context: Quotient set of an equivalence relation
form.wave2.set63.set-of-equivalence-clas.text: Given an equivalence relation ∼ on a set S, its quotient set is S/∼={[x]:x∈S}, the collection of all ∼-equivalence classes.

form.wave2.set63.set-of-related-elements.text: If ∼ is an equivalence relation on S and x∈S, the equivalence class [x] is the set {y∈S:y∼x}. Its elements are representatives of the same class.

form.wave2.variant71.connected.01.context: General topology: connected by no nontrivial open separation, empty space included
form.wave2.variant71.connected.01.text: A topological space X is connected if it cannot be written as the union of two disjoint nonempty open subsets.

form.wave2.variant71.connected.02.context: General topology: connected by no nontrivial open separation, empty space included
form.wave2.variant71.connected.02.text: A topological space X is connected precisely when its only subsets that are both open and closed are ∅ and X.

form.wave2.variant71.connected.03.context: General topology: connected by no nontrivial open separation, empty space included
form.wave2.variant71.connected.03.text: A topological space X is connected precisely when there is no continuous surjection from X onto the discrete two-element space.
